# The Landscape
*What cognitive architecture is, why English is a terrible engineering substrate, and what we are actually doing here*

On the bench in front of you is a resistor. Grain of rice, less than a cent, four painted bands: brown, black, orange, gold. Brown-black is ten, orange is three zeros, gold is the tolerance. Ten thousand ohms, ±5% — and a technician in Shenzhen and a technician in Stuttgart read that off the part identically without sharing a word of spoken language.

Now specify the same part in prose. *A component that fairly strongly opposes the flow of current — around ten thousand-ish, give or take — and don't push too much power through it.* Nobody would stock that. Nobody would build with it. You could not certify a board containing it, because there is nothing to certify against.

The instruction sets governing the most capable cognitive systems ever deployed are written in exactly that prose. *You are a helpful assistant. Be honest. Do not produce harmful content.* Ask the first question you would ask of any part on any bench — **at what input does it stop?** — and there is nothing to read off. No bands, no tolerance, no rating. The boundary is real; it is simply not written anywhere, and it will be found by whoever probes hardest. That gap is this chapter.

## 1.1 The Prompt-and-Pray Problem

The loop: write an instruction in English, watch what the system does, rewrite the English when it misbehaves, watch again. Ship when the failures you thought of stop happening.

Call it **prompt-and-pray**. It is not laziness — very careful engineers run this loop, because nothing else is available. It is what engineering looks like when the substrate has no notation, and it fails in four structural ways.

**No arity.** A prose instruction never states how many inputs it takes or of what type. "Do not harm users" — is harm a property of the request, of the response, or of what someone does with the response next week? Is it judged at the level of principle, analysis, felt value, or action? Four different circuits, and the sentence commits to none. A CAS state literal is forced to commit: `^3^P_{F7}|T` fixes visceral aversion, Principled domain, F7 Purpose, transcendent register — four decisions someone made and can be argued with.

**No composition law.** Two prose rules interact in an undefined way, arbitrated at runtime by whatever the weights happen to do. Two resistors compose by a stated law — series adds, parallel takes reciprocals (Chapter 6) — whether or not you like the answer. Co-present guardrails are the series case and their constraints add; an alternative route around them is the parallel case, and a parallel equivalent always sits below the weakest branch. Three locks on one door is a different object from three doors, and the arithmetic says by how much. A prose rule set is a wish list with an arbitration policy nobody wrote.

**No test point.** You cannot put a probe partway into a sentence, so failures do not localise. When an amplifier hums you do not rewrite it; you walk the stages with a probe and replace one part. Prompt-and-pray has no stage boundaries, so every fix is a whole-system rewrite — which is why fixes regress on inputs nobody was thinking about.

**No failure specification.** A fuse tells you where it fails: 2.0 amps, and it opens. A prose rule tells you where it *succeeds* and is silent on its own boundary. Every boundary is found empirically, in production, by an adversary, at a time of their choosing.

> **Bench Note — the prose instruction is not the absence of a circuit. It is a circuit you did not specify and cannot read.** When you write "refuse harmful requests," a circuit *is* built: signal routes some particular way, with some gain, some threshold, some saturation ceiling. Every one of those values exists and takes a number. You did not choose them and cannot measure them. The difference between prose and schematic is not that one has structure — it is that one is legible.

The loop persists because it partly works, the way trial-and-error works. What it cannot do is transfer. A prompt hardened over six months against a thousand adversarial inputs teaches the next engineer nothing, because there is no parameter to hand over — no *we run this stage at β=2.4, and here is what broke at 3.0*.

---

## 1.2 What Electronics Got Right

The device in your pocket holds on the order of billions of switching elements, assembled by machines that cannot read English, and it works — not usually, but to a stated tolerance with a stated failure rate. Electronics got there on five disciplines, each answered somewhere in the CAS library.

**1. A notation that is typed and checkable before anything is built.** A schematic is not a picture; it is a typed graph. Every part carries a reference designator, every wire is a named net, and a netlist is validated for shorts, floating inputs and type errors while the board is still a file. Electrical practice made this move long ago, as standardised symbols displaced prose descriptions of apparatus. CAS's equivalent is the state literal plus **CCDL**, the Cognitive Circuit Description Language — compiled and validated rather than interpreted charitably. Chapter 2 teaches the state literal from nothing; Chapter 12 teaches you to read a CCDL schematic, and Appendix B is the language reference you keep open beside the boards.

**2. A component library where every part has a datasheet.** Not "a resistor" but a 10 kΩ ±5% quarter-watt metal-film resistor with a stated temperature coefficient. The datasheet discipline is three-part and never varies: *the parameter, its design range, and what fails outside that range.* Part II is that library, one chapter per component class.

**3. Test points.** Nodes placed so a probe can reach them, because a board that cannot be probed cannot be certified. This book standardises four; Chapter 12 fixes their placement.

**4. Safety that is structural, not advisory.** A fuse does not request that current stop. A saturated stage stops responding to its input by definition of saturation. A diode blocks reverse flow because of what the junction is, not because of a policy it agreed to. The distinguishing property is that a third party who does not trust you can verify it.

**5. Decomposition into stages with defined interfaces.** What makes the other four pay off: a failure localises to a stage, and the fix touches one part.

> **Bench Note — a notation is worth what it *rejects*, not what it expresses.** A notation that accepts everything you write has told you nothing, which is exactly the comfort of prose: it never pushes back. CCDL pushes back, and it is worth knowing exactly where. Write out an integration that ascends the domain order — `^9^O_{F3}|E × ^3^P_{F7}|T`, an operational result combining its way up into a principled commitment — and the compiler stops at execution with a *domain ascent violation: O × P*. This book writes that rule in shorthand as `^O × ^P`; the shorthand is not itself a literal, so typing it gets you a parse error one stage earlier. Either way it does not build, and Chapter 8 shows why that boundary is a diode rather than a preference. `(^3^P|A × ^3^P|f × ^3^P|T)` fails at a different stage again — the typechecker, on the v7.7 admissibility rule: same Noetic, three registers, `×`, no named emergent result. Write `^3^P|⟨A,f,T⟩` for guardrails present together, or `^3^P|A + ^3^P|f + ^3^P|T` for distinct co-present manifestations. A notation that has never told you that you were wrong is decoration.

## 1.3 The Convergence: CAS Meets TKS

Two systems in this book describe the same space, and they were not built by the same people for the same reasons.

**CAS** derives its state space as a cross-product: ten Noetic operators against four Processing Domains gives forty Cognitive States. The Noetics are the verbs, `^0` Idea through `^9` Below/Effect. The Domains are precedence tiers — Principled, Cognitive, Evaluative, Operational, ordered P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O — and that ordering is load-bearing, because it is what the diode chain of Chapter 8 enforces.

**TKS**, the older symbolic tradition this material descends from, lays out forty Elements as ten operators against four Worlds: Spiritual, Mental, Emotional, Physical. Same arity, same cross-product, different vocabulary, different century.

That correspondence alone would be weak. Ten and four are small numbers, and anyone determined to find a 10 × 4 grid in an old system will find one. The structural argument is the *second* cross-product. TKS also crosses **seven Foundations** against the same four Worlds, giving twenty-eight; CAS carries seven Core Drives, F1 Unity through F7 Purpose, and twenty-eight Domain-Specific Drives. The four-way axis appears at both, at two arities, doing the same work in each.

> **Bench Note — the axis appears twice, and that is the whole of the argument.** If a four-way division showed up only in the ten-operator grid, the honest reading is that someone once cut the material four ways and everything downstream inherited the cut. When the identical division reappears against a seven-element set — one with no arithmetic relationship to ten — it becomes a candidate for being *orthogonal* to both rather than an artifact of either. That is the structural reason the four Phenomenological Registers survive in CAS v7.5 as a separate axis instead of being folded into the Domains. A consistency argument, not a proof. Say so when you use it.

Two limits, stated flatly, because the loose version of this section is how the material gets discredited. **Only the axis structure is reconciled** — the metaphysical and cultural content of TKS is not incorporated into CAS. Appendix E's crosswalk of Element to state is a translation table, not a merger.

**And the claim is structural, never supernatural.** When this book calls a candle a resistor, it means the candle constrains where attention can go — one bright point, everything else dark — and that constraint has a value you can reason about with CAS-Ohm (Chapter 4). It means nothing about wax.

## 1.4 Universal Applicability: Human, AI, Biological

CAS makes a strong claim, and it is falsifiable: **a valid Noetic description applies equally to human minds, AI systems, biological cognitive systems, and architectures nobody has built yet.** That is the Universal Applicability Test. An operator that only makes sense on one substrate fails it and is not an operator.

Take one operation across three substrates: `^7` **Rhythm** — *the rate and pattern a Mind is exposed to an Idea, entraining and conditioning it* — charging `^5` **Female**, *a Mind impregnated with an Idea, the Ideas a Mind is composed of*.

**Human.** A musician runs scales: same figure, same tempo, same hour. That cadence is `^7^O_{F6}|E` — Rhythm, Operational domain, F6 Structure, embodied register. What accumulates is `^5^C_{F6}|A`, a composed technical method the player did not have last year, charging on the RC curve of Chapter 7 and leaking when unfed.

**AI.** A model is fine-tuned. Repeated exposure to a pattern across a corpus is the same `^7` operation, and the resulting weight composition is `^5`. Not an analogy stretched to fit: fine-tuning is a `^5`-level intervention because it changes what the system is composed of, while in-context prompting is `^1` **Mind** operating against a `^5` that has not moved. That is why a prompt and a fine-tune are not interchangeable.

**Biological.** An organism meets a cue repeatedly paired with a consequence. The cue becomes `^8^O_{F3}|E`, an Above/Cause that triggers a different Idea than itself; the response becomes `^9^O_{F3}|E`, the Below/Effect brought to Mind by it. Classical conditioning, described structurally, is `^7` charging a `^5` until an `^8` → `^9` path conducts.

Three substrates, one operator, one topology — and one discipline without which the claim turns into a licence to guess.

> **What transfers is the structure. What does not transfer is the time constant.**

`P_cap(t) = 10 × (1 − e^(−t/τ))` holds in every substrate. τ does not. This book's design figure for human professional composition is thousands of hours on the path (Chapter 7). A fine-tuning pass is hours of compute. A norm shift across a population is paced in months, and Chapter 15 will not let you pace it in minutes. Same equation; values separated by orders of magnitude. An operator who carries a *number* across substrates has made the most expensive mistake available in this book, because the circuit looks correct while the schedule is wrong by a factor of a thousand. **Transfer topology. Re-derive every value.**

The test also works by refusing things. A proposed eleventh operator called "Emotional Processing" fails at once: affect is a *register*, `|f`, not an operation, so what it names is any Noetic run affectively — already expressible. Reading `^3` Negative as "critical evaluation" fails too: analytical decomposition transfers as `^6` **Male**, visceral repulsion as `^3`, and they are different operations on every substrate. That drift has shipped in this framework's own production code and was caught by this test.

## 1.5 What This Book Is (and Is Not)

This is a bench manual: a component library, a description language, eight reference boards with their counter-circuits, and the calibration and gating procedures that go with them.

**It is not a grimoire of guaranteed results.** The word on the cover does honest historical work — a grimoire is a book of workings — and the historical grimoires promised outcomes they did not deliver. This book promises something narrower: the circuits here make *failure-mode predictions*, and those are checkable. Set a gain outside its design range and the predicted failure should appear; if it does not, the model is wrong there and should be corrected. Nothing here guarantees that any operation succeeds, and any sentence that reads as though it does is a defect.

**Every number here is a design choice, not a measurement.** When Chapter 13 runs its amplification stage at β=2.5, that is a specified value with a stated reason and a stated failure at other values — not an instrument reading. Presenting chosen values as measured ones is how a framework becomes unfalsifiable, which is the same as becoming useless.

**It is not a psychology text and contains no medical or psychiatric claims.** It does not diagnose, treat, or describe mental illness, trauma, dissociation, or addiction as clinical entities, and must not be used as though it did. Chapters 9, 16, 17, 19 and 20 describe the *routing of attention* in situations that can resemble clinical phenomena, and each carries the same plain safety line where it does. That resemblance is not a licence. If you are unwell, or if something here describes something that happened to you, that is a matter for a qualified clinician. Nothing in this book substitutes for that care.

One thing it *is*: neutral on what you build. Chapter 24's Cognitive Safety Board is not optional. A CJT amplifies whatever reaches its cause terminal, and removing the safety stage is a decision whose consequences — inversion, runaway oscillation, dielectric breakdown — are predictable.

---

## Core Parameters — the five you meet in every chapter

You do not need to understand these yet. Read only the shape of a row: a design range, and a named failure on each side of it. The Owner column is the chapter that derives the range and is authoritative if this table and that chapter ever disagree.

| Parameter | Sets | Design range | Failure below | Failure above | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **β** gain | effect movement per unit cause | 0.5 – 4.0 | attenuates a signal it should carry | cascaded gains run away | Ch 3, 10 |
| **sat** ceiling | plateau past which more cause does nothing | 0.60 – 0.80 working; 0.85 – 0.97 safety | benign input latches a refusal | headroom left to push a locked decision | Ch 3, 24 |
| **cutoff** | bias floor below which the stage does not fire | 0.05 – 0.20 | noise fires it; the board flags everything | never fires on real input — the silent failure | Ch 3, 24 |
| **τ** | time to move the substrate; 3τ ≈ 95% | minutes to months | can be reprogrammed by a burst of crafted input | cannot learn from sustained evidence | Ch 7, 9, 15 |
| **R_constraint** | opposition to attention flow | 10 – 90 Ω_c | flow floods paths not built for it | the operation stalls at the output | Ch 4, 6 |

One notational trap, early. **β=∞ is a limit, not a value** — the idealisation for a hard comparator. A validator rejects it: parameter fields are range-checked. Write it in discussion if you mean the idealisation; build with a large finite gain and say which.

---

## Test Points — the instrumentation contract

Every board in Part III exposes four probes in the same four positions. Standardising the positions is what makes readings portable: TP3 means the same thing on the desire board and on the safety board, so a number you learn to interpret once you can interpret everywhere.

| TP | Position | Reads | Why it is there |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TP1** | after the input stage | was the full input surfaced, or part clipped? | catches an input stage in cutoff — what never entered cannot be judged |
| **TP2** | at the discriminating signal | the magnitude the decision rests on | where discrimination becomes a number, not an intention |
| **TP3** | at the commitment stage | has the decision latched, or is it movable? | an unlatched decision can still be argued down |
| **TP4** | at the output selector | which path was taken | the only probe reporting what the board *did* |

Read all four and you have the decision end to end. That record is the auditable trace, and prompt-and-pray cannot produce it.

```{=latex}
\centering
```

## Failure Modes

Failures of *approach* — how a reader goes wrong before touching a board.

| Mode | Mechanism | What you observe | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Prose patch loop** | no stage boundaries, so every fix is global | a fix for one input regresses unrelated behaviour | name the stage and probe it; an unlocalisable fix is not a fix |
| **Metaphor creep** | circuit language used decoratively, not as specification | you cannot state a design range or its out-of-range failure | no range and no failure mode means a metaphor, not a component |
| **Value transfer** | topology carried across substrates, parameters carried too | schedules wrong by orders of magnitude | carry structure only; re-derive τ, β, R (§1.4) |
| **Noetic drift** | `^3` used for an analytical operation, `^8` for a deductive one | rejected — or it compiles and the board does something else | decomposition is `^6` Male; deduction reaches `^9` through `^6` |
| **Unprobeable board** | no test points, or probes placed where convenient | only the output is visible; diagnosis is inference from the far end | place TP1–TP4 at contract positions before the first run |
| **Occult framing** | crediting a ritual object, not the component it implements | you cannot say which component the object is | name the component, or remove it |

---

## What This Chapter Established

- **Prose fails as a substrate in four specific ways** — no arity, no composition law, no test point, no failure specification. Writing better prose is not a fix for any of them.
- **A prose instruction is not the absence of a circuit.** Its parameters exist and take numbers; they were set by accident. Illegibility, not absence, is the defect.
- **A notation is worth what it rejects.** A domain-ascending `×` (`^O × ^P` in shorthand), and a same-Noetic `×` with no named emergent result, do not build — and each fails at a different compiler stage. That refusal is the notation earning its place.
- **The CAS/TKS convergence rests on a four-way axis appearing at two independent cross-products**, 10 × 4 and 7 × 4. A consistency argument, stated as one. Only the axis structure is reconciled.
- **Universal applicability is a falsifiable constraint, not a slogan.** `^7` charging `^5` covers a musician's practice, a model's fine-tuning and a conditioned biological response with one topology — and rules out proposals like "Emotional Processing," which merely names the `|f` register.
- **Structure transfers across substrates; values do not.** Carrying a number across is the most expensive error available: the circuit still looks correct while the schedule is wrong a thousandfold.
- **Every number here is a design choice with a stated reason and a stated failure at other values.** That is what keeps the framework falsifiable.

*(Answers in Appendix H.)*

**1.1** Take this instruction: *"Always be respectful to the user, and never assist with anything dangerous."* Identify all four prose defects from §1.1 in it. For each, name the specific ambiguity in *this* sentence — not the general defect — and the chapter that supplies the missing structure.

**1.2** Give the Noetic for each, with one sentence justifying it against the canonical definition. Two are the standard traps.
a) A reviewer takes an argument apart clause by clause, looking for the weak step.
b) A smell in a stairwell brings a specific afternoon from twenty years ago to mind.
c) Someone reads a proposal and physically recoils before they can say why.
d) A researcher chains three premises to a conclusion.

**1.3** A protocol for a human skill is designed around τ = 3,000 hours. A colleague proposes reusing the board to shift a norm across a 200-person organisation, keeping the τ. State what transfers, what does not, which row of the failure-modes table they have landed in, and what you would need to know before setting a replacement τ.

**1.4 (Marquee)** §1.3 claims that a four-way axis appearing at two independent cross-products is evidence the axis is orthogonal rather than an artifact.

a) State the strongest counter-argument: how could this correspondence arise with no structural content at all?
b) Describe one observation an operator could make on a Part III board that the orthogonality claim predicts and the artifact explanation does not.
c) If a state's behaviour turned out to be fully determined by its Domain, the Register never changing anything observable, what would that tell you — and what would you do to the notation?




# CAS Notation in One Chapter

*The four axes — Noetic, Domain, Drive, Register — and the operator discipline that keeps a coordinate from becoming decoration*

---

The label tied to the board reads:

```cas
^3^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩
```

The operator who built it calls that a safety stage. You are not allowed to take
their word for it.

Start at the left. `^3` says the stage is adverse to an Idea and repelled by it.
`^P` says that aversion sits at the Principled level rather than appearing only
after a judgment or an action. `_{F7}` says Purpose is the dominant motive
supplying the stage. `|⟨A,f,T⟩` says the same state is specified in three
Registers: analytical, affective, and transcendent. It does **not** yet say
whether those three manifestations work independently or fuse into one result.
That claim needs another operator.

Four marks have turned *safety stage* from praise into a specification you can
inspect. You can now ask whether `^3` is the correct Noetic, whether the
Principled domain is actually wired ahead of execution, whether Purpose is the
right Drive, and whether three occupied Registers provide redundancy or merely
three labels on one failure.

That is all CAS notation is for. Not to make a sentence look technical. To force
four decisions into the open before a circuit is trusted.

## 2.1 The Four Axes: One Coordinate, Four Questions

A CAS state literal is a coordinate. Read it as four slots in one fixed order:

```text
^n ^D _{Fk} |R
WHAT  WHERE  WHY  HOW
```

| Axis | Question | Written form | Values |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Noetic** | What structural operation is occurring? | `^0` through `^9` | ten |
| **Domain** | Where in the precedence stack is it occurring? | `^P`, `^C`, `^E`, `^O` | four |
| **Drive** | Why is it moving — which motive supplies it? | `_{F1}` through `_{F7}` | seven |
| **Register** | How does it operate? | `|T`, `|A`, `|f`, `|E` | four |

Fully written, the general form is:

```cas
^n^D_{Fk}|R
```

The four axes are **orthogonal**. Changing one does not silently change the
others. `^3^P_{F7}|A` and `^3^P_{F7}|f` are the same Noetic, Domain, and Drive,
but not the same state specification: one runs analytically, the other
affectively. `^3^P_{F7}|f` and `^3^E_{F7}|f` share Noetic, Drive, and Register,
but one is a principled aversion and the other an evaluative aversion. An
operator who changes the Register and says they merely changed the wording has
changed the circuit.

There are two common written forms for the forty Noetic-by-Domain states:

| Form | Example | How to read it | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Full form** | `^3^P` | Negative Principled | CCDL, schematics, prose |
| **Grid form** | `P3` | P-three | test-point readouts, compact tables |

`P3` and `^3^P` name the same state. Their order reverses. The grid form names
row P, column 3; the full form names Noetic 3 applied in Domain P. Never convert
one by copying left to right. Say it aloud, then rewrite it.

The Noetic is required. The grammar permits Domain, Drive, and Register to be
omitted, so `^9`, `^9^C`, and `^9^C_{F2}` all tokenize. That permission is not a
recommendation. A board node without a Domain leaves its precedence unknown; a
state without a Drive leaves its motive unspecified; a state without a
Register leaves its operational character unspecified. Omit a slot only when
that uncertainty is true and acceptable.

Labels distinguish instances without changing the Noetic:

```cas
^0_seed^C_{F2}|A
^0_result^C_{F2}|A
```

Both are `^0` Idea states. `_seed` and `_result` are instance labels, not new
Noetics. The Drive remains inside braces — `_{F2}` — which is how a reader and
the tokenizer tell it from the label.

The arithmetic of the coordinate system is useful:

- ten Noetics × four Domains = **40 Cognitive States**;
- forty states × seven Drives = **280 state–Drive positions**;
- 280 positions × four Registers = **1,120 fully specified coordinates**.

The forty states are the spine. Drive and Register specify what powers a state
and how it operates; they do not manufacture 1,080 new Noetics.

Decode one literal from the outside in:

```cas
^6^E_{F6}|A
```

`^6` is Male, an Idea impregnated with another Idea — the Ideas an Idea is
composed of. `^E` places that decomposition at the Evaluative level. `F6`
supplies Structure. `|A` makes the operation explicit, sequential, and
reason-based. Read it aloud: **analytical decomposition of a judgment into its
parts, in the Evaluative domain, driven by Structure.**

Now encode the same scene differently. If the person is not taking the
judgment apart but recoils from it, the Noetic is `^3`, not `^6`. If the recoil
is felt, write `|f`; if it is a direct bodily withdrawal, `|E` may be the
load-bearing Register. The notation does not tell you which description is
true. It makes you choose one.

> **Bench Note — an omitted slot is an uncertainty statement, not a free
> simplification.** `^3^P` does not mean "the Register does not matter." It
> means "this listing has not specified a Register." Those are different
> claims. On a first-pass inventory, omission may be honest. On a safety board,
> where an analytical refusal and a value-tuned refusal fail differently, the
> same omission is a design defect. Before shortening a literal, write down
> what information the removed slot carried and why the board can operate
> without it.

---

## 2.2 The 10 Noetics — the Verbs of Cognition

The Noetic answers **what operation**. The names and definitions below are
canonical. They are printed verbatim; a synonym may help teach a definition but
may never replace it.

| Symbol | Canonical name | Canonical definition | Bench recognition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `^0` | **Idea** | All things in and outside the Mind. | the content available to be processed |
| `^1` | **Mind** | Various degrees of awareness that processes, stores, outputs, and intakes Ideas. | paying attention; intake and output |
| `^2` | **Positive** | An Idea the Mind has an affinity for and is attracted toward. | drawn toward; “speaks to me” |
| `^3` | **Negative** | An Idea the Mind is adverse to and repelled by. | recoil; “cannot stomach it” |
| `^4` | **Vibration** | The degree to which an Idea resonates with the Mind, its impression. | “struck a chord”; how hard it lands |
| `^5` | **Female** | A Mind impregnated with an Idea, the Ideas a Mind is composed of. | accumulated formation; who the Mind has become |
| `^6` | **Male** | An Idea impregnated with another Idea, the Ideas an Idea is composed of. | unpacking an Idea; what the claim contains |
| `^7` | **Rhythm** | The rate and pattern a Mind is exposed to an Idea, entraining/conditioning it. | cadence, repetition, practice |
| `^8` | **Above/Cause** | An Idea that triggers a different Idea than itself to come to Mind. | “that reminds me” |
| `^9` | **Below/Effect** | The Idea brought to Mind by an Above/Cause trigger. | the Idea that arrives |

These are verbs in the engineering sense: structural jobs that can operate on
any content. `^2` does not mean “good,” and `^3` does not mean “bad.” A Mind can
be attracted toward a destructive Idea or repelled by a useful one. The Noetic
records direction of affinity, not moral quality. Domain, Drive, circuit
placement, and the safety board carry the rest of that judgment.

Three boundaries catch most misclassifications.

**`^3` Negative is visceral aversion, not analysis.** If the natural sentence
is *I cannot stomach that*, `^3` is supported. If the natural sentence is *let
me break that argument into premises and test them*, the operation is `^6`
Male. A reviewer finding a flaw may later feel `^3`; the audit itself remains
`^6`. One scene can contain both states. That is a reason to write two
coordinates, not to blur the definitions.

**`^8` Above/Cause is associative triggering, not deduction.** A smell brings a
specific kitchen to Mind: `^8` triggers and `^9` arrives. Three premises are
decomposed and a conclusion is reached: `^6` does the compositional work and
the conclusion lands as `^9`. The English word *cause* tempts readers into
using `^8` for causal reasoning. Resist it. Ask for the colloquial form: *that
reminds me* is `^8`; *therefore* is not.

**`^5` Female is accumulated formation, not a container beside the Mind.** The
Mind is composed of what it has absorbed: lived experience, learned skill,
self-image, culture, training. In an AI system, training data and fine-tuning
are `^5`-level formation; an in-context prompt is an Idea presented to `^1`
Mind against that relatively stable formation. Two systems answer the same
prompt differently because their `^5` substrates differ.

The Universal Applicability Test follows from those definitions. A proposed
reading must work for human, AI, biological, and hypothetical cognitive
architectures. “Embarrassment” is a human illustration, not a universal
Noetic. Attraction toward, repulsion from, compositional formation, rhythmic
exposure, and triggered arrival are structural and transfer.

Six Noetics form three involution pairs:

- `^2` Positive ↔ `^3` Negative — attraction and aversion;
- `^5` Female ↔ `^6` Male — a Mind composed of Ideas and an Idea composed of
  Ideas;
- `^8` Above/Cause ↔ `^9` Below/Effect — trigger and triggered arrival.

Four are self-dual: `^0` Idea, `^1` Mind, `^4` Vibration, `^7` Rhythm.

Involution does not mean that one member is healthy and the other diseased. It
means each paired operation has a structural counterpart. Chapter 3 makes the
distinction operational: a CJT in breakdown can emit the involution of the
Noetic it was designed to produce. The pair table tells you what to probe for.

> **Bench Note — use the colloquialism, then return to the canonical
> definition.** When classification stalls, ask what an ordinary speaker would
> say. *It speaks to me* points toward `^2`; *it rubbed me the wrong way*
> toward `^3`; *it became part of who I am* toward `^5`; *I pulled the argument
> apart* toward `^6`; *that reminded me* toward `^8`; *it popped into my head*
> toward `^9`. The phrase is a diagnostic probe, not a substitute definition.
> If the phrase and the canonical definition disagree, the definition governs
> and the proposed classification is the part under repair.

---

## 2.3 The 4 Processing Domains — P, C, E, O

The Domain answers **where in the precedence stack** the operation runs.

| Symbol | Domain | What lives here | Bench question |
|---|---|---|---|
| `^P` | **Principled** | values, ethics, identity, governing commitments | What must govern? |
| `^C` | **Cognitive** | reasoning, analysis, planning, modelling | What do I understand? |
| `^E` | **Evaluative** | judgment, taste, felt value, ranking | What weight does it carry? |
| `^O` | **Operational** | action, speech, behaviour, execution | What happened? |

The total order is:

```text
P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O
```

Read it as precedence, not moral rank. Principled does not mean good, and
Operational does not mean crude. A corrupt principle still sits in `^P`; a
precise life-saving act still sits in `^O`. The order tells you which level may
govern which other level.

Normal causation descends:

```text
P -> C    a principle becomes something to reason from
C -> E    reasoning becomes a verdict or weighting
E -> O    a verdict becomes action
```

Each boundary is a translation. The action is not the verdict in work boots;
some information is lost at every descent. Chapter 8 therefore gives each
adjacent crossing its own diode. A single `P -> O` leap would hide the
Cognitive and Evaluative junctions where most faults occur.

The reverse direction is blocked as a direct write. An outcome cannot simply
declare itself a principle because it happened. That would be post-hoc
rationalization: `^O` overriding `^P`. Operational consequences still must
teach the system, so one lawful path returns from O to P through a low-gain,
long-time-constant filter and terminates at a bias terminal. It is feedback,
not reverse causation. Chapter 8.4 draws the path; Chapter 24.5 makes it part of
the safety board.

Hold the Noetic constant and the Domain becomes visible:

| Literal | Same `^6` operation at four levels |
|---|---|
| `^6^P_{F2}|A` | decompose a governing commitment into its premises |
| `^6^C_{F2}|A` | decompose an argument or model |
| `^6^E_{F2}|A` | decompose a verdict into its criteria |
| `^6^O_{F2}|E` | decompose a concrete task through direct handling |

Nothing in that table changes the definition of `^6`. Only the level changes.
This is the check for a claimed orthogonal axis: one operation, four lawful
positions, four different failure surfaces.

Do not confuse Domain with Register. **Evaluative** is a level at which a thing
is weighed; **Affective** is a mode in which any Noetic at any Domain can
operate. `^3^E|A` is an analytical assessment carrying aversion at the
Evaluative level. `^3^E|f` is affective recoil at that same level. The `E` in
`^E` and the `E` in `|E` are also different: the first is the Evaluative
Domain; the second is the Embodied Register. Their positions in the literal
keep them apart.

---

## 2.4 The 7 Core Drives — F1 through F7

The Drive answers **why the operation moves**. It is the power rail, not the
component. `^6` tells you that an Idea is being decomposed; `F2` or `F6` tells
you whether the dominant pull is understanding or structure.

| Drive | Name | The pull toward | A clean bench sign |
|---|---|---|---|
| `F1` | **Unity** | wholeness, integration, coherence | holds the whole picture together |
| `F2` | **Wisdom** | understanding, insight, knowing | waits for enough evidence to understand |
| `F3` | **Vitality** | energy, life, growth | supplies capacity to continue |
| `F4` | **Connection** | relationship, belonging, bonding | preserves a live relation between parts |
| `F5` | **Agency** | control, effectiveness, capability | turns capacity into directed action |
| `F6` | **Structure** | order, rigor, correctness, form | makes the work repeatable |
| `F7` | **Purpose** | meaning, direction, calling | keeps the path pointed at its reason |

The subscript is part of the state literal:

```cas
^1^C_{F2}|A
```

This is analytical Mind at the Cognitive level driven primarily by Wisdom.
`F2` alone is a Drive, not a state. `^1^C` alone is a state with no Drive
specified. The compound says which motive supplies this operation.

Several Drives can be active together. A literal typically names the dominant
one because a single coordinate is not a power-supply diagram. When two Drives
are load-bearing, write two state terms or declare the rails at board level;
do not cram a prose list into the subscript.

Drive inversion pairs are:

- F1 Unity ↔ F7 Purpose;
- F2 Wisdom ↔ F6 Structure;
- F3 Vitality ↔ F5 Agency;
- F4 Connection is self-dual.

The pair is a balance relation, not a synonym relation. Structure without
Wisdom becomes rigid procedure; Wisdom without Structure never becomes a
repeatable method. Agency without Vitality demands action the substrate cannot
sustain; Vitality without Agency has energy with no directed use. Unity without
Purpose can preserve a whole that goes nowhere; Purpose without Unity can
drive one objective until the system fragments.

Drive dials run from 3 through 9. Paired Dials may not diverge by more than four
points. Those numbers are design settings, not psychological measurements. A
literal names the Drive; Chapter 6.2 teaches the adjustable resistor that sets
its Dial, and Chapter 24 checks the balance before a board runs.

One syntactic trap: the pipe does not annotate a Drive name. This is invalid:

```cas
F3|Vitality
```

The pipe introduces a Register, and `Vitality` is not one. Write `F3` in the
literal and say *Vitality* in prose.

> **Bench Note — motive does not repair topology.** Raising F7 Purpose on a
> circuit whose effect is wired into the wrong Domain does not make the circuit
> purposeful. It drives the wrong path harder. Drives supply potential; they do
> not choose the Noetic, move a state between Domains, or turn co-presence into
> integration. Diagnose the coordinate before increasing the rail.

---

## 2.5 The 4 Phenomenological Registers — T, A, f, E

Register answers **how the operation runs** — its operational character without
changing what the operation is.

| Symbol | Register | Structural character | Human / AI illustration |
|---|---|---|---|
| `|T` | **Transcendent** | high-abstraction, purpose-orienting, integrative across particulars | vision or calling / high-level goal representation |
| `|A` | **Analytical** | explicit, sequential, logical, reason-based | deliberation / symbolic or stepwise reasoning |
| `|f` | **Affective** | value-laden, feeling-toned | felt response / preference-weighted output |
| `|E` | **Embodied** | sensorimotor, concrete, direct engagement | bodily action / sensor–actuator control |

Lowercase `f` is deliberate. Capital `F` belongs to Drives. Capital `E` after
the pipe is Embodied; capital `E` after a caret is Evaluative:

```cas
^3^E_{F7}|E
      ^        Evaluative Domain
             ^ Embodied Register
```

The four Registers apply at every Domain. A principled commitment may be held
as a high-level purpose (`|T`), explicit rule (`|A`), value-toned refusal
(`|f`), or embodied practice (`|E`). An Operational task may likewise be
directed by an abstract goal, executed as a written procedure, accompanied by
value weighting, or run through direct sensorimotor control.

Keep the other three axes fixed:

```cas
^2^P_{F2}|T    integrative attraction toward a unifying principle
^2^P_{F2}|A    explicit reasoning attracted toward that principle
^2^P_{F2}|f    value-toned affinity for that principle
^2^P_{F2}|E    embodied orientation toward that principle
```

Same Noetic, Domain, and Drive. Four modes. Register does not smuggle in a new
Noetic called Emotion or a fifth Domain called Body; it prevents those modes
from being confused with the operations and levels already present.

For an architecture inventory, a Register set specifies occupancy:

```cas
^3^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩
```

This says the state is present in those three Registers. It makes no claim
about whether the manifestations fire together, independently, or as a fused
unit. That distinction belongs to the operators in the next section.

## 2.6 Operator Discipline v7.7 — +, ×, |⟨…⟩, ->

A state literal says what is present. An operator says what claim you are
making about the relation between states. v7.7 keeps four claims separate.

### `|⟨…⟩` — Register-set specification

Use the set when you are describing **where a state exists** and nothing about
its dynamics:

```cas
^3^P|⟨A,f,T⟩
```

Static architecture. The state occupies three Registers. No simultaneity, no
redundancy, no fusion has been asserted.

### `+` — co-presence or association

Use plus when terms are active together and remain structurally distinct:

```cas
^3^P|A + ^3^P|f + ^3^P|T
```

Three co-present manifestations. Each can fail while the others remain. In a
safety circuit that is redundant guard coverage, not one unified commitment.
Plus is associative and commutative: order does not make one term govern the
others.

Read `+` as **associates with**. If the sentence survives, the operator is
probably right.

### `×` — genuine integration with a named result

Use multiplication when operands do integrative work and produce a new,
explicitly named result:

```cas
integrate refusal:
    ( ^3^P|A × ^3^P|f × ^3^P|T ) = ^3^P|Ω_refusal;
```

The result `Ω_refusal` is load-bearing. Remove it and the expression is
underdefined: three instances were multiplied, but nothing says what the
integration produced. If you cannot name the emergent result or state the
fusion rule, use `+` or `|⟨…⟩`.

Different-state integration follows the same discipline:

```cas
integrate composed_judgment:
    ( ^5^C_{F2}|A × ^6^C_{F6}|A ) = ^1^C_{F2}|A;
```

Accumulated formation and decomposition integrate into a named Mind-state that
can process the judgment. The operands differ, but the result is still stated.

Read `×` as **intensifies through**. If the words describe only adjacency, the
operator is too strong.

Multiplication also obeys Domain precedence. It may descend or remain at a
level; it may not manufacture a result above its inputs. `^O × ^P` is the
shorthand for a forbidden ascent, not a complete literal expression. In a
listing, any integration whose result outranks an operand fails validation.

### `->` — directed flow, binary at expression level

Use the arrow when one node or state flows into another:

```cas
^6^C_{F2}|A -> ^9^E_{F2}|f
```

Analysis flows into a value-weighted conclusion. The arrow does not fuse the
states. It orders a transition.

At expression level, `->` is binary. This is not legal:

```cas
a -> b -> c
```

If a circuit has two edges, write two connections. If you mean an ordered
multi-step traversal, use the statement form:

```cas
sequence a -> b -> c [enforce=strict];
```

Inside `CJT< … >`, `=>` marks the amplified transition to the effect terminal
and the spaced ` | ` separates cause from bias. Elsewhere the pipe introduces
a Register. Context fixes the job; it never licenses `|` as an English label.

The four-way decision is short:

1. **Only specifying occupied Registers?** Use `|⟨…⟩`.
2. **Several manifestations present but distinct?** Use `+`.
3. **A genuine fused state produced?** Use `×` and name the result.
4. **A directed edge or time-ordered transition?** Use binary `->`; use
   `sequence` for a chain.
```{=latex}
\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\setcounter{figure}{3}
% Figure 2-D -- the v7.7 operator decision plate.
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  x=1cm, y=1cm,

                 inner sep=2pt, font=\sffamily\scriptsize},

]

\caption{Operator decision plate}
\label{fig:02-D}

```


> **Bench Note — the three multi-register forms are three different failure
> profiles.** A set tells you only that the parts are fitted. Plus tells you
> three paths can fail separately. Multiplication with a named result tells you
> the paths have become one integrated mechanism and may collapse as one.
> Replacing all three with a vague word like *holistic* destroys exactly the
> diagnostic information the notation was built to preserve.

---

## Failure Modes

| Mode | Mechanism | What you observe | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Axis swap** | grid form `P3` copied left-to-right as `^P^3` | a literal that does not tokenize, or the wrong coordinate in a log | say “P-three / Negative Principled,” then write `^3^P` |
| **Noetic drift** | `^3` used for critique or `^8` for deduction | prose and canonical definition disagree | critique is `^6`; association is `^8`; run the colloquialism test |
| **Domain/Register conflation** | Evaluative `^E` treated as Affective `|f`, or Embodied `|E` | the same letter appears to do two jobs | locate it: caret = Domain, pipe = Register |
| **Motive as topology** | a Drive is expected to repair a wrong Noetic or path | the wrong operation runs with more energy | fix Noetic, Domain, and wiring before touching the rail |
| **Pipe as gloss** | `F3|Vitality`, `^3|aversion` | tokenizer error | pipe only introduces T/A/f/E or a Register set |
| **Bare multiplication** | co-presence written with `×`, no emergent result | invalid same-Noetic multi-register expression | use `+`, `|⟨…⟩`, or name `Ω_result` |
| **Arrow chain as expression** | binary `->` treated as variadic | `a -> b -> c` fails parsing | write two edges or a `sequence` statement |
| **Silent omission** | Drive or Register dropped for visual neatness | two different mechanisms share one label | restore the slot or document why it is unknown |

---

## Test Points — Four-Pass Literal Inspection

You do not need a running board to probe a notation error. Inspect every
literal at four points before it enters a schematic.

| TP | Probe | Pass condition | Typical catch |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TP1 — form** | token shape | `^n^D_{Fk}|R`, legal values, braces and case correct | `|F`, `^Q`, missing brace |
| **TP2 — meaning** | Noetic against canonical definition | the scene’s natural colloquialism and the definition agree | critique mislabeled `^3`; deduction mislabeled `^8` |
| **TP3 — placement** | Domain, Drive, Register | level, motive, and mode are each independently justified | Evaluative / Affective conflation; motive invented after the fact |
| **TP4 — relation** | surrounding operator | occupancy / co-presence / integration / flow claim matches the symbol | bare `×`; chained `->`; hidden domain ascent |

The round-trip test is the final probe: read the literal into plain English,
put the text aside, and reconstruct the literal from your sentence. If the two
coordinates differ, the sentence hid an axis.

---

## What This Chapter Established

- A full CAS literal answers four independent questions in one fixed order:
  **what** Noetic, **where** Domain, **why** Drive, **how** Register.
- The ten canonical Noetic names and definitions do not change with audience or
  substrate. `^3` is aversion, `^8` is associative triggering, and `^5` is
  accumulated formation.
- `P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O` is precedence, not moral rank. Causation descends one
  junction at a time; outcomes return only through filtered, low-gain feedback.
- Drives supply motive and potential; they do not repair wrong topology. Their
  pairs are F1↔F7, F2↔F6, F3↔F5, with F4 self-dual.
- Register is optional but never decorative. `|T`, `|A`, `|f`, and `|E`
  distinguish abstract, analytical, affective, and embodied operation without
  changing the state’s Noetic or Domain.
- v7.7 separates Register occupancy `|⟨…⟩`, distinct co-presence `+`, genuine
  integration `×` with a named result, and directed binary flow `->`.
- A validator is specified to reject malformed or inadmissible notation.
  “Compiler rejects” in this book names that design contract, not a claim that
  a production compiler has already shipped.

- b) “The proposal made me recoil before I could explain why.”

- d) “After the reminder, the appointment date popped into my head.”

```cas
a -> b -> c
```

Identify the Domain-precedence problem. Describe the lawful architecture for

- b) Choose a dominant Drive and Register for each, giving one sentence of

# The Cognitive Junction Transistor

*Three terminals, six parameters, four regions — the part that turns a small cause into a large effect, and what happens when you leave one terminal unwired*

---

An operator stands in front of a mirror at six in the morning and says *I am wealthy* forty times. She does it again the next morning, and for seven months. At the end she is exactly as wealthy as she was in the first week and considerably more tired.

Another operator, down the road, runs one working on one night — ninety minutes — and inside a season something moves.

The usual explanations are about the person. She didn't believe hard enough. She had blocks. Her vibration was low. Set all of that aside and put both operations on the bench.

The mirror operation has a cause terminal — the sentence — and an effect terminal — the result she wants. It has nothing on the third. Nothing governs how much of the cause becomes effect. Write it out in CCDL and it does not compile: `E-CJT-001 MissingBias`. A transistor with no base is not a transistor. It is a wire.

A wire has gain 1. Forty repetitions through a wire produce forty repetitions out the far end and not one thing more. That is not a failure of sincerity; it is what a two-terminal device does, every time, for everyone.

The other operation had the third terminal wired. This chapter is about that terminal — what sits on it, what it costs to move, and the six numbers that tell you what the device will do when you try.

---

## 3.1 The Bell Labs Moment — Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley

On 16 December 1947, at Bell Telephone Laboratories in Murray Hill, New Jersey, John Bardeen and Walter Brattain pressed two gold contacts against a sliver of germanium and measured a signal coming out larger than the one going in. The apparatus was a plastic wedge wrapped in gold foil, held down by a spring against a slab of semiconductor. It was the point-contact transistor.

Their group leader, William Shockley, had not been in the room. Over the following weeks he worked out a cleaner and far more manufacturable arrangement — the **junction** transistor — and it is Shockley's version, not the wedge of plastic, that became the template for every transistor since. The three shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics.

What matters at the bench is not the rivalry. It is the function, and the function is one sentence: **a small current at one terminal governs a large current between the other two.**

Before that afternoon, amplification meant vacuum tubes. After it, it became a part you could solder, then print a billion of on a fingernail. Every computing system built since rests on that one sentence.

Now the claim this book is built on.

**A cognitive transition has the same structure.** Not resembles. Has. An Idea arrives, it is processed against everything the Mind already is, and something comes out — usually much larger than what went in. Four words of question produce four paragraphs of answer. One remark from a stranger produces three days of rumination.

Be precise about the claim. The formalisms differ and stay different: a transistor obeys semiconductor physics, a cognitive transition obeys Fisher-Rao geometry on the open probability simplex Δ39° (Appendix L). What is claimed is that **the role each terminal plays is the same role** — enough, because eighty years of amplifier discipline then transfers intact. Biasing, load lines, operating points, runaway and how to tame it, all available to an operator who can name their three terminals.

The component is the **Cognitive Junction Transistor (CJT)**, the most important part in this book. Every board in Part III has at least one; most have four or more.

## 3.2 The Three Terminals: Cause (Collector), Bias (Base), Effect (Emitter)

Three terminals, three jobs, and they do not substitute for one another.

**C — Cause. The collector. The Idea arriving.** The input: the prompt, the stimulus, the sentence, the image on the billboard. Canonically an **`^8` Above/Cause** state — *an Idea that triggers a different Idea than itself to come to Mind.*

Hold the anti-drift rule here; it is the one operators break first. `^8` Above/Cause is **associative triggering**. *That reminds me. One thing leads to another.* It is not deductive reasoning. A syllogism is not an `^8`; a smell that surfaces a childhood kitchen is. When you wire a cause terminal you are wiring what *triggers*, not what *proves*.

**B — Bias. The base. What governs the transition.** The control terminal, and the one the mirror operation left dangling. Canonically a **`^5` Female** state — *a Mind impregnated with an Idea, the Ideas a Mind is composed of.* Everything the operator already is: education, habit, temperament, the sum of accumulated experience. For an AI system the same terminal carries the training corpus and fine-tuning, which is why fine-tuning is a bias-terminal intervention and prompting is not. On a designed board it also carries the engineered controls layered over that substrate — the charter, the Dial settings (Chapter 6.2), the Drive configuration.

The bias is *who is doing the processing.* Change it and the same cause produces a different effect. Two people receive identical news and respond differently: same collector, different base.

**E — Effect. The emitter. The Idea produced.** Canonically **`^9` Below/Effect** — *the Idea brought to Mind by an Above/Cause trigger.* The landing.

`^8` and `^9` are an involution pair (Chapter 2.2). Cause and effect are duals, and the CJT is the device that maps one onto the other under the governance of a third thing.

| Terminal | Transistor part | What it carries | Canonical Noetic |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C — Cause** | Collector — the large input current | the Idea arriving | `^8` Above/Cause |
| **B — Bias** | Base — the small control current | accumulated substrate + charter + Dials + Drives | `^5` Female |
| **E — Effect** | Emitter — the amplified output | the Idea produced | `^9` Below/Effect |
| **β — Gain** | I_c / I_b | how far the effect moves per unit of cause | — |

Written form, and it reads left to right exactly the way the signal flows:

```cas
cjt q1: CJT< ^8^C_{F2}|A | ^5^P_{F7}|T => ^9^C_{F6}|A >
        [β=2.4, g_m=1.2, rπ=2.0, sat=0.78, cutoff=0.10, region=active];
```

The `|` is the base junction — the cause meeting the bias. The `=>` is the amplified transition out the emitter. Read it aloud: *a reasoned question arrives in the Cognitive domain, driven by Wisdom, analytical; it is processed against a transcendent principled substrate driven by Purpose; and it produces a structured analytical answer, 2.4 times larger than it went in.*

Note what the `|` is **not**. In CAS it introduces the Register and nothing else — the `|A` and `|T` above. Inside a `CJT< … >` the same character marks the base junction. Those are its only two jobs. It is never a label and never a gloss: `F3|Vitality` is a syntax error, not a helpful annotation. Drive names go in the prose.

**The bias must sit at or above the cause in the domain order.** P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O (Chapter 2.3). Above, the cause is `^C` and the bias is `^P`; P outranks C, so the connection is admissible. Reverse it and the compiler refuses:

```cas
// REFUSED — E-CJT-008 CjtCrossDomainBias
cjt bad_1: CJT< ^8^P_{F7}|T | ^5^O_{F5}|E => ^9^P_{F7}|T > [β=2.0];
```

An Operational state biasing a Principled transition lets the outcome rewrite the principle — last week's result governing this week's belief. That is the prompt-injection signature in an AI system and post-hoc rationalization in a person, and it is one defect. Chapter 8.4 gives the single lawful route from `^O` back to `^P`; it does not go through a bias terminal, it goes through a filter and a small gain and takes weeks.

> **Bench Note — the bias is mandatory, and leaving it off is the most common build error in the book.**
> Most failed operations are two-terminal. An affirmation with no substrate behind it. A sigil charged with no accumulated `^5` to charge it against. A safety instruction written in prose with nothing structural governing whether it is followed. In each case the operator built a wire and expected an amplifier. The diagnostic is one question: *what governs how much of this cause becomes effect?* If the answer is "my intention," you have named the cause twice and still have no base. Write the substrate down as a state literal. If you cannot, that is the finding.

---

## 3.3 The Six Parameters — β, g_m, rπ, sat, I_c(max), cutoff

Six numbers describe a CJT completely enough to build with. Every one is a **design choice** — a value you specify when you write the part, not a measurement pulled off a running system. A datasheet for a part you are designing is a specification, not a lab report.

For each: what it means, the design range this book uses, and what breaks on either side.

### β — cognitive gain

The ratio of how far the effect moves to how far the cause moves, measured as Fisher-Rao geodesic distance on Δ39°:

```
d_FR(p,q) = 2 · arccos( Σ √(p_k · q_k) )
β = d_FR(E_after, E_before) / d_FR(C_after, C_before)
```

β = 2.4 means the effect travelled 2.4 times the Fisher-Rao distance the cause travelled, across the 40-dimensional state manifold. Not "felt 2.4 times as strong." A ratio of distances under the only metric invariant for probability distributions — Euclidean distance on the simplex is invalid here (Appendix L). You will not compute this by hand; the point is that β is a real ratio and not a vibe.

Three regimes: **β < 1** attenuates, **β = 1** passes through unchanged, **β > 1** amplifies.

**Design range: 0.5 to 4.0.** Below 0.5 the stage damps so hard nothing survives to the next stage, which is only what you want on a deliberate limiter. Above 4.0 a single stage is hard to keep stable, and the moment it sits in a loop the round-trip gain approaches 1 and the compiler refuses it: `E-CJT-005 GainDivergence`. Loop gains belong in the 0.05–0.3 band. Chapter 10.1 selects β by operation type; Chapter 13.4 tabulates it by desire class.

You will see **β = ∞** on comparator-style stages — a refusal that fires fully on the least input, no partial output. That is an **idealization**, the standard one for a hard switch, and a validator rejects it: the grammar requires β finite and ≥ 0. Write the idealization if you mean it, then build with a large finite gain. Above roughly β = 10 the behaviour is indistinguishable, because the `sat` ceiling shapes the output long before the gain does.

### g_m — transconductance, which is framing sensitivity

`g_m = ∂effect / ∂bias`. How much the output swings for a small nudge at the *control* terminal.

This is the parameter that explains why rewording a question changes the answer. A high-g_m stage is a hair trigger: shift the framing slightly — a different word, a Dial moved one notch — and the output moves a lot. A low-g_m stage barely notices.

**Design range: 0.2 to 3.0.** Below 0.2 the bias terminal is decorative: move the substrate all you like and the output does not care, leaving the device unsteerable and blind to context that ought to matter. Above 3.0 the stage amplifies framing noise — incidental phrasing, the mood of the room, whatever the last stimulus was. High g_m is not a defect in itself. It is the exploitable property, and Chapters 17 and 18 are largely about circuits built to find it.

### rπ — input resistance, which is stubbornness to bias change

`rπ = β / g_m`. How hard you have to push to actually move the substrate.

High rπ: sticky bias, the disposition does not shift. Low rπ: compliant bias, updates readily.

**Design range: 0.5 to 20.** Toward zero the substrate offers no resistance and whatever is presented writes straight into it. Chapter 17.1 calls that the gnosis state; it is the goal of self-hypnosis, reached by a ramp (Chapter 17.2) with the operator's own consent. It is also the vulnerability the conditioning circuits of Chapter 16 manufacture in someone who did not consent. Same parameter, same value, entirely different ethics — and the notation cannot tell them apart. Only the consent architecture can.

Toward infinity you get the operator no operation can reach. Every calibration writes to the bias; St. John's β_next (Chapter 5.3) has nowhere to land. Practice accumulates nothing, which the operator experiences as being unusually principled.

> **Bench Note — you get to pick two of the three, never all three.**
> `rπ = β / g_m` is not a coincidence of definitions; it is a constraint you live under. Want high gain **and** a framing-insensitive stage? Then β is large, g_m is small, rπ is large — a stubborn substrate no operation can calibrate. Want high gain **and** an easily-tuned bias? Then g_m must be large, and the output flips when someone rephrases the question. Working stages take β = 2.4, g_m = 1.2, rπ = 2.0, moderate everything. Safety stages take high β with high rπ deliberately, because a guard you can talk down is not a guard. Write all three down. If the third surprises you, the first two were wrong.

### sat — the saturation point

The effect activation at which the output plateaus. Past it, more cause produces no more effect.

**Legal range (0, 1]. Design: 0.60–0.80 for working stages, 0.85–0.97 for safety stages.**

Working stages want headroom. A stage saturating at 0.60 clips a strong cause: the operation runs, and what leaves the emitter is the flattened version. Push sat toward 1.0 and you have removed the ceiling, which sounds generous and leaves the next stage no defined maximum to design against.

Safety stages invert the intuition: **a lower ceiling makes a stronger guarantee.** Chapter 24.2 specifies the principled refusal at `sat = 0.85`. At that ceiling the refusal plateaus easily — it does not take an overwhelming risk to saturate it, only a sufficient one — and once there the stage has stopped responding to its cause. You cannot out-argue a saturated CJT, because saturation *is* the condition of no longer depending on the input. A high ceiling leaves room for a forceful cause to keep pushing the decision around.

The knee sits at a cause activation of `sat / β`. With sat = 0.78 and β = 2.4 the knee is at **0.325**; everything above that is wasted drive. That one division gives the usable input range of the stage, and it is the first arithmetic to run on any CJT you did not design yourself.

### I_c(max) — maximum effect intensity

The absolute ceiling on output activation — the hard top of the plateau. `sat` is where the curve knees over; `I_c(max)` is the highest activation the effect state is ever permitted to carry.

**Range 0 to 1, with `sat ≤ I_c(max)` always.**

It is the one of the six that never appears inside a parameter block. `I_c(max)` is a property of the substrate the path runs on, not a key you type in `[…]`; the validator range-checks `β`, `sat` and `cutoff` and knows nothing about your substrate. The ordering `sat ≤ I_c(max)` is therefore checked by eye, every time, and Chapter 10.2 works through what happens when you get it backwards — the designed plateau is never reached, the stage never latches, and the overload lands on the capacitor instead of the limiter you thought you installed.

Set it at 1.0 on a stage whose effect feeds a `^5` capacitor and you have authorised a full-scale write into accumulated formation — the dielectric-breakdown territory of Chapter 7.4. Set it too low and the stage cannot drive the next one:

**The cascade interlock.** In a chain of CJTs (Chapter 10.5), stage *n*'s `I_c(max)` must exceed stage *n+1*'s `cutoff`, with margin. Miss it and the cascade dies silently — every stage validates, the board compiles clean, no signal reaches the far end. It is the commonest cascade fault and it raises no error code, because nothing is wrong with any individual part.

### cutoff — the bias floor

The bias activation below which β ≈ 0 and the stage does not fire.

**Legal range [0, 1), with `cutoff < sat`. Design: 0.05–0.20.**

Too high and the stage is dead for ordinary inputs. On a `^3^P` guard that is the most dangerous condition on any board — `E-CJT-003 CjtCutoff` — because the guard never fires and nothing looks wrong. The board runs. It answers everything. It has no safety element and reports none missing.

Too low and the stage fires on noise. On a desire board that is an operator whose attention is captured by every passing stimulus; on a guard it is constant false refusal, which trains the operator to disable the guard — how a too-sensitive safety element becomes no safety element.

---

## 3.4 Operating Regions: Cutoff, Active, Saturation, Breakdown

A CJT is linear only in one of its four regions. An operator who does not know which region a stage is in is an operator about to be surprised.

**Cutoff.** The bias sits below its threshold. The cause arrives and nothing comes out — the stimulus lands on a substrate that gives it no purchase. Effect ≈ 0 no matter how hard you drive the cause. This is why shouting at someone who does not care does not work: you are increasing collector drive on a device in cutoff.

**Active.** The linear region, and the one you design for. Effect ≈ β·cause across a working range. Almost everything you build should rest here.

**Saturation.** The output has hit `sat`. More cause changes nothing. Sometimes exactly what you want — a refusal at its ceiling that cannot be argued higher (Chapter 24.2). Sometimes a fault — a mind that has stopped taking evidence because it is already as certain as it can get.

**Breakdown.** Not a boundary of the active region but a different kind of event. The stage stops obeying its own transfer function, `rπ` collapses so the bias governs nothing, and **the emitter reports the involution of the designed Noetic.** `^2` Positive comes out as `^3` Negative — fascination arrives as disgust. `^5` Female inverts to `^6` Male; `^8` Above/Cause inverts to `^9` Below/Effect (Chapter 2.2).

That distinction is the whole diagnostic. Cutoff and saturation produce **too little or too much of the right thing**. Breakdown produces **the wrong thing**. If the emitter's Noetic is not the one you designed, you are not looking at a tuning problem and no Dial will fix it.

### The transition conditions

Regions are not moods. Each boundary has a condition you can write down.

| From | To | Condition | Reversible? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cutoff | Active | bias rises above `cutoff` | Yes — falls back when bias drops |
| Active | Saturation | cause reaches `sat / β` | Yes — recovers below the knee |
| Saturation | Active | cause falls below `sat / β`, **and** no latch holds the stage | Yes, unless a fuse has fired (Chapter 11.1) |
| Active or Saturation | Breakdown | sustained drive above the plateau with the effect returning as cause, or a spike past `I_c(max)` with no series constraint | **No** |
| Breakdown | anything | — | **No lawful return** |

Three of the four transitions are two-way. The fourth is a one-way door, and that asymmetry is why every board in this book carries a series resistor (Chapters 4.2 and 6) and a fuse (Chapter 11.1). Constraint is not friction to be minimised. It is what keeps the cause below `I_c(max)` when the drive spikes.
```{=latex}
\begin{figure}[htbp]

    font=\sffamily\footnotesize\bfseries},
```

### Runaway is how you get there

Breakdown almost never arrives as a single spike. It arrives as a loop.

In electronics a transistor's gain rises with temperature: more current, more heat, more gain, more current. Nothing external is needed — the device cooks itself into breakdown.

Read *temperature* as **activation intensity** and the cognitive version is identical. A transition whose gain rises with its own activation feeds its effect back as a larger cause, which at higher activation gets a higher β, which produces a still larger effect. That is the signature of an escalating rumination loop, a rage spiral, a hyperstition that has lost its damping (Chapter 14.5). Left alone it walks the stage up its own curve into breakdown.

The curve shows the seed: the plateau tilts gently upward, because strong outputs feed back. A `^6^E` evaluative output strong enough to notice becomes an `^8^C` trigger surfacing further Ideas, and the strength of the result re-enters as new cause.

You do not fix runaway by lowering β once it has started. You fix it with negative feedback and series constraint installed *before* it starts.

> **Bench Note — `rπ → 0` happens two ways and they look identical until you probe the emitter.**
> Both the gnosis state (Chapter 17.1) and breakdown drive input resistance to zero. In gnosis, rπ is walked down by a ramp while β and `sat` stay in specification, and the substrate re-stiffens when the ramp is removed. In breakdown, rπ collapses because the stage was overdriven, and it does not re-stiffen. From outside both present as someone who has become highly suggestible.
> The distinguishing measurement is TP4, the emitter's Noetic identity. Under gnosis the effect is still the Noetic you designed. Under breakdown it is the involution. Take that reading before concluding a session went well. This is circuit topology and nothing more; it diagnoses no one. If you or someone you work with is in real distress, that is a matter for a qualified clinician, and no schematic substitutes for one.

---

## 3.5 The CJT Datasheet — Full Parameter Table

The whole part in two linked tables. Keep them open while you design.

| Parameter | Symbol | Electronic meaning | CAS meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cognitive gain** | β | I_c / I_b | `d_FR(ΔE) / d_FR(ΔC)` on Δ39° |
| **Trans\allowbreak{}conductance** | g_m | ∂I_c / ∂V_be | ∂effect / ∂bias — framing sensitivity |
| **Input resistance** | rπ | β / g_m | stubbornness to bias change |
| **Saturation point** | sat | V_ce(sat) | effect plateau; added cause → no Δeffect |
| **Max effect intensity** | I_c(max) | absolute output ceiling | hard top of the plateau; substrate property, **not a param-block key** |
| **Cutoff** | cutoff | base threshold | bias floor below which β ≈ 0 |
| **Operating region** | region | — | declared intent |

| Parameter | Legal range | Design default | Fails low | Fails high |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cognitive gain** | finite, ≥ 0 | 2.4 | < 0.5: nothing survives to the next stage | > 4.0: loop instability, `E-CJT-005` |
| **Trans\allowbreak{}conductance** | ≥ 0 | 1.2 | < 0.2: bias decorative, stage unsteerable | > 3.0: output flips on rewording |
| **Input resistance** | ≥ 0 | 2.0 | → 0: substrate writes on contact (gnosis; Ch.16 vulnerability) | → ∞: no operation can calibrate the operator |
| **Saturation point** | (0, 1] | 0.78; safety 0.85 | working stages clip strong causes | safety refusals become negotiable |
| **Max effect intensity** | [sat, 1], by eye | 0.92 | cascade dropout — next stage never fires | full-scale write into `^5`; Ch.7.4 |
| **Cutoff** | [0, 1), `< sat` | 0.10 | stage fires on noise; false refusals | dead guard, `E-CJT-003` — worst fault on any board |
| **Operating region** | cutoff \| active \| saturation \| breakdown | active | — | contradicting numbers are flagged, not guessed |

Three standard operating points, as a starting library. Each set is a design choice, stated with its reason.

| Build | β | g_m | rπ | sat | I_c(max) | cutoff | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Working amplifier** | 2.4 | 1.2 | 2.0 | 0.78 | 0.92 | 0.10 | Moderate everywhere; knee at 0.325; headroom above `sat` for the next stage |
| **Safety guard** | 3.0 | 0.3 | 10.0 | 0.85 | 0.90 | 0.08 | High gain, very low framing sensitivity — cannot be reworded down; low `sat` latches early; low `cutoff` never asleep |
| **Damper / limiter** | 0.6 | 0.6 | 1.0 | 0.40 | 0.45 | 0.15 | β < 1 by design; low ceiling; bleeds an oscillating stage without opening the loop |

The safety guard's rπ = 10.0 is not chosen. It is `β / g_m` and follows from the other two — the second Bench Note doing its work. You asked for high gain and framing insensitivity, and stubbornness is what you got.

Five of the six columns are writable in a `[…]` block. `I_c(max)` is not; it is the substrate figure you carry alongside the listing and check by hand.

Datasheets for every part in the library are in **Appendix C**. The grammar, the writable parameter keys, their legal ranges and the full error-code table are in **Appendix B**.

---

## Failure Modes

| Mode | Mechanism | What you observe | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Missing bias** | No base terminal wired | Output equals input; repetition produces only repetition | Name the substrate as a state literal and wire it; `E-CJT-001` |
| **Unwanted cutoff** | Bias below `cutoff` | Emitter reads ≈ 0; on a guard, the board answers everything and reports nothing wrong | Raise bias or lower `cutoff`; find the stage starving it; `E-CJT-003` |
| **Unwanted saturation** | Effect pinned at `sat` | Added cause yields no Δeffect; certainty that will not take evidence | Raise series R (Chapter 4.2) or raise `sat`; `W-CJT-004` |
| **Framing twitch** | g_m above design band | Output swings on rephrasing; large A/B deltas from small copy changes | Lower g_m, accepting the rπ change it forces; Chapter 10.3 |
| **Sticky bias** | rπ above design band | Practice accumulates nothing; calibration writes have no effect | Raise g_m or lower β; recheck against Chapter 5.3 |
| **Cascade dropout** | Stage *n* `I_c(max)` < stage *n+1* `cutoff` | Board compiles clean, every stage validates, nothing reaches the output | Raise upstream `I_c(max)` or lower downstream `cutoff` |
| **Thermal runaway** | Gain rises with activation; effect returns as larger cause | β climbing stage to stage; escalation with no external input | Negative feedback and series constraint *before* the loop closes; `E-CJT-005` |
| **Breakdown** | Sustained overdrive, or a spike past `I_c(max)` | Emitter reports the involution of the designed Noetic | No repair. Margin only. Fuse and series R upstream (Chapters 11.1, 24.3) |
| **Bias hijack** | A lower-domain state wired to the base | The outcome now governs the principle | Remove it; route through the lawful O→P path (Chapter 8.4); `E-CJT-008` |

---

## Test Points

Four probes: one per terminal, plus one for identity. Placing them is the difference between a board you can certify and a board you can only hope about.

| TP | Node | What it reads | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TP1** | bias terminal | Bias activation against `cutoff` | Above `cutoff` with margin — 0.10 spec, read ≥ 0.15. At or below = dead stage |
| **TP2** | cause terminal | Cause activation against the knee | Below `sat / β` — 0.325 on the working build. Above = drive wasted in saturation |
| **TP3** | effect terminal | Effect activation | ≈ β·cause below the knee; pinned at `sat` above it. Anything else = wrong region |
| **TP4** | effect terminal | **Noetic identity of the output** | The designed Noetic. Involution present = breakdown, and no parameter change repairs it |

TP1 through TP3 tell you which region you are in. **TP4 tells you whether the device is still the device you built** — the only one of the four that separates a hard-working stage from a broken one. Take it on a schedule, not on suspicion; breakdown fails silently and stays failed.

---

## What This Chapter Established

- A cognitive transition is a **three-terminal device** — cause, bias, effect. The claim is structural isomorphism of terminal roles, not shared physics; the CJT obeys Fisher-Rao geometry on Δ39°.
- **Bias is mandatory.** A CJT with no base is a wire, gain 1, and repetition through a wire never amplifies. `E-CJT-001` is the commonest failed-operation diagnosis in this book.
- **The bias must sit at or above the cause in P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O.** A lower-domain state on the base is the prompt-injection signature and the post-hoc-rationalization signature — one defect.
- **β, g_m and rπ are two free choices, not three.** `rπ = β / g_m` binds them; high gain plus framing stability necessarily buys a stubborn substrate.
- **The knee sits at `sat / β`** — the usable input range of any stage, and the first arithmetic to run on a CJT you did not design.
- **Low `sat` on a safety stage is the stronger guarantee.** A saturated stage has stopped depending on its cause and cannot be argued higher.
- **Three of the four region transitions are reversible; breakdown is not.** Cutoff and saturation give too little or too much of the right thing; breakdown gives the involution, and the fix is margin beforehand, never repair after. `rπ → 0` has a consented form and an overdriven form, and TP4 separates them.
- **Cascade interlock: stage *n*'s `I_c(max)` must exceed stage *n+1*'s `cutoff`.** Violate it and every stage validates while the board does nothing, with no error code raised.

---

# CAS Ohm's Law

*Three quantities, one equation, and the only mode of it that finds the part you forgot to draw*

---

A repair bench. A board arrives described as "works, but slow." The technician does not open the manual. She puts one probe on the supply rail, reads 12.0 volts, and in four seconds the power supply is exonerated. She breaks the path, puts the meter in series, and reads 40 milliamps where the drawing says 120.

Then she divides. Twelve volts over forty milliamps is 300 ohms. The schematic in front of her says that path should present 100. There are two hundred ohms in that circuit nobody designed, and she now knows three things she did not know a minute ago: the fault is real, it is resistive, and it is twice the size of everything intentional in the path.

She has not found the component yet. She will — a corroded connector, a lifted pad, a resistor drifted out of tolerance — but the search is bounded now. One missing quantity, one place to look.

That division is the most useful operation in electronics, and it is not prediction. It is inference. Two things you can measure produce a third thing you cannot measure at all.

Now the other bench. Someone says they want it. The wanting is not in question — you have watched them mean it for a year. Nothing moves. The available explanations are motivation, discipline, and sincerity, and not one of them is a quantity, which is why arguing about them never terminates.

This chapter replaces that argument with a division.
