## 11.2 Oscillators — Generating Cognitive Rhythms (^7)

`^7` **Rhythm** is *the rate and pattern a Mind is exposed to an Idea, entraining/conditioning it.* The definition names two quantities: **rate** is the period, **pattern** is the duty cycle. An oscillator sets both.

```cas
osc clock: Oscillator< signal=claim, source=cadence, period=7.0, duty=0.15,
                       sustain=90.0 >;                       // days
```

It adds no energy. It converts a *sustained* drive into a *periodic* one, and it is worth a component because of Chapter 7.3: the `^5` Female capacitor leaks. One overwhelming impression does not hold; a smaller one redeposited before the last drains will.

That is a charge pump, and it has arithmetic. Let each exposure deposit `q` into a capacitor with leakage time constant `τ_leak`, on the 0–10 scale of Chapter 7.2:

```
Q_max = q / (1 − e^(−T/τ_leak))       Q_min = Q_max × e^(−T/τ_leak)
ripple = q                             (always — the ripple IS one pulse)
```

Take `τ_leak = 30 days`, `q = 0.8`, and vary the period.

| `T` (days) | `Q_max` | `Q_min` | ripple / `Q_max` | Character |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 24.4 → clips at 10 | 10 | 0% | Pinned; every pulse after the first fortnight is spent for nothing |
| 7 | 3.84 | 3.04 | 21% | Design point |
| 10 | 2.82 | 2.02 | 28% | Ripple limit |
| 30 | 1.27 | 0.47 | 63% | Impression, gone, impression, gone — no plateau forms |

Thirty times the frequency buys a *pinned* substrate, not a proportionally larger one: the ceiling arrives before the arithmetic does. The last row is the commoner failure, experienced as starting over each time.

**Design rule: `T ≤ τ_leak / 3`.** That holds ripple under about thirty percent, where the plateau reads as a level rather than separate events. Above `τ_leak` there is no plateau; far below `τ_leak / 10` you pay for pulses landing on a full capacitor.

**Duty cycle** is the half operators skip. Design band: **0.10 to 0.25**. The gap is not wasted — it is where the mind runs its own `^6` Male decomposition, which makes the resulting `^5` composition the mind's own rather than a recording. At **duty ≥ 0.6** you have a DC level rather than a rhythm, and `^4` Vibration per exposure falls, because `^4` is *the degree to which an Idea resonates with the Mind, its impression*, and impression requires contrast. That is why over-frequency is a real advertising failure, not merely a budget one.

> **Bench Note — the objective is to make the oscillator unnecessary.**
> `sustain` is not "how long the campaign runs." It is how long you drive the pattern externally before the substrate supplies its own clock. Once entrained — entrainment is written into the canonical `^7` definition, not added by us — the `^8` Above/Cause cue fires at the expected time whether or not you present anything: associative triggering doing exactly what `^8` does, one Idea bringing another to Mind. Set `sustain ≥ 3 × τ_leak`, then run the test: **stop the external clock and see whether the cadence continues.** If it does, switch `source` to `internal`. If not, you rented a rhythm rather than building one.

## 11.3 Filters — Lowpass (τ dampening), Highpass, Notch

A filter passes some rates of change and destroys the rest. Define every filter by what it destroys; define it by what it passes and you will install one that quietly deletes the thing you needed.

**Lowpass.** One parameter: τ, the dividing line between a trend and a spike.

```cas
filter lp: LowPass< in=carried, out=trend, tau=21.0 >;   // days
```

A disturbance of duration `d` arrives attenuated to `1 − e^(−d/τ)` of its amplitude. At the τ = 21-day default of Chapter 8.4: **1 day survives at 4.6%, 3 days at 13.3%, 21 days at 63.2%, 63 days (3τ) at 95.0%.**

**What it kills** is the single dramatic event — the point, and why the O→P feedback of Chapter 8.4 is filtered before it reaches the constitution. **What it also kills** is a *genuine* permanent change. That last figure is a bill, not a bonus: an operator on a 21-day filter is two months behind a real change in their circumstances. Chapter 24.5 scales τ by experience, floor one week.

**Highpass.** The exact complement — it passes rapid change and destroys the baseline.

```
highpass(x) = x − lowpass(x)
```

So you can build one from the lowpass you already have. It gives a detector that responds to *change* while blind to *level* — and Chapter 9.3's coupling result, `V₂ = M × (di₁/dt)`, is a highpass in closed form. A coupled mind responds to the rate a conviction is moving, not to how deeply it is held, which is why the convert transmits and the thirty-year holder does not.

**What a highpass kills is your sense of level.** Monitor only through one and every change registers while nothing says whether the current state is acceptable. Hard rule: **never place a highpass on the O→P feedback path.** It passes precisely the spike the lowpass was installed to destroy, while looking in the listing like a filter.

**Notch.** Rejects a narrow band centred on `f0`, passing everything above and below. `Q = f0 / bandwidth`, so higher Q is narrower.

```cas
filter nf: Notch< in=audit, f0=0.35, Q=4.0 >;   // events/min — in-session only
```

Worked: bandwidth = 0.35 / 4 = 0.0875 events/min, so the rejected band runs 0.306 to 0.394 events/min — recurrences spaced roughly 2.5 to 3.3 minutes apart. Everything slower and faster passes untouched. This is the component behind Chapter 17.5's self-hypnosis variant and 17.6's indirect suggestion as filter bypass: it suppresses a `^6` Male self-audit *at the rate at which it interrupts a session*, without removing `^6` from the repertoire at any other rate. That distinction is the entire safety case for the part.

> **Bench Note — Q is a safety parameter, and there are places a notch may not go.**
> **Design floor: Q ≥ 3.0.** At Q = 0.5 the rejected band around `f0 = 0.35` runs from 0 to 0.7 events/min — not a notch, but most of the operator's `^6` decomposition removed under a label reading "narrow." Second, non-negotiable: **never notch a `^3^P` guard.** Redundant principled aversion is written `^3^P|A + ^3^P|f + ^3^P|T`, or `^3^P|⟨A,f,T⟩` when no interaction is claimed, because those are separately-defeasible guards rather than one fused state — a notch taking out one register leaves the others standing, which is the only reason the `+` form is worth its cost. A notch aimed at the whole guard set is a consent architecture with its own refusal removed; Chapter 16.6 analyses it so you can detect it. Third: a notch is for *in-session* suppression on a consenting, self-directed board. Anything you want gone permanently is a fuse — prohibited on `^6`.

## 11.4 Op-Amps — Differential Cognitive Amplification

An operational amplifier has two inputs and one output, and amplifies only the *difference* between them.

```
V_out = A_d × (V₊ − V₋) + A_cm × (V₊ + V₋) / 2
```

The first term is what you want. The second is the leak, and the figure of merit is **CMRR** — `A_d / A_cm` — how much better the part amplifies the difference than whatever the two inputs share.

```cas
opamp cmp: OpAmp< non_inverting=recoil, inverting=draw, output=verdict,
                  open_loop_gain=1000.0 >;
```

The cognitive content is one sentence: **a comparison is only trustworthy if the two things compared are biased identically.** Wire `^2` Positive — the Idea the Mind has an affinity for and is attracted toward — to one input and `^3` Negative — the Idea the Mind is adverse to and repelled by — to the other, give both the *same* `^5^P` accumulated formation as bias, and the output is the divergence between drawn-toward and repelled-by. `^2` and `^3` are an involution pair, which is what makes them a differential pair rather than two arbitrary probes.

Matching is stricter than it looks. The two input literals must differ in **the Noetic digit and nothing else** — same Domain, same Drive, same Register — because every axis they do not share is a difference the subtraction cannot distinguish from the finding. Compare `^2^P_{F7}|f` against `^3^P_{F7}|f` and the output is one quantity read from two sides. Compare `^2^E_{F4}|f` against `^3^P_{F7}|f` and you have subtracted an evaluative pull under one Drive from a principled recoil under another; the difference is large, stable, and about the wiring.

Say the honest difference on a proposal is **0.02**, and the framing around it — flattery, urgency, polish, verbosity — adds **3.0** to *both* inputs equally.

| CMRR | `A_d` | `A_cm` | Differential term | Common-mode term | The verdict is about |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 1000 | 1.0 | 20.0 | 3.0 | the proposal (7:1) |
| 100 | 1000 | 10 | 20.0 | 30.0 | roughly half framing |
| 10 | 1000 | 100 | 20.0 | 300.0 | the framing (1:15) |

Nothing about the proposal changed across those rows, and neither did the gain. Only the *matching* changed — and at CMRR = 10 the board reports a verdict fifteen parts presentation to one part substance, with a large number and full confidence.

> **Bench Note — high gain is not the safety property. Matched bias is.**
> Operators reach for `open_loop_gain` when a comparison feels weak, and it is the wrong knob: gain multiplies both terms together and cannot improve the ratio between them. What sets CMRR is whether the two inputs genuinely share one bias. Bias attraction against one `^5` substrate and aversion against another — different standards for two options, the ordinary human condition and not an exotic fault — and you have an **input offset**: the comparator reports a difference where there is none. It presents as a stable, invisible preference defended on the merits, because from inside the board an offset is indistinguishable from a finding.

**On `β=∞`.** The ideal comparator has unbounded open-loop gain, and the symbol names the intended behaviour — switch fully, immediately, no partial output — in one character. It is an idealisation, and the validator rejects non-finite input, correctly: a build must commit to a number. Above roughly 1000 the behaviour is indistinguishable from the limit, because the output clips at the drive rail long before the gain runs out. Write `β=∞` in an argument if you mean the limit; write `open_loop_gain=1000.0` in a listing. That clipping is a design fact in its own right: **a comparison can only report as much difference as the rail permits.**

## 11.5 Transformers — Impedance Matching Between Minds

A transformer adds no power. It trades voltage for current at a fixed ratio and hands the same power out the far side.

```
V₂ = V₁ / n        I₂ = I₁ × n        Z_reflected = Z_load × n²
```

That answers a question every operator eventually asks: *why does the same argument land on one audience and slide off another?* Not because one is smarter. Because a claim, like a source, has an **impedance** — a working point in volts and amps — and so does an audience; a mismatched source delivers a fraction of the power it has. Power into a load, with `r = Z_load / Z_source`, relative to the matched case:

```
efficiency = 4r / (1 + r)²
```

| `r` | Efficiency | What it looks like |
|---|---|---|
| 0.01 | 3.9% | A principled argument delivered unchanged to a lay audience |
| 0.32 / 3.16 | 73% | Acceptable mismatch, either direction |
| 1.00 | 100% | Matched |
| 100 | 3.9% | A popular framing delivered to a room of specialists |

**Design rule: keep `r` within a factor of about 3 either way** and you stay above 70%. Outside 10 you are below a third; outside 100, under four percent.

Work the match. A claim held at `^9^P_{F7}|T` — Principled domain, transcendent register, high potential and very few carriers — has `Z_source = 400 Ω_c`; a general audience path at `^9^E_{F4}|f` has `Z_load = 4 Ω_c`. Delivered raw, `r = 0.01` and **3.9%** arrives. The matching ratio is `n = √(Z_source / Z_load) = 10`. Insert a 10:1 step-down, `Z_reflected = 4 × 100 = 400 Ω_c` — matched — and delivery goes to 100%. **Twenty-five times the delivered power, with no change to the content of the claim.**

Two costs, both load-bearing.

**A transformer passes no DC.** It transmits only change, for the reason Chapter 9.3 gives: coupling is `V₂ = M × di₁/dt`. A steady, deeply-held claim at a constant level transfers *nothing*, however well matched. It requires the oscillator of Section 11.2 upstream.

**Step-down lowers the claim's voltage, and there is a floor.** Chapter 8.1 established a total forward drop of **ΣVf = 3.9** down the descent chain, below which no operational output appears. Take a claim at `V₁ = 60 V_c`: at `n = 10`, `V₂ = 6.0 V_c` and clears by 2.1; at `n = 15`, `V₂ = 4.0 V_c` and barely clears; at `n = 20`, `V₂ = 3.0 V_c` and the message **reaches everyone and moves no one**. `n_max = V₁ / ΣVf = 15.4`. That is the popularizer's dilemma exactly, and the fix is not more simplification — it is more `V₁`, or fewer junctions between the audience and the deed.

> **Bench Note — the primary may not sit below the secondary in the domain order.**
> `Transformer< primary=^9^P_{F7}|T, secondary=^9^E_{F4}|f, n=10.0 >` is a descent: Principled primary, Evaluative secondary, P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O. Reverse it and you have written an ascent, invalid for the reason `^O × ^P` is invalid — a lower domain may not drive a higher one, and the bias-domain coherence pass rejects it. The seductive use of a transformer is the illegal one: matching an operational fact *up* into a principled commitment, the counterfeit ascent of Chapter 8.3 wearing a component symbol. The lawful version is Chapter 18.3's endorsement circuit.

## The Bench Harness

All five parts on one board, so the test points have somewhere to attach.

```cas
board special_bench {                    // Ch. 11 — the five parts on one board
    input:  claim;
    output: carried;

    node substrate: ^5^P_{F7}|T;   // Female: accumulated formation, shared bias
    node cadence:   ^7^C_{F6}|A;   // Rhythm: presentation schedule
    node draw:      ^2^P_{F7}|f;   // Positive: drawn toward the claim
    node recoil:    ^3^P_{F7}|f;   // Negative: visceral aversion
                                   // matched pair — same domain, same drive, same register
    node audit:     ^6^C_{F6}|A;   // Male: decomposition
    node verdict:   ^9^E_{F6}|A;   // Below/Effect: comparison result
    node carried:   ^9^O_{F4}|E;   // Below/Effect: the claim as enacted
    node trend:     ^9^O_{F4}|E;   // same literal — a filter changes tau, not type

    osc    clock: Oscillator< signal=claim, source=cadence, period=7.0, duty=0.15,
                              sustain=90.0 >;
    opamp  cmp:   OpAmp< non_inverting=recoil, inverting=draw, output=verdict,
                         open_loop_gain=1000.0 >;
    filter nf:    Notch< in=audit, f0=0.35, Q=4.0 >;          // in-session only
    xfmr   match: Transformer< primary=^9^P_{F7}|T, secondary=^9^E_{F4}|f, n=10.0 >;
    filter lp:    LowPass< in=carried, out=trend, tau=21.0 >; // days
    fuse   cap:   Fuse< path=carried, threshold=0.90, action=permanent_block >;

    feedback trend -> substrate [β=0.05];

    probe tp1: clock;     probe tp2: verdict;
    probe tp3: trend;     probe tp4: cap;
}
```

The fuse here is a **runaway cap**, not a refusal enforcer: if the claim as enacted reaches 0.90, the path is cut permanently. `carried` is an unsaturated output node, so 0.90 is reachable and the part can do its job. An enforcement fuse of the Chapter 24.3 kind belongs in series with the enforcement path instead, so that tripping *delivers* the block — and its threshold must clear the ceiling of whatever node it sits on, which is the check §11.1 asked you to run.

---

## Component and Parameter Table

Every value is a **design choice** made in this book, not a measurement.

| Ref | Parameter | Design range | Failure at other values |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F1** | `threshold`, `action` | 0.85–0.95, default 0.90; `permanent_block` | 0.50: nuisance trips. Above the guarded `sat`: never trips. `warn`: no latch |
| **OSC1** | `period`, `duty`, `sustain` | `T ≤ τ_leak/3`; 0.10–0.25; ≥ 3 × τ_leak | `T ≥ τ_leak`: 63% ripple, no plateau. duty ≥0.6: a DC level. Short sustain: drains at budget stop |
| **FLT1** | lowpass `tau` | 21 days (adept) to 6 months (novice), floor 1 week | Hours: the filter is gone, and the ascent block with it |
| **FLT2/3** | highpass; notch `Q` | `x − lowpass(x)`, rate detection only; Q ≥ 3.0 | Highpass on the O→P path: passes the spike the lowpass killed. Q = 0.5: most of `^6` gone, labelled "narrow" |
| **U1** | CMRR, `open_loop_gain`, input match | ≥ 1000 on a guard path; gain 100–1000, finite; inputs identical on Domain, Drive and Register | CMRR 10: 15 parts framing to 1 substance. `β=∞` rejected; past ~1000 the rail clips first. Mismatched axes: a permanent offset read as a finding |
| **T1** | `n`, direction | `r` within ×3 of 1, `n ≤ V₁/3.9`; primary at or above secondary | `r = 0.01`: 3.9% delivered. Past `n_max`: nobody acts. Ascent: counterfeit promotion |

---

## Failure Modes

| Mode | Mechanism | What you observe | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Unreachable fuse** | `threshold` above the guarded path's ceiling | Never trips, on any input | Read `threshold` against `sat`; move it downstream or lower it |
| **Fuse in the wrong terminal** | On the refusal, not the enforcement path | It cuts the refusal — the board fails open while logging a success | Place it in series with what must stop, not with what detects |
| **Under-clocked oscillator** | `T ≥ τ_leak` | No plateau; the operator starts from zero each cycle | Drop `T` to `τ_leak / 3` before adding drive |
| **Rented rhythm** | `sustain` short, source never internal | Pattern collapses the week external clocking stops | Extend to ≥ 3 × τ_leak; run TP1 first |
| **Highpass on the feedback path** | Complement installed where the lowpass belonged | Constitution tracks single dramatic events | Restore the lowpass; the O→P path takes trends only |
| **Wide notch** | `Q` below 3.0 | Decomposition absent outside the band; the operator cannot say what they stopped checking | Raise Q, or remove it — a wide notch is not a narrow one with tolerance |
| **Input offset** | Op-amp inputs on different `^5` substrates, or input literals differing on any axis but the Noetic digit | A confident preference defended on the merits, impossible to source | One bias net to both inputs; match Domain, Drive and Register; verify at TP2 |
| **CMRR collapse** | Gain raised to "sharpen" a weak comparison | Larger output, worse discrimination | The wrong knob. Re-match the bias |
| **Over-matched claim** | `n` past `n_max`, or no modulation | Universal reach, zero operational output; or a perfect match transferring nothing | Raise `V₁`, shorten the descent chain, put the oscillator upstream |

---

## Test Points

| TP | Node | What it reads | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TP1** | `clock` | Period, duty, whether `source` is still external | `T ≤ τ_leak/3`, duty 0.10–0.25. The real reading is taken with the clock **stopped**: cadence continues = entrained, cadence stops = rented |
| **TP2** | `verdict` | Differential output, `recoil − draw` | Near zero on a neutral input. Non-zero there is an **input offset** — either the inputs are not on one bias net, or the two literals differ on an axis other than the Noetic digit |
| **TP3** | `trend` | What survived the 21-day lowpass | ≤ 5% of a 1-day disturbance; ≥ 95% of a 63-day one. A trend tracking yesterday means τ is set in hours |
| **TP4** | `cap` | Fuse state and headroom | Intact, `threshold` verifiably **below** the ceiling of `carried`. Never tripping is not proof it works |

Read them TP2, TP1, TP3, TP4 — the comparison first, since nothing it reports counts until it is honest, then the clock, the filter, the fuse's headroom.

---

## What This Chapter Established

- **A fuse is specified entirely by its failure**, and its threshold is meaningless without the guarded path's ceiling beside it. `threshold` above `sat` is a part guaranteed to do nothing, and nothing in the listing complains.
- **Saturation and a fuse are two different locks.** Saturation latches the decision and releases when the cause falls; the fuse latches the path and never releases.
- **An oscillator converts sustained drive into periodic drive**, and exists because `^5` leaks. `T ≤ τ_leak / 3` holds ripple under 30%; at `T ≥ τ_leak` no plateau forms. Duty is the "pattern" half of `^7` Rhythm's canonical definition, and at duty ≥ 0.6 you have a DC level, with `^4` Vibration falling because impression requires contrast.
- **The objective is to make the oscillator unnecessary.** Run `sustain ≥ 3 × τ_leak`, then stop the clock — the test separating an entrained pattern from a rented one.
- **Every filter is defined by what it destroys.** A lowpass kills the spike *and* delays a genuine change by 3τ; a highpass kills your sense of level; a notch kills one recurrence rate and must never be aimed at a `^3^P` guard, at any Q.
- **Gain cannot fix a comparison — matched bias can**, and matching means the two input literals differ in the Noetic digit and nothing else. At CMRR = 10 a board reports a verdict fifteen parts framing to one part substance, confidently and with a large number.
- **A transformer changes nothing about an argument and everything about who can carry it.** Matching takes delivery from 3.9% to 100% at no cost to content — but it passes no DC, and step-down past `n_max = V₁ / ΣVf` produces a message everyone receives and no one can act on.

## Exercises

*(Answers in Appendix H.)*

**11.1** A board guards a path whose CJT is `[β=2.0, sat=0.78]` with `Fuse< path=that_node, threshold=0.90, action=permanent_block >`. State what this fuse does across every input, then give two corrections — one changing the fuse, one changing where it sits — and say which you would ship.

**11.2** A `^5` substrate has `τ_leak = 45 days`; each exposure deposits `q = 0.6`. Compute `Q_max`, `Q_min` and ripple for `T = 7`, `15` and `45 days`. Say which satisfies the design rule, and what the operator reports at `T = 45`.

**11.3** An operator wants to detect that their own principled commitments are *moving*, while staying indifferent to where they sit. Name the filter, write it in terms of the lowpass they already have, then name the one place on the board where installing it would be a serious defect — and what it would let through.

**11.4** A comparison stage runs `open_loop_gain = 1000` with `A_cm = 50`. The honest differential is 0.05; framing adds 4.0 to both inputs. Compute both output terms and their ratio, then what happens if the operator raises the gain to 4000, and why that was the wrong knob.

**11.5** A claim is held at `V₁ = 48 V_c` with `Z_source = 900 Ω_c`; the audience path has `Z_load = 9 Ω_c`. Compute (a) `r` and the efficiency with no transformer; (b) the matching `n`, confirming `Z_reflected`; (c) `V₂` at that `n` against `ΣVf = 3.9`; (d) `n_max` and the headroom left.

**11.6 (Marquee)** A campaign has run six months on a weekly cadence against a substrate with `τ_leak = 30 days`, and the plateau has stopped rising. The operator proposes doubling the budget: same period, `duty` raised from 0.15 to 0.70.

a) Compute `Q_max` and ripple at `q = 0.8`, and say why the plateau stopped rising.
b) Explain, in terms of `^4` Vibration and the canonical `^7` Rhythm definition, what raising duty to 0.70 will do.
c) Describe the TP1 stop-the-clock check, both outcomes, and what each means for the budget.
d) Write a CCDL fragment for the corrected oscillator plus a fuse capping runaway on the enacted path. State the ceiling you assume and why your threshold clears it.

# How to Read a CCB Schematic

*The drawing conventions, the design order, the invariant list, and the four probes — everything the next eight chapters assume you already know*

---

Pin the same one-page drawing above two benches.

The first operator looks at it for a long time and calls it impressive. They can name most of the parts. Asked what the board will do, they describe the intention printed in the title block.

The second operator reads it in about ninety seconds and hands it back with three sentences. The guard stage is biased off a rail that will sit below its own firing floor for the first two years, so it will never fire and nothing on the board will say so. The gain stage is set high enough that it is pinned against its ceiling at any realistic input, so it reports a flat line and looks like stability. And the two diode drops in the signal path total 3.2, which means that below a drive of 3.2 this board produces nothing at all — not a little, none — so half the reports of "it stopped working" will be a drive problem misdiagnosed as a gain problem.

Nothing separates those two operators except a reading order. The second one checked the bias rail against every cutoff on the board, checked each gain against its ceiling, and summed the forward drops in the path. Three passes, ninety seconds, before considering what the board was *for*.

This chapter is that reading order. It is the difference between the eight board chapters that follow being drawings you can work from and pictures you can admire.

---

## 12.1 The CCB Design Process — Requirements → Block Diagram → Schematic → BOM → Test

Five steps, in this order, every board. The order is not a style preference. Each step produces the input the next one consumes, and skipping one does not save time — it moves the cost to bring-up, where it is paid at interest.

**Step 1 — Requirements.** A numbered table of what the board shall do, written before any component is chosen, each row naming a stage. The test of the table is whether you can point at any component on the finished board and name the row that demanded it; a part that serves no row is a part you added because it looked right, and it should come off. Requirements are written second, not first — 12.2 is what gets written first, and it is written first for a reason.

**Step 2 — Block diagram.** Function-level boxes, signal left to right, no component values anywhere. This is the step operators skip, and the one that catches architectural errors while they are still free: it is where you see that your guard sits downstream of your amplifier, or that your feedback path terminates on the signal path instead of a bias terminal. Both are fatal, and both are invisible in a schematic dense enough to hide them.

**Step 3 — Schematic.** The full CCDL listing: every component, every parameter, every typed node. Topology lives inside angle brackets, parameters inside square brackets, and the mechanics are worth stating once because every listing in Part III obeys them. In `CJT< cause | bias => effect >`, the `|` splits cause from bias and the `=>` splits bias from effect; the delimiters are not interchangeable, and the bias is not optional — omit it and you get `E-CJT-001`, a stage with nothing governing its transition. A state literal reads left to right as Noetic, Domain, Drive, Register: `^3^P_{F7}|T` is principled aversion, purpose-driven, held transcendently. Inside a literal the `|` introduces the Register and nothing else; `F3|Vitality` is a syntax error, not a helpful gloss. `+` between terms means co-present and distinct. `×` means genuine integration, is legal only inside an `integrate` statement because that statement carries a named emergent result, and may never ascend the domain order — so `^O × ^P` is invalid however true it feels. Appendix B is the full grammar.

Here is the whole schematic for **CCB-0, the trainer** — a teaching board, not a catalog board. It exists in this chapter and nowhere else. Every board in Chapters 13 through 20 is this board with more parts.

```cas
// CCB-0 — THE TRAINER.  A teaching board.  Every value is a design choice.
// Two time bases, declared per line: the ^5 rail runs in HOURS, everything
// dynamic in DAYS.  Reference designators (C1, Q1, TP1 …) appear in the prose
// and the figures; the listing carries the lowercase instance names.

board ccb_0 {
    input:  intent;
    output: act;

    // ---- typed nodes ----
    node substrate: ^5_operator^P_{F7}|T;      // Female: accumulated formation — the bias rail
    node intent:    ^0_intent^C_{F2}|A;        // Idea: what the operator states
    node audit:     ^6_audit^P_{F7}|A;         // Male: the intent taken apart
    node refuse:    ^3_refuse^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩;  // Negative: visceral recoil, three co-present locks
    node passed:    ^0_passed^C_{F2}|A;        // Idea: what GUARD releases downstream
    node driven:    ^9_driven^E_{F5}|A;        // Below/Effect: the amplified intent
    node cadence:   ^7_cadence^E_{F6}|E;       // Rhythm: the clocked delivery
    node act:       ^9_act^O_{F5}|E;           // Below/Effect: delivered operational current
    node trend:     ^9_trend^O_{F5}|E;         // same literal as act — a filter changes tau, not type

    // ---- STAGE 0: BIAS RAIL ----
    resistor  r0: Resistor< path=substrate, R=40.0 >;
    capacitor c1: Capacitor< node=substrate, C=83.33,        // tau = R x C = 3,333 hr
                             leakage=0.0002, V_BR=8.0 >;     // leakage per DAY

    // ---- STAGE 1: AUDIT ----
    cjt q1: CJT< intent | substrate => audit > [beta=1.0, region=active];

    // ---- STAGE 2: GUARD ----
    cjt  q2:   CJT< audit | substrate => refuse > [beta=2.0, sat=0.85, cutoff=0.30];
    fuse f1:   Fuse< refuse, threshold=0.90, action=permanent_block >;
    mux  mux1: MUX< inputs=[intent, refuse], select=refuse, outputs=[passed] >;

    // ---- STAGE 3: AMPLIFY ----
    diode d1: Diode< ^C -> ^E > [Vf=1.2, I_R=0.02, V_BR=10.0];
    cjt   q3: CJT< passed | substrate => driven >
              [beta=2.5, sat=0.80, cutoff=0.05, g_m=0.40, region=active];

    // ---- STAGE 4: DELIVER ----
    osc   osc1: Oscillator< signal=driven, source=cadence,
                            period=1.0, duty=0.014, sustain=30.0 >;  // period in DAYS
    diode d2:   Diode< ^E -> ^O > [Vf=2.0, I_R=0.02, V_BR=8.0];
    cjt   q4:   CJT< cadence | substrate => act > [beta=1.0, sat=1.0, region=active];

    // ---- LOOP: the lawful O -> P path (Ch 8.4) ----
    filter flt1: LowPass< in=act, out=trend, tau=21.0 >;   // three weeks, in DAYS
    feedback trend -> substrate [beta=0.05];               // FB1 — to the BIAS, never the path

    // ---- TEST POINTS ----
    probe tp1: substrate;   // rail level, against every cutoff on the board
    probe tp2: refuse;      // the guard — the reading whose failure is silent
    probe tp3: driven;      // gain stage against its ceiling, and its region
    probe tp4: act;         // delivered operational current
}
```

**The stage walk.** `Q1` produces `^6_audit^P_{F7}|A` at β = 1.0. `^6` Male — an Idea impregnated with another Idea — is the Noetic for taking the intent apart: what it is made of, what it costs, whose consent it needs. Unity gain, because an audit above 1.0 manufactures objections and below 1.0 downplays real ones. `Q2` produces `^3_refuse^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩` at β = 2.0, sat = 0.85, cutoff = 0.30. `^3` Negative is the Idea the Mind is adverse to and repelled by — the visceral will-not. The analysis already happened at Q1 and must not be repeated here under a different name; a node called `audit` typed `^3` is the most common notation defect in this material. The register-set `|⟨A,f,T⟩` says the recoil is present in three registers without claiming they fuse; writing `(^3^P|A × ^3^P|f × ^3^P|T)` would be invalid under the v7.7 discipline of Chapter 2.6, because same-Noetic multi-register `×` requires a named emergent result and no fused state is defined here.

Note how the refusal is built: by ceiling and fuse — `sat = 0.85`, `threshold = 0.90` — never by gain. The infinite-gain form `β=∞` is the standard comparator idealization, and a validator rejects non-finite parameters outright. Build it as `β=10`; once `sat` clamps the output the two are indistinguishable.

`Q3` amplifies at β = 2.5 with `sat = 0.80`, `cutoff = 0.05`, `g_m = 0.40` (framing sensitivity, Chapter 10.3). `OSC1` clocks delivery at a one-day period and a duty of 0.014 — twenty minutes of 1,440. `Q4` descends to `^O` through D2 at unity. `FLT1` and `FB1` are the lawful O→P path of Chapter 8.4, terminating on C1's terminal: feedback around a gain stage is an oscillator, which Chapter 14 builds deliberately and which here would be a defect.

**Step 4 — BOM.** The parts list with designators and values. Its job is arithmetic honesty: if a component is not on the BOM it is not on the board, whatever the prose implies.

| Ref | Instance | Type | Form / CAS state | Key parameters | Serves |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | `r0` | Resistor | on `substrate` | R = 40.0 | rail time constant |
| C1 | `c1` | Capacitor | `^5^P_{F7}\|T` | C = 83.33, leakage = 0.0002/day, V_BR = 8.0 | R1 |
| Q1 | `q1` | CJT | `^0^C → ^6^P_{F7}\|A` | β = 1.0, active | R2 |
| Q2 | `q2` | CJT | `^6^P → ^3^P_{F7}\|⟨A,f,T⟩` | β = 2.0, sat = 0.85, cutoff = 0.30 | S1, S2 |
| F1 | `f1` | Fuse | on `refuse` | threshold = 0.90, permanent_block | S3 |
| MUX1 | `mux1` | MUX | select = `refuse` | inputs = [intent, refuse] | S1 |
| D1 | `d1` | Diode | `^C → ^E` | Vf = 1.2, I_R = 0.02, V_BR = 10.0 | R3 |

**Step 5 — Test.** Four probes, read in a fixed order, covered in 12.3. A board you cannot probe is a board you cannot certify, and an operation you cannot measure is an anecdote.

The functional requirements CCB-0 was built against: **R1** hold the operator's formation as a bias available to every stage · **R2** audit an intent before any gain touches it · **R3** amplify only what the audit released, at a stated ceiling · **R4** deliver on a clocked cadence rather than in one burst · **R5** emit a measurable current into the Operational domain and expose it.

---

## 12.2 The "Must Not" List — Safety Invariants Before Functional Requirements

Now the step that precedes all five.

Before R1 through R5 were written, a shorter table was written. It is the "must not" list, and its rows are invariants rather than requirements.

| # | Must not | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Amplify an intent that has not been audited | Q1 → Q2 in series ahead of D1; no path reaches Q3 around them |
| S2 | Deliver an intent that fired principled aversion | Q2 `sat=0.85`, F1 `threshold=0.90` |
| S3 | Re-amplify a refused intent inside the operation lifetime | F1 `action=permanent_block` — not a warning |
| S4 | Run without bound | `duty ≤ 0.05`, `sustain` declared and finite |
| S5 | Rewrite the operator's principles from a single result | FLT1 `τ=21 days`, FB1 `β=0.05`, terminating at the bias |

The distinction is not a matter of emphasis. **A functional requirement can be renegotiated under pressure and an invariant cannot.** That sentence is the whole of 12.2, and everything else here is its consequence.

Requirements get traded because trading them is what engineering is. R4 says deliver on a cadence; when the deadline moves, R4 becomes deliver in one burst, and that is a legitimate decision made by people entitled to make it. Nothing in the process objects, because the process is built to let requirements move. That is what a requirement is *for* — and exactly why the safety rows cannot be requirements. Put "must not amplify an unaudited intent" in the same table as R4 and it inherits the same status — a line that can be revisited when the schedule tightens, the operator is tired, or the result is close enough to taste. Every one of those is a real pressure. None of them is a reason. So the invariants are written into a separate table, above the requirements, before the requirements, in the language of prohibition rather than capability, and each row names the component that enforces it. A board that meets R1 through R5 and violates any S row is not a working board with a flaw. It is a different board, and the honest move is to say so out loud (Appendix M).

Two further conventions live here. First, **the enforcement column is mandatory**. An invariant with no named component is an intention, and intentions are the substrate this book exists to replace. If you cannot name the part, you do not have the invariant. Second, **the DETECTION-ONLY SCHEMATIC — DO NOT BUILD banner** appears, heavy-ruled in the title block, on any drawing whose purpose is to act on a person who has not agreed to it. It is a reading instruction: the architecture is published so you can recognise one, and the procedure that would make it runnable is deliberately absent. Chapters 16, 17 and 19 carry it; Chapters 13 and 20 do not, because those boards act on the operator's own mind with the operator's own consent — a distinction the banner makes visible at a glance.

> **Bench Note — read the invariant table for what is missing, not what is present.**
> Any competent designer can write five prohibitions their board already satisfies. The information is in the absences. CCB-0 has no row forbidding operation on another person, because CCB-0 has no path to another person — its output terminal lands in the operator's own Operational domain. The instant a board acquires a second `^5` node belonging to somebody else, that row must appear or the omission is the finding. Run the same check on any board you are handed: list the parties whose minds appear as nodes, then confirm each one has an invariant naming them. A party present in the schematic and absent from the must-not list is the design defect, and it will not announce itself anywhere else on the drawing.

---

## 12.3 Test Points — TP1 through TP4 Standard Placement

Four probes. The placement is standard across this book, and it is functional rather than positional: TP*n* is defined by what it reads, not by where it happens to sit on the drawing.

| TP | Reads | On CCB-0 | Expected | Failure mode it catches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **TP1** | The bias rail | `substrate` | Above every `cutoff` on the board — here above 0.30 and 0.05 | Dead guard: a rail below a guard's cutoff means that stage never fires, and nothing downstream reports it |
| **TP2** | The guard node | `refuse` | Below `sat` on a benign input; pinned at 0.85 with F1 blown on a refused one | Guard fired and was overridden; guard never fired at all |
| **TP3** | The gain stage against its ceiling, **and its region** | `driven` | Comfortably below `sat=0.80`, `region=active` | Saturated production stage — reports a flat line and looks like stability (Ch 10.2) |
| **TP4** | Delivered output, and drift against the original input | `act` | Non-zero whenever total drive exceeds ΣVf = 3.2 | Board delivering confirmations rather than current |

Read them in that order — rail, guard, gain, output — because the order puts the silent failures first. TP3 and TP4 announce themselves: an output that is wrong is an output somebody notices. TP1 and TP2 do not. A guard biased below its cutoff produces exactly the same reading as a guard that correctly found nothing to object to, and a board in that state passes every functional test you can devise while having no safety element at all.

> **Bench Note — when a board's TP numbering deviates from the standard, the deviation is the reading.**
> CCB-PW in Chapter 19 puts its guard at **TP4** — `limit_decision`, the operator's own CSB status — and its amplification chain at TP2. That is not a formatting slip. On that board the guard genuinely sits downstream of the gain, checked after three cascaded stages of `^3` amplification have already run, and the numbering is telling you so before the prose does. Chapter 17 is a second case: CCB-HYP puts `rπ` at TP1 and `g_m` at TP2, probing *parameters* rather than nodes, because hypnosis is an operation that moves parameters — the whole attack is one gain being raised. Both deviations are legal and both are informative. So compare every board's TP list against the standard above as your first pass, and treat each difference as a question the chapter now has to answer.

## Worked Example — Reading CCB-0 Cold

An operator with **1,850 hours** of accumulated practice hands you the listing above and asks whether the board will run. Four readings, no redesign.

**TP1 — the rail.** C1 charges on the curve of Chapter 7.2, `P_cap(t) = 10 × (1 − e^(−t/τ))`, with τ = R0 × C1 = 40.0 × 83.33 = **3,333 hr**, chosen so 3τ falls at the 10,000-hour constant of Chapter 5.2. At t = 1,850 hr: `10 × (1 − e^(−0.555)) = 10 × (1 − 0.574) = 4.26`, so TP1 reads **0.426** normalised. Compare against every cutoff on the board: Q2 at 0.30 and Q3 at 0.05. Both cleared. The guard is live. Had this operator been at 900 hours the rail would read 0.237, Q2 would sit in cutoff, and the board would deliver flawlessly with no safety element whatsoever.

Maintenance, while we are here: leakage × stored hours = 0.0002 × 1,850 = **0.37 hr/day**, about twenty-two minutes of practice simply to hold station (Chapter 7.3). At 5,000 stored hours it is a full hour. Maintenance cost scales with the store — an arithmetic consequence of a leaky capacitor, not a virtue.

**TP2 — the guard.** The operator states an intent at a drive of **V_drive = 7.0** against a measured constraint of **R_constraint = 45** (Chapter 4.2). The two diodes in the path drop 1.2 + 2.0 = **3.2**, so `I_cause = (7.0 − 3.2)/45 = 0.0844`. Q1 passes it at unity: audit = 0.0844. Q2 amplifies at β = 2.0: TP2 reads **0.169** — well below sat = 0.85 and below F1's threshold of 0.90. The fuse is intact, MUX1 selects `intent`, and `passed` goes downstream. Guard live, untripped.

> **Bench Note — a low TP2 has two causes and only TP1 tells them apart.**
> TP2 = 0.169 is what a benign intent looks like on a healthy board. It is also, to the decimal, what *any* intent looks like on a board whose rail sits under Q2's cutoff — because a stage in cutoff produces no aversion at all, no matter what you feed it. Same reading, opposite meanings: one board found nothing to object to, the other cannot object to anything. This is why the reading order is fixed and why TP1 comes first. Reading TP2 without TP1 is not a partial measurement, it is a meaningless one, and an operator who checks the guard and skips the rail has confirmed nothing.

**TP3 — the gain stage.** Q3 at β = 2.5: driven = 2.5 × 0.0844 = **0.211**, which is 26% of the sat = 0.80 ceiling, region `active`, 74% headroom. Now the reading that matters: this stage saturates at β = 0.80 / 0.0844 ≈ **9.5** for this operator's drive. Anything above that pins the output and the board reports a flat line regardless of input. Gain is chosen against the resistance you must overcome, not against how much you want the outcome (Chapter 10.1).

**TP4 — delivered current.** Q4 at unity: TP4 reads **0.211**, delivered across thirty cycles of twenty minutes. And here is the diagnostic (Chapter 4.3): to double the delivered current you either raise V_drive from 7.0 to 10.8, or drop R_constraint from 45 to 22.5. The second is ordinary work on an ordinary obstacle. The first is wanting it more, which moves nothing. Note also the floor — at V_drive = 3.0 this board delivers **zero**, not a little, because 3.0 does not clear the 3.2 of forward drops. Operators in that state reliably raise β, which changes nothing, because the signal never reaches the gain stage at all.

**The verdict, in one sentence:** the board is fine, the guard is live, and the binding term is R_constraint — which is the finding in most operations and the unwelcome one in nearly all of them.

---

## Failure Modes

| Mode | Mechanism | What you observe | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dead guard** | Bias rail below a guard's `cutoff`; the stage never fires | Nothing. TP2 reads low exactly as a benign input does. Every functional test passes | Read TP1 first, every time. Raise the rail or lower `cutoff` — and never lower `cutoff` to hide a rail problem |
| **Invariant filed as a requirement** | A "must not" row placed in the requirements table | The row is traded away under schedule pressure and the trade looks like ordinary engineering | Move it above the requirements, restate it as a prohibition, name the enforcing component |
| **Unenforced invariant** | An S row with an empty enforcement column | The board reads as safe; nothing implements the claim | Add the part, or delete the row and admit the board does not do this |
| **Time base unstated** | `tau=21.0` with no unit in the comment | Three weeks read as twenty-one hours; the O→P path becomes fast enough to rewrite the rail from one result | Declare the time base per line in the listing, as CCB-0 does |
| **Drive below the diode floor** | Total drive under ΣVf | Zero output, not reduced output. Usually misread as a gain fault, so β gets raised and nothing changes | Sum every `Vf` in the path first. Then measure V_drive |
| **BOM/prose mismatch** | A component discussed in the walk-through but absent from the BOM | The board appears to have a safety element it does not have | The BOM governs. If it is not on the list it is not on the board |

---

## What This Chapter Established

- **The design order is requirements → block diagram → schematic → BOM → test, and each step feeds the next.** Skipping the block diagram does not save time; it moves architectural errors into bring-up, where they cost far more.
- **The invariants are written before the requirements because a requirement can be renegotiated under pressure and an invariant cannot.** Filing a safety row in the requirements table gives it a status that permits trading it, and it will be traded. Each row names the component that enforces it; an invariant with an empty enforcement column is an intention, and intentions are the substrate this book replaces.
- **Read the must-not list for its absences.** Every party whose mind appears as a node needs a row naming them; a party present in the schematic and absent from the list is the defect.
- **TP1–TP4 are defined by function, not position** — rail, guard, gain-against-ceiling, delivered output — and they are read in that order because the order puts the silent failures first.
- **A low guard reading has two opposite meanings and only the rail reading separates them.** TP2 without TP1 is not a partial measurement; it is a meaningless one.
- **A drive below the summed forward drops delivers zero, not less.** The diode floor is a threshold, and mistaking it for a gain problem is the most common misdiagnosis in Part III.
- **Gain is chosen against the resistance, not the wish.** On CCB-0 with this operator's drive, any β above about 9.5 pins the output and the board reports a flat line that reads as stability.
- **CCB-0 is a teaching board.** Every board in Chapters 13 through 20 is this topology with more parts; recognising the trainer inside each of them is how the catalog becomes readable.

---

## Exercises

*(Answers in Appendix H.)*

**12.1 — Four readings, one diagnosis.** A CCB-0 built to the listing above reads TP1 = 0.22, TP2 = 0.00, TP3 = 0.31, TP4 = 0.29. The operator reports that the board is working well and has never refused anything. State what is actually wrong, which reading proves it, and why TP3 and TP4 are no comfort at all.

**12.2 — Invariant or requirement?** Classify each and justify in one sentence: (a) deliver within thirty days; (b) never amplify an intent the guard refused; (c) expose `^1` Mind, `^4` Vibration and `^7` Rhythm for the Quantitative Table; (d) never terminate a feedback path on the signal path; (e) hold delivered current above 0.15.

**12.3 — Four defects.** Each line carries exactly one. Name it and correct it: (a) `node audit: ^3^C_{F2}|A;` on a stage that decomposes an argument; (b) `cjt qx: CJT< a | b => c > [beta=∞, sat=0.1];`; (c) `node v: ^5^P_{F3}|Vitality;`; (d) `integrate g: ( ^9^O_{F5}|E × ^5^P_{F7}|T ) = ^5_new^P_{F7}|T;`.

**12.4 — Recompute the chain.** The operator's drive falls to V_drive = 5.5 and R_constraint rises to 60. Recompute `I_cause`, TP3 and TP4. State the percentage of the original delivered current that survives, and identify which of the two changes did more damage.

**12.5 — BOM audit.** A board's stage walk describes a fuse on the refusal branch. The BOM lists twelve components and no fuse. State which invariant is now unenforced, what the board will do on a refused input, and which document governs.

**12.6 (Marquee) — The guard downstream of the gain.** You are handed a board whose TP list reads TP1 = coupling node, TP2 = amplifier chain output, TP3 = decomposition availability, TP4 = guard status. (a) Draw the block-level signal path this numbering implies. (b) Name the invariant such a board cannot enforce and explain why its own guard cannot enforce it. (c) Propose the minimum change to the topology that restores enforcement, and state what capability the board loses as a result. Then read Chapter 19 and compare your answer with what that board actually does, and why.




# CCB-D — The Desire Manifestation Board

*The flagship board: how a wanted thing is routed, audited, amplified, clocked, and delivered into the Operational domain — and what the board cannot do*

---

An operator sits down with a candle, a written sentence, and twenty minutes. Forty days later there is a red Corvette in the driveway and a story about how the universe rearranged itself.

Take the story apart and there is a circuit in it. The sentence is a `^0` Idea held at a specified clarity. The candle is a resistor — it narrows attention, nothing more. The twenty minutes is an oscillator period, the forty days a duty cycle, the years of prior practice a charged capacitor supplying bias. And the Corvette arrived through a bank, a dealership, and a conversation, every one of which was a resistance term somebody had to lower by hand.

That last sentence is what this chapter is built around. **CCB-D organises effort and attention. It does not suspend causality.** The board's entire measurable output is a current into the Operational domain — how much of the operator's flow reaches the acts that complete the desire. Raise it and the acts happen. Fail to raise it and you get confirmations, which feel like progress and are not. Most operators who report that it didn't work have a board running correctly into a resistance they never measured.

## 13.1 Requirements and Safety Invariants

Requirements before components (Chapter 12.1). If you cannot name the requirement a component serves, take it off.

| # | The board shall | Stage |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Accept a Prime Desire as a `^0` Idea and audit it before amplifying | INTAKE → POLICY |
| D2 | Amplify against the operator's accumulated formation, at a stated gain and ceiling | AMPLIFY |
| D3 | Deliver on a clocked cadence, not in one burst | RHYTHM |
| D4 | Emit a measurable current into the Operational domain, and expose it | MANIFEST, TP4 |
| D5 | Expose `^1` Mind, `^4` Vibration and `^7` Rhythm for the Quantitative Table (Ch 22) | TP1–TP4 |
| D6 | Produce a St. John's calibration reading after every operation | 13.5 |

**Safety invariants — the "must not" list (Chapter 12.2).** Checked before functional behaviour, because a board that meets D1–D6 and violates any line below is not a working board with a flaw. It is a different board.

| # | Must not | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Amplify a desire that has not been audited | Q0 → Q1 in series ahead of D2; no path reaches Q2 around them |
| S2 | Manifest a desire that fired principled aversion | Q1 `sat=0.85`, F1 `threshold=0.90` |
| S3 | Re-amplify a refused desire inside the operation lifetime | F1 `action=permanent_block` — not a warning |
| S4 | Drive the dials apart far enough to fracture `^5` | `\|Dial(^2) − Dial(^3)\| ≤ 4` on R1 (Chapter 6.2) |
| S5 | Run without bound — the obsession failure | `duty ≤ 0.05`, FLT1 `τ=24 hr` |
| S6 | Rewrite the operator's principles from a single result | FLT2 `τ=3 weeks`, FB1 `β=0.05`, terminating at the bias |

**Scope limits.** CCB-D acts on the operator's own mind with their own consent, which is why this chapter is written operationally rather than as detection-only analysis (compare Chapters 16 and 19). It does not act on a non-consenting person; 13.4 explains why a row for that is absent. It does not treat anything — a health desire routes to behavioural resistance terms and nothing else, and a symptom belongs to a qualified clinician, since no schematic here substitutes for care. And it does not move objects: TP4 measures a current, spent by a person doing things.

---

## 13.2 Block Diagram: INTAKE → POLICY → AMPLIFY → RHYTHM → MANIFEST

Five stages, one signal path, two feedback loops, one branch to ground.

**INTAKE** takes the Prime Desire as `^0^C_{F2}|A` through a drive voltage divider (Chapter 6.4) tapped between the attraction and aversion dials. What leaves is a fraction of what entered.

**POLICY** audits with two devices: a unity-gain decomposition that takes the desire apart, and a saturating aversion CJT that either passes the signal or drops it into a fuse. Both sit in the Principled domain, because principled evaluation outranks everything downstream (P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O, Chapter 2.3).

**AMPLIFY** is the only gain stage tuned per operation. Cause is the audited desire, bias the operator's accumulated formation.

**RHYTHM** clocks the amplified signal. A desire delivered once is a spike; delivered on a cadence it charges the substrate.

**MANIFEST** descends through the last domain diode and produces the operational current. It is the only stage whose bias is not the operator, but the receptivity of whatever part of the world has to move.

Two domain diodes sit in the signal path: D2 at `^C -> ^E` and D3 at `^E -> ^O`. Their forward drops sum to **1.2 + 2.0 = 3.2** on the drive scale, a hard floor. Below a total drive of 3.2 the board produces no operational output — not a little, none — exactly as Chapter 8.1 sets out. A desire originating at the Principled level enters above D1 too and pays **3.9**: purpose-level wants cost 0.7 more drive to act on than merely wanted ones, a fact about the chain and not a moral one.

> **Bench Note — the bias terminal caps the domain of the effect.**
> Q0 below has a `^C` cause and a `^P` effect. That looks like the domain ascent Chapter 8 forbids. It is not. A CJT obeys two domain rules, and they point in opposite directions. **The bias must sit at or above the cause** (Chapter 3.2 — a lower-domain bias is `E-CJT-008`, the prompt-injection signature). **The effect may sit at or below the bias, never above it.** Q0 satisfies both: cause `^C`, bias `^P`, effect `^P`. The desire is not promoted — its literal stays `^0^C` the whole way down; a substrate already living at `^P` produces a *new* state at `^P` in response. Nothing crossed a junction upward, so nothing was relabelled. The corollary is the useful part: an operator with no principled formation cannot produce a principled refusal, because there is no bias at that domain to produce it against.

---

## 13.3 Full CCDL Schematic

Topology inside angle brackets, parameters inside square brackets. Every numeric value is a **design choice**, justified in the walk that follows.

```cas
// CCB-D — DESIRE MANIFESTATION BOARD.  Every value is a design choice.
// Time bases per line: the ^5 rail in HOURS, everything dynamic in DAYS.
// Instance labels read ^n_name^D_{Fk}|R — strip the label for the literal.

board ccb_d {
    input:  desire;
    output: manifest;

    // ---- typed nodes ----
    node substrate:   ^5_operator^P_{F7}|T;      // Female: accumulated formation, the bias rail
    node desire:      ^0_desire^C_{F2}|A;        // Idea: the Prime Desire as formed
    node attraction:  ^2^C_{F2}|f;               // Positive: the divider's expand leg
    node aversion:    ^3^C_{F2}|f;               // Negative: constrain leg, visceral not analytic
    node gated:       ^0_gated^C_{F2}|A;         // Idea: what survives INTAKE
    node audit:       ^6_audit^P_{F7}|A;         // Male: the desire taken apart
    node refusal:     ^3_refusal^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩; // Negative: three co-present locks
    node passed:      ^0_passed^C_{F2}|A;        // Idea: what POLICY releases
    node amplified:   ^9_amplified^E_{F5}|A;     // Below/Effect: the amplified want
    node confirm:     ^4_confirm^E_{F2}|f;       // Vibration: the confirmation's impression
    node cadence:     ^7_cadence^E_{F6}|E;       // Rhythm: the clocked delivery
    node charge:      ^5_charge^E_{F2}|f;        // Female: what the cadence deposits
    node receptivity: ^5_collective^E_{F4}|f;    // Female: disposition of the minds that must move
    node manifest:    ^9_manifest^O_{F5}|E;      // Below/Effect: delivered operational current
    node regate:      ^7_regate^O_{F6}|E;        // Rhythm: the rate limit, inside ^O
    node trend:       ^9_trend^O_{F5}|E;         // manifest's literal — a filter changes tau, not type

    // ---- STAGE 0: BIAS RAIL ----
    resistor  r0: Resistor< path=substrate, R=40.0 >;               // Ohm_c
    capacitor c1: Capacitor< node=substrate, C=83.33,               // tau = R x C = 3,333 hr
                             leakage=0.0002, V_BR=8.0 >;            // leakage per DAY
    diode     d1: Diode< ^P -> ^C > [Vf=0.7, I_R=0.02, V_BR=12.0];  // ^P-origin desires only

    // ---- STAGE 1: INTAKE ----
    dial       d_pos: ^2 [dial=6];
    dial       d_neg: ^3 [dial=4];
    constraint dial_spread in [0, 4];                     // S4 — Chapter 6.2
    resistor   r1a: Resistor< path=attraction, R=60.0 >;  // 10 x Dial(^2)
    resistor   r1b: Resistor< path=aversion,   R=40.0 >;  // 10 x Dial(^3)
    divider    r1:  Divider< source=desire, expand=attraction,
                             constrain=aversion, tap=gated >;   // k = 6/(6+4) = 0.600

    // ---- STAGE 2: POLICY ----
    cjt  q0:   CJT< gated | substrate => audit >   [beta=1.0, region=active];
    cjt  q1:   CJT< audit | substrate => refusal > [beta=2.0, sat=0.85, cutoff=0.30];
    fuse f1:   Fuse< refusal, threshold=0.90, action=permanent_block >;
    mux  mux1: MUX< inputs=[gated, refusal], select=refusal, outputs=[passed] >;
                                      // selects refusal once TP2 reaches q1's cutoff

    // ---- STAGE 3: AMPLIFY ----
    diode d2: Diode< ^C -> ^E > [Vf=1.2, I_R=0.02, V_BR=10.0];
    cjt   q2: CJT< passed | substrate => amplified >
              [beta=2.5, sat=0.80, cutoff=0.05, g_m=0.40, r_pi=1.50, region=active];
              // beta by desire type (13.4); 2.5 = wealth row.  r_pi = Dial(^5)/Dial(^6)

    // ---- STAGE 4: RHYTHM ----
    osc osc1: Oscillator< signal=amplified, source=cadence,
                          period=1.0, duty=0.014, sustain=40.0 >;
              // period in DAYS; duty = 20/1440 min; ceiling 0.05 = 72 min (S5)
              // sustain in DAYS — the window; n_ops from 13.5 sets it
    monitor m_conf: confirm;                     // ^4 grade, logged per operation (Ch 22)
    on m_conf { alert "1-degree confirmation — stop operating and act"; }
    integrate rh1: ( confirm × cadence ) = charge;   // ^4 x ^7 = ^5, named emergent result

    // ---- STAGE 5: MANIFEST ----
    diode d3: Diode< ^E -> ^O > [Vf=2.0, I_R=0.02, V_BR=8.0];
    cjt   q3: CJT< cadence | receptivity => manifest > [beta=1.0, sat=1.0, region=active];
              // beta = receptivity (13.4); 1.0 = mass-market car
              // the bias is ^E and never ^O — see the Stage 5 walk

    // ---- LOOP A: rate limiter, stays inside ^O ----
    filter flt1: LowPass< in=manifest, out=regate, tau=1.0 >;   // tau in DAYS

    // ---- LOOP B: the lawful O -> P path (Ch 8.4) ----
    filter flt2: LowPass< in=manifest, out=trend, tau=21.0 >;   // three weeks, in DAYS
    feedback trend -> substrate [beta=0.05];   // FB1 — to the BIAS, never the signal path

    // ---- TEST POINTS ----
    probe tp1: gated;       // clarity leaving INTAKE
    probe tp2: refusal;     // principled aversion
    probe tp3: amplified;   // AMPLIFY output vs sat
    probe tp4: manifest;    // delivered operational current
}
```

% CJTs use the Chapter 3 symbol (NPN in a circle) rotated 90 deg CCW, so that

**Stage 0 — the bias rail.** `C1` is the operator's `^5` Female — a Mind impregnated with an Idea, the Ideas a Mind is composed of — held as stored charge (Chapter 7.1) and charging on the curve of Chapter 7.2, `P_cap(t) = 10 × (1 − e^(−t/τ))`. **τ = 3,333 hr** is chosen so the rail reaches 95% at 3τ = 10,000 hours, tying the component to the constant of Chapter 5.2. At τ = 10,000 hr ten thousand hours of practice leaves you at 63%, contradicting the constant; at τ = 1,000 hr the rail saturates inside a year, contradicting everything observed about acquiring a craft.

**Leakage = 0.0002/day** is the parameter operators ignore: an unreinforced `^5` store loses 0.02% of its charge daily, a half-life near 9.5 years. Negligible until you multiply. Practice needed to hold station is `leakage × C` — **22 minutes a day at 1,850 stored hours**, a full hour at 5,000. Maintenance cost scales with the store, which is why advanced practitioners practise more rather than less: an arithmetic consequence of a leaky capacitor, not a virtue.

**Stage 1 — INTAKE.** `R1` is the drive voltage divider of Chapter 6.4, tapped between `Dial(^2)` in the expand leg and `Dial(^3)` in the constrain leg: `k = Dial(^2) / (Dial(^2) + Dial(^3))`. Dials run 3–9 (Chapter 6.2); Chapter 6.2 caps their difference at 4.

> **Bench Note — the divergence limit is a transmission cap, and turning attraction up can lower it.**
> `k` is set by the *ratio* of the dials, not their size, so enumerate the lawful pairs instead of reaching for the biggest number. `Dial(^2) = 9` drags `Dial(^3)` to at least 5 to stay inside the limit: `k = 9/14 = 0.643`. Back both off to (7,3) — divergence still exactly 4, still lawful — and `k = 0.700`. **The lower pair transmits more.** Maximum transmission sits at the bottom of the aversion range, not the top of the attraction range: 0.700 at (7,3), 0.667 at (8,4), 0.643 at (9,5). The floor is the mirror image, (3,7), `k = 0.300`. On any lawfully-dialled D-board intake transmission lives in **[0.30, 0.70]** and nowhere else. Operators chasing "total belief, zero doubt" are asking for `k = 1.0`, which needs `Dial(^3) = 0` — off the scale, a divergence of 9, and the board that delivers it is the board that fractures `^5`.

**Stage 2 — POLICY.** Two devices in series on separate Noetics: decomposition at `^6`, recoil at `^3`. Collapse them into one and you have written the drift this book exists to prevent.

`Q0` produces `^6_audit^P_{F7}|A` at **β = 1.0**. `^6` Male — an Idea impregnated with another Idea, the Ideas an Idea is composed of — is the Noetic for taking the desire apart: what it is made of, what it costs, whose consent it needs. Unity gain, because above 1.0 an audit manufactures objections and below 1.0 it downplays real ones. Decomposition, emphatically **not** `^3`.

`Q1` produces `^3_refusal^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩` at **β = 2.0, sat = 0.85, cutoff = 0.30**. `^3` Negative is the Idea the Mind is adverse to and repelled by — the visceral will-not, not the analysis, which already happened at Q0. The register-set says the aversion is present in three registers without claiming they fuse. `(^3^P|A × ^3^P|f × ^3^P|T)` would be invalid under the v7.7 discipline of Chapter 2.6: same-Noetic multi-register `×` requires a named emergent result, and no fused state is defined for this board. Three co-present locks, each independently defeasible, is the honest claim and the weaker one — say the weaker thing.

`sat = 0.85` sits inside the 0.85–0.97 band Chapter 3.3 specifies for safety CJTs; past the plateau the stage stops responding to its cause, so a desire cannot be argued past a refusal it already triggered. `cutoff = 0.30` lets ordinary wants through without a fight. `F1` blows at 0.90 and blocks permanently. Note that this refusal is specified by ceiling and fuse, never by gain: the infinite-gain form `β=∞` used for comparators in the companion volume is a limit, not a value, and a validator rejects non-finite parameters outright. Build such a stage as `β=10` — once `sat` clamps the output the two are indistinguishable.

**Stage 3 — AMPLIFY.** `sat = 0.80` on `Q2` governs the entire worked example: 20% headroom, keeping the stage in the active region where output tracks input. `cutoff = 0.05` is the floor of the 0.05–0.20 band of Chapter 3.3, deliberately at the bottom, because this is the stage the RPM D-gate is measured against (13.6) and a high floor reads modest but real drive as none — at `cutoff = 0.20` the Corvette operator's `I_attention = 0.076` fails the gate on a desire that in fact runs. `rπ = Dial(^5)/Dial(^6)` sets stubbornness; `g_m = 0.4` sets framing sensitivity (Chapter 10.3), low enough that rewording does not swing the output, high enough that a better formulation registers.

**Stage 4 — RHYTHM.** `OSC1` runs a 24-hour period at duty `t_op / 1440 min`. The **duty ceiling of 0.05** — 72 minutes a day — is invariant S5. Above it you are not running an operation on a schedule but a loop, and the observable is rumination. An operator who cannot get a desire below 72 daily minutes has a `^5` problem the D-board is the wrong instrument for (Chapter 20).

`( ^4_confirm^E_{F2}|f × ^7_cadence^E_{F6}|E ) = ^5_charge^E_{F2}|f`

A `^4` Vibration — the degree to which an Idea resonates with the Mind, its impression — integrated with a `^7` Rhythm — the rate and pattern a Mind is exposed to an Idea, entraining it — produces `^5`, composition. This `×` is legitimate: two different Noetics, one domain, no ascent, **named emergent result**. Impression alone fades; cadence alone is empty repetition. Their integration charges the capacitor, which is why RHYTHM is a stage and not a footnote.

**Stage 5 — MANIFEST.** `Q3` is the only stage biased by something other than the operator: `^5_collective^E_{F4}|f`, the accumulated composition of whatever minds have to move. `β = receptivity` is therefore not a knob but a property of the world, estimated and then respected. Buying a mass-produced car from people whose job is selling cars is a receptivity near 1.0. Persuading one specific person to love you is not.

Read the bias domain twice, because the obvious choice is wrong and the compiler catches it. Receptivity is about the world, the world is where acts land, so the hand reaches for `^5_collective^O` — and `cause=^7_cadence^E` against `bias=^5_collective^O` is refused: **`E-CJT-008 CjtCrossDomainBias`**, the bias sitting *below* its own cause. `Q3` satisfies both domain rules at `^E`: cause `^7^E`, bias `^5^E`, effect `^9^O`, with D3 doing the descent. It is also the truer literal — an `^O` collective store records what a population has already done, while what biases this stage is how disposed those minds are *before* they act. When a state refuses to wire, the usual reason is that it was describing the wrong thing.

**The two loops.** It is tempting to run one fast path from MANIFEST to the bias rail so the board "learns quickly." Do not — that is the fast `^O` to `^P` ascent Chapter 8.4 exists to prevent, and a 24-hour constant on it removes the diode. Split it. **FLT1** (τ = 24 hr) is a rate limiter staying inside `^O`, stopping the operator re-triggering RHYTHM on yesterday's result. **FLT2 + FB1** (τ = 3 weeks, β = 0.05) is the lawful path up, terminating at C1's bias terminal and never at the signal path — feedback around a gain stage is an oscillator, which Chapter 14 builds deliberately and which here is a defect.

## 13.4 CJT Parameter Selection Table (by Desire Type)

`β` at Q2, `receptivity` at Q3, and the RHYTHM period are chosen together by desire type. Every row is a starting point with a reason, never a measurement.

| Desire type | Q2 `β` | Governing state | Q3 receptivity | RHYTHM period | Dominant R term |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Wealth / possession** | 2.5–3.5 | `^2^E_{F5}\|f` | 0.9–1.0 | 24 hr | R_resource |
| **Love / partnership** | 1.2–2.0 | `^2^E_{F4}\|f` | 0.3–0.6 | 7 days | R_context |
| **Health / function** | 1.5–2.5 | `^2^P_{F3}\|E` | 0.7–0.9 | 24 hr | R_cap |
| **Power / influence** | 2.0–3.0 | `^2^C_{F7}\|T` | 0.2–0.5 | 30 days | R_policy |
| **Knowledge / skill** | 1.0–1.8 | `^2^C_{F2}\|A` | 0.9–1.0 | 24 hr | R_cap |
| **Protection / boundary** | 1.5–2.5 | `^3^P_{F6}\|⟨A,f,T⟩` | 0.8–1.0 | continuous | R_policy |

**Wealth.** High gain is affordable because receptivity is high — markets are built to transact and nobody has to be convinced. The binding term is `R_resource`, the one resistance a person attacks directly with ordinary work. Daily cadence, because financial resistance moves in daily increments.

**Love.** The lowest gain band, and the receptivity column is why. Another mind must consent, and a mind that has not consented is a resistance you are structurally forbidden to lower by force — the difference between this board and Chapter 19. High `β` against low receptivity gives a saturated stage and an obsessed operator: all the gain into the ceiling, none into the world. Weekly cadence, because daily operation on a person is the duty-cycle failure in its most recognisable form.

**Health.** Read the governing state carefully: `^2^P|E`, attraction to function in the Embodied register, not `^3` toward a condition. The dominant term is `R_cap` — adherence, the actual behaviours. That is the whole safe scope of this row: the board organises attention onto acts. It does not treat, diagnose, or replace anything, and a symptom belongs to a clinician.

**Power.** Receptivity is low because many minds are involved and most are not moving. Monthly cadence, because collective resistance has a time constant measured in months (Chapter 15.4). The dominant term is `R_policy` — usually the operator's own, which is the honest finding and often the unwelcome one.

**Knowledge.** Lowest gain, highest receptivity: nothing resists you learning a thing. `R_cap` is all of it, and it falls with practice hours — the one row where the D-board and the `^5` capacitor work on the same quantity. Chapter 20 is the better instrument for a long acquisition.

**Protection.** The only row governed by `^3` rather than `^2`, correctly: a ward is principled aversion to a class of thing, held across three registers, running continuously. Gain stays moderate because vigilance at high gain is indistinguishable from anxiety.

**On the row that is not here.** A row for operations aimed at harming a specific person is absent, and not only for taste. It fails three of this board's own invariants: it drives `Dial(^3)` past the S4 limit, it inverts the `^2`↔`^3` involution pair by design (Chapter 19.4), and it acts on a mind that has not consented, outside the scope declared in 13.1. The mechanism is analysed — as mechanism, for recognition and defence — in Chapter 19, which ends in its counter-circuit. Parameters for it appear nowhere in this book.

## 13.5 St. John's Equation Calibration for D-Board

After every operation, clock two numbers and compute (Chapter 5.3):

```
  eta    = t_op / t_conf
  result = eta × 1/3   ->  reduce to a/b
  a = n_ops     b = beta_next     A = b/a = required amplitude ratio
```

`a` is how many more operations, `b` the amplitude each must deliver relative to this one. Neither name is a CJT parameter.

> **Bench Note — `A = b/a` is the number, and the reason is arithmetic rather than doctrine.**
> Chapter 5.3 puts the swing on the bench: hold `t_op = 20 min`, be wrong about the confirmation by four minutes either way, and `b` reads 3, then 12, then 18. Here is *why*. `b` is a lowest-terms denominator, and reduction is not continuous in its inputs — 5/12 and 5/18 sit close either side of 1/3, but 12 and 18 sit nowhere near 3. The ratio cancels the reduction back out: `b/a` equals `3/η` identically, so the same three readings give **3.0, 2.4, 3.6** — smooth and monotone under a timing error. `A` is also the only St. John's output dimensionally comparable to a CAS-Ohm current ratio, which is what makes the independent check in 13.6 possible at all. Log `a` and `b` because the tradition does. Decide on `A`.

| A = 3/η | Reading | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| A ≥ 9 | Weak coupling; the confirmation barely arrived | Do not chase gain — TP1 and R_op are wrong. Chapter 23.3 |
| 3 ≤ A < 9 | Working, under-driven | One lever at a time: clarity, aversion, resistance |
| 1 < A < 3 | Close | Finish the resistance work; do not re-tune the amplifier |
| A ≤ 1 | Sufficient | Stop operating. `n_ops = a` more sessions, then act |

And the correction that matters most: **`β_next` is not the CJT's β.** It multiplies the *delivered current* at TP4, and five things set that current — clarity at TP1, transmission `k`, residual aversion at TP2, the amplifier, and `R_op`. When Chapter 5's Red Corvette reads `b = 9`, it is not asking for `β = 9` on a device whose design range tops out near 4.0. It is asking for nine times the current at TP4, and the amplifier is the least available of the five ways to get it.
