```{=latex}
  {$R(I)\ne R(I)'$};
\node[note,anchor=north west,align=left,text width=43mm] at (7.05,-2.72)
  {$+$ the cast happened\\
   $+$ the operator knows what it felt like\\
   $+$ the log has a row};
\node[note,anchor=west,text=casEedge] at (0.15,-3.38)
  {no arrow $R(I)'\to R(I)$ exists};

\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{Commutative diagram}
\label{fig:21-C}
\end{figure}
```


**The left identity is what makes the gate cheap.** Descend into any prerequisite, find it lacking, come back up with the target unchanged and nothing consumed. That licenses running the whole gate, failing at A0, re-wording, and running it again from the top — which the worked example does. Scanning is lossless. There is no such thing as spending a desire by inspecting it, and the operator who won't run the gate because "looking too hard will kill it" is describing a property the mathematics does not have.

**The right non-identity is what you cannot get around.** Once the cast has fired, re-embedding the resulting state does not hand back the configuration you came from. No inverse arrow, therefore no `undo` component to draw — and **CCDL has no `undo` statement, which is a design claim, not an oversight** (App. B, §B.2.1: look for it; it is not there). Three consequences follow:

1. **An un-cast would be an unlawful ascent.** Reversing a cast requires the Operational outcome to reach back and rewrite the Principled prerequisite that authorized it: `^O × ^P`, invalid notation for the same reason it is invalid engineering (Ch. 8.3). The one lawful upward path here is the filtered O→P feedback, τ = 21 days at β = 0.15. It *updates* the substrate; it does not *restore* it.
2. **Infinite gain does not manufacture an inverse.** `β=∞` is the standard idealization for a hard switch, used in exactly that sense on the CSB's red path (Ch. 24) with the note that a validator rejects non-finite parameters and a real build writes a large finite number. Here the objection is deeper than range-checking: the reverse arrow does not exist *at any gain*, so no finite substitute exists either. A large β on a reverse path specifies a component that is not merely unbuildable but undefined.
3. **A second reading of a gate is not comparable to the first.** This is the checkable face of `η ∘ ε ≠ id`. After firing, the A0 readings cannot be re-taken clean, because one of the three ratings is now contaminated by knowing what the cast felt like. The prerequisite space you re-enter is a different space.

Now the discipline, because this result is over-read more often than it is used. **Section-retraction does not imply:**

- **That the outcome is guaranteed.** Irreversible is not effective. The gate authorizes; it delivers nothing. A cast that produced no confirmation at all still cannot be un-cast.
- **That consequences are permanent.** You may cast a counter-operation — a *new* target with its own full RPM gate, cost, and risk, not an inverse. What is unavailable is making the first cast not have happened.
- **That satisfied prerequisites stay satisfied.** They decay: charge leaks (Ch. 7.3), rails sag, schedules lapse.
- **Anything moral.** The asymmetry is structural. It says nothing about whether the cast should have been made, and a reader who hears a warning in it is hearing their own.

> **Bench Note — decay is not inversion, and confusing them produces a superstition.** A prerequisite can *become* unsatisfied by attrition: stop practising and the `^5` rail drops, stop clarifying and `R_context` climbs back. What cannot happen is a prerequisite being *un-satisfied by an operation designed to reverse it*. The signatures differ — attrition is slow, monotone, visible in the log as a drifting rail; reversal is unavailable at any speed. The operator who conflates them concludes that neglecting a working takes it back. It does not. It loses them the capacity to run the next one, while the first one stands.

## The Full CCDL Listing — CCB-RPM

```cas
board ccb_rpm {                          // CCB-RPM — the prerequisite gate
    input:  stated_desire;               // as the operator first words it
    output: authorization;               // ARM or HOLD — never a cast
    node practice_rail: ^5^P_{F7}|T;     // Female: accumulated practice — bias only

    // ---- S1  A0 AUTHENTICATION ----
    node stated: ^0_stated^C_{F2}|A;      node parts:           ^6^C_{F6}|A;
    node pull_open:      ^2^E_{F5}|f;     node pull_private:    ^2^E_{F5}|f;
    node pull_condition: ^2^E_{F5}|f;     node witness_load:    ^2^E_{F4}|f;
    node object_premium: ^4^E_{F5}|A;     node a0_ok:           ^2^E_{F7}|T;
    cjt q_dec:  CJT< stated | practice_rail => parts >          [β=1.0];
    cjt q_open: CJT< parts  | practice_rail => pull_open >      [β=1.0];
    cjt q_priv: CJT< parts  | practice_rail => pull_private >   [β=1.0];
    cjt q_cond: CJT< parts  | practice_rail => pull_condition > [β=1.0];
    diff d_witness: Differential< plus=pull_open, minus=pull_private,
                                  out=witness_load >;
    diff d_premium: Differential< plus=pull_open, minus=pull_condition,
                                  out=object_premium >;
    fuse    f_witness: Fuse< path=witness_load, threshold=0.30,
                             action=block_until_decomposed >;
    monitor m_proxy:   Monitor< signal=object_premium, limit=[0.20, 1.00],
                                action_on_violation=PROXY_TARGET >;
    cjt q_a0: CJT< witness_load | practice_rail => a0_ok > [β=1.0, cutoff=0.05];

    // ---- S2  D-GATE ----
    rail F5: Agency [v=7];                rail F2: Wisdom [v=6];
    node path_in: ^1^C_{F5}|A;            node d_ok: ^4^E_{F5}|A;
    diode d2: Diode< ^C -> ^E > [Vf=1.2]; diode d3: Diode< ^E -> ^O > [Vf=2.0];
    resistor r_cap:      Resistor< path=path_in, R=25 >;
    resistor r_policy:   Resistor< path=path_in, R=0  >;
    resistor r_context:  Resistor< path=path_in, R=30 >;
    resistor r_resource: Resistor< path=path_in, R=20 >;
    monitor m_drive: Monitor< signal=path_in, limit=[0.10, 1.00],
                              action_on_violation=D_GATE_HOLD >;
    cjt q_d: CJT< path_in | practice_rail => d_ok > [β=1.0, cutoff=0.05];

    // ---- S3  W-GATE ----
    node idea:    ^0^C_{F2}|A;   node w_sched: ^6^C_{F6}|A;
    node w_board: ^1^C_{F2}|A;   node w_param: ^6^C_{F6}|A;
    node w_calib: ^4^E_{F2}|A;   node w_sheet: ^7^O_{F6}|E;
    node w_ok:    ^6^E_{F6}|A;
    monitor m_idea: Monitor< signal=idea, limit=[0.60, 1.00],
                             action_on_violation=IDEA_UNFORMED >;
    gate g_w: AND< idea, w_sched, w_board, w_param, w_calib, w_sheet >;
    cjt q_w: CJT< g_w | practice_rail => w_ok > [β=1.0];

    // ---- S4  P-GATE ----
    node p_gnosis: ^1^C_{F1}|T;  node p_load:   ^7^C_{F6}|A;
    node p_access: ^5^E_{F4}|f;  node p_recoil: ^3^E_{F7}|f;
    node p_ok:     ^7^E_{F3}|E;
    monitor m_budget: Monitor< signal=p_load,   limit=[0.00, 0.50],
                               action_on_violation=OVERCOMMIT >;
    monitor m_absorb: Monitor< signal=p_recoil, limit=[0.00, 0.25],
                               action_on_violation=ARRIVAL_AVERSION >;
    gate g_p: AND< p_gnosis, p_load, p_access, p_recoil >;
    cjt q_p: CJT< g_p | practice_rail => p_ok > [β=1.0];

    // ---- S5  ARM / HOLD ----
    gate g_ready: AND< w_ok, p_ok >;      gate g_arm: AND< a0_ok, d_ok, g_ready >;
    node arm:  ^9^O_{F5}|E;               node hold: ^9^E_{F6}|A;
    diode d_out: Diode< ^E -> ^O > [Vf=2.0];
    mux out: MUX< inputs=[hold, arm], select=g_arm >;

    // ---- S6  LEDGER: the lawful ascent, and the only one ----
    filter f_log: LowPass< in=arm, out=trend, tau=21.0 >;   // days
    feedback trend -> practice_rail [β=0.15];

    probe tp1: witness_load;   probe tp2: path_in;
    probe tp3: g_ready;        probe tp4: out;
}
```

**S1.** All three pull probes and both differentials sit at `^E` deliberately. What the bench reads is the operator's *evaluation* of their own pull, not the world-level fact of who is watching, and modelling it at `^E` keeps an unlawful `^O → ^E` ascent out of the listing — the move Chapter 23's intake makes at `^C`. The bench samples; it does not drive. `block_until_decomposed` names the only lawful path past F1: re-word, then re-run from the top.

**S2.** The resistor values are this operator's, on this desire, today — inputs, not constants of the board. The diodes carry the descent drop explicitly rather than folding it into `R`, because an operator who cannot see the 3.2 `V_c` will not subtract it.

**S3–S4.** `AND` and only `AND` (S1). Two P-gate inputs are monitored ceilings rather than possessions — `p_load` and `p_recoil` enter as pass/fail from their monitors, which is why the monitors carry the numbers and the gate carries none.

**S5–S6.** `g_arm` is the last reversible point on the board; the diode past the MUX is the descent into the cast and has no counterpart pointing back. The ledger is the one lawful ascent — `arm` at `^O` reaching `practice_rail` at `^P` — legal only because it is filtered at τ = 21 days and held at β = 0.15, inside the 0.05–0.3 band Part III uses for every feedback path (Ch. 8.4).

## Parameter and BOM Table

Every value is a design choice made in this book, not a measurement.

| Ref | Component | Setting | Why | Failure at other values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Witness fuse | 0.30, `block_until_decomposed` | A third of the pull is where the audience sets the amplitude | 0.50: audience-carried desires pass. 0.10: operator stops logging honestly |
| M1 | Proxy monitor | premium ≥ 0.20 | Smallest gap surviving self-rating noise | Lower: proxies read as prime. Higher: real targets held undecided |
| Q1–Q8 | Verdict CJTs | β = 1.0 | **A gate that amplifies is not a gate** (S2) | β > 1 manufactures readiness; β < 1 hides drive that is really there |
| — | CJT `cutoff` | 0.05 | Bottom of the 0.05–0.20 band (Ch. 3.3), matching Ch. 13's AMPLIFY floor | 0.20: modest but real drive reads as no drive |
| D2, D3, D_out | Descent diodes | Vf 1.2, 2.0 | Chapter 8.2 drops, carried explicitly | Folded into `R`: margin overstated ~2× |
| R1–R4 | Constraint stack | 25 / 0 / 30 / 20 `Ω_c` | This operator, this desire (Ch. 4.4 ranges) | Treated as board constants: the gate stops reading the operator |
| M2 | Drive monitor | `I` ≥ 0.10 = 2 × cutoff | One bad day must not drop the stage into cutoff | 1.0×: fires today, not across a campaign |
| G1 | W-gate | 6-input AND | Possession is binary (S1) | Summed: 5-of-6 arms with the board selection missing |
| M3 | Idea clarity | ≥ 0.60 | Bottom of Ch. 13.6's TP1 band | Lower: conditions pass as scenes, TP1 reads low all campaign |
| M4 | Budget monitor | load ≤ 0.50 | Half the minutes leaves room for a bad week | 0.90: one missed session reads as insufficient drive |
| M5 | Arrival aversion | ≤ 0.25 | Above it the operation opposes itself | Ignored: casting harder amplifies both sides |
| FLT1 | Ledger lowpass | τ = 21 d, β = 0.15 | The only lawful `^O → ^P` path (Ch. 8.4) | Short τ or high β: one operation rewrites the substrate |

## Worked Example — Operation R-1

**The operator.** Two years, 1,100 logged hours. Bias rail per Chapter 7.2, τ = 3,333 hr:

```
  P_cap = 10 × (1 − e^(−1100/3333)) = 10 × (1 − 0.719) = 2.81
```

The rail sits at **2.8** of 10 — thinner than the Corvette operator's 4.3 (Ch. 13.6). It matters only as bias, and it is one more reason every verdict CJT here runs at unity.

**Stated desire.** *I run my own studio.*

**A0, pass 1.** Three readings, written before any subtraction: `0.82`, `0.44`, `0.74` — the condition being recognized as the person whose judgement decides, delivered without a studio.

```
  witness_load   = 0.82 − 0.44 = 0.38   ≥ 0.30  →  F1 BLOWS
  object_premium = 0.82 − 0.74 = 0.08   < 0.20  →  M1: PROXY_TARGET
```

Both instruments fire and they agree: the pull is largely audience, and the object stands in for standing. Decomposition breaks the wording into three parts — the work, the authority over the work, the standing of having one — and the third carries most of the amplitude. The operator re-words to the second.

**A0, pass 2.** *I decide what work I take and when.* Fresh readings `0.78`, `0.71`, `0.36`: witness load **0.07**, premium **0.42**. Both pass. No cast has fired; under `ε ∘ η = id` the first pass cost nothing but the readings.

**D-gate.** `V_drive` = F5 at 7 plus F2 at 6 = **13 `V_c`**. Origin `^C`, landing `^O`, so `ΣVf = 1.2 + 2.0 = 3.2`. Stack: `R_cap 25` (can do the work, has never priced or scheduled it), `R_policy 0`, `R_context 30` (the target is undefined for any actual week), `R_resource 20` (the hours exist; the buffer to refuse a job does not) — `R_in = 75`.

```
  I_attention = (13 − 3.2) / 75 = 9.8 / 75 = 0.1307 A_c
  margin      = 0.1307 / 0.05  = 2.61×      →  PASS
```

Run it against the *original* target and the gates couple visibly: `R_cap` 45 (never run a business) and `R_resource` 35 (capital) give `R_in = 110`, `I = 0.089`, margin **1.78× — MARGINAL**. The re-specification did not merely find a truer target; it removed 35 `Ω_c` of constraint. **An A0 failure presents downstream as resistance, which is why A0 is first.** Then the cheap repair Chapter 4.4 ranks first — one afternoon defining the week takes `R_context` from 30 to 10: `I = 9.8/55 = 0.178`, margin **3.56×**.

**W-gate.** Items 2–6 in hand. Item 1 reads **0.55** — `IDEA_UNFORMED`, hold. The cause is structural: the new target is a condition, not a scene. The operator gives it one — a specific Tuesday, one job declined, one accepted — and re-reads **0.71**. Six of six.

**P-gate.** Gnosis 2° reliably (Ch. 22.1). Plan: 4 operations, `t_op` 20 min, 72-hour spacing (Ch. 23.2), 12 days.

```
  planned = 4 × 20 = 80 min      available = 20 min/day × 12 = 240 min
  load    = 80 / 240 = 0.33      ≤ 0.50   →  pass
```

Access present; arrival aversion **0.18** — mild unease at the first declined job, not recoil. Pass.

**Arm.** `g_arm` closes, TP4 goes to `ARM`, `d_out` conducts, the cast fires. Two full passes, roughly fifty minutes on paper, zero casts — and it caught a target that would otherwise have run this chapter's opening log.

---

## Test Points

| TP | Node | Reads | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TP1** | `witness_load` | `pull_open − pull_private` | < 0.30. Read it beside M1: both failing at once is a re-wording, not a re-tuning |
| **TP2** | `path_in` | `I_attention`, `A_c` | ≥ 0.10 (2 × cutoff). Between 0.05 and 0.10 is MARGINAL — fires today, not across a campaign |
| **TP3** | `g_ready` | W `AND` P | Closed, or the *named* open input. "Not ready" is not a reading; which of the ten items is missing, is |
| **TP4** | `out` | The authorization edge | `HOLD` with its deciding number, or `ARM`. **The last reversible point on the board** |

Read them in order: is the desire mine, is there current, do I hold the schematic and the schedule — and only then arm. TP4 is the only reading you cannot take twice.

---

## Failure Modes

| Mode | Mechanism | What you observe | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gate skipped as ceremony** | The scan is treated as delay | A long log on one target, every confirmation 3° or worse, amplifier raised repeatedly | Run A0 on the logged target; expect the wording to fail |
| **A0 read after the fact** | Third rating written once the differential is known | Witness load landing just under 0.30 suspiciously often | Three ratings in ink before any subtraction |
| **Naive D-gate** | `V/R` computed without `ΣVf` | Margin overstated ~2×; a stage in cutoff on a board that "passed" | Subtract the descent chain; recompute every gate that crossed domains |
| **W-gate summed** | Six items scored and averaged | 5-of-6 arms, and the missing item is usually the board selection | `AND`. No partial credit (S1) |
| **Schedule at full budget** | Load planned near 1.0 | Campaign stalls in week two, reads as insufficient drive | Load ≤ 0.50; re-plan `n_ops`, not β |
| **Recoil cast through** | Arrival aversion above 0.25, run anyway | Confirmations arrive and are not felt; the operator undoes the arrival | Self-directed sub-operation first (Ch. 20, Ch. 23.3) |
| **Scan mistaken for undo** | Operator fires, then re-runs the gate "to take it back" | A second A0 reading that will not settle; two incomparable pass-1 rows | §21.5. Re-running is a new authorization, never a reversal |
| **Ledger over-gained** | τ shortened or feedback β raised | The substrate moves after single operations; held thresholds drift | τ = 21 d, β ≤ 0.3. Never remove the filter |

---

## What This Chapter Established

- **A0 is answered by subtraction, not introspection.** Two differentials — witness load (trip ≥ 0.30) and object premium (hold ≥ 0.20) — turn "is this really what I want" into two numbers whose common-mode bias cancels. The repair is `^6` decomposition, never `^3`.
- **The D-gate is Chapter 4 with a threshold on it.** `I = (V_drive − ΣVf)/R` against the downstream `cutoff`, 2× margin required. The Red Corvette's 1.52× is MARGINAL here — and Chapter 13.6 already called it thin.
- **The descent chain is where the margin goes.** `7/50 = 0.14` and `(7−3.2)/50 = 0.076` describe one operation; the naive form overstates by nearly double, and the error grows with how far the desire must descend.
- **W and P are `AND` gates, and that is a safety invariant.** Five-sixths of a schematic is not a circuit at 83%; it is undefined. The characteristic arming failure is 5-of-6 with the board selection wrong.
- **The gates are not independent.** Re-specifying at A0 removed 35 `Ω_c` from the stack and moved the D-gate from 1.78× to 2.61×. An unauthenticated desire presents downstream as resistance.
- **Scanning is free: `ε ∘ η = id`.** Descend into a prerequisite, find it lacking, return with the target unchanged. Two full passes cost the worked example fifty minutes and no casts.
- **Firing is not reversible: `η ∘ ε ≠ id`.** No inverse arrow, so no `undo` component and none in CCDL. An un-cast needs an `^O × ^P` ascent, and `β=∞` on a reverse path does not help — the arrow is undefined, not merely large.
- **What irreversibility does not mean.** Not that the outcome is guaranteed, not that consequences are permanent, not that prerequisites cannot decay, and nothing moral. **Decay is not inversion** — attrition is slow and visible as a drifting rail; reversal is unavailable at any speed.

---

## Exercises

**21.1** An operator rates `pull_open = 0.70`, `pull_private = 0.66`, `pull_condition = 0.58`. Compute both A0 quantities, give each verdict, and say which single instrument decided the gate.

**21.2** A desire originates at `^P` and lands at `^O`. Drives are F7 at 8 and F6 at 5; the stack is `R_cap 15`, `R_policy 40`, `R_context 10`, `R_resource 5`; the AMPLIFY stage has `cutoff = 0.10`. Compute `ΣVf`, `I_attention`, and the margin. Verdict? Now name the term you would repair first, and why it is *not* the largest one.

**21.3** Recompute 21.2 naively as `V_drive / R`. Give the margin both ways and the percentage error, then say in one sentence why the error grows with the origin domain.

**21.4** An operator holds all six W-gate items but reads Idea clarity at 0.52, and proposes weighting the gate so six-of-six at 0.52 clears. Write the two-sentence reply, name the invariant, and describe the operation that arms as a result.

**21.5** A campaign plans 6 operations of 25 minutes over 18 days against 15 available minutes per day. Compute the load, give the P-gate verdict, and state two re-plans that clear it — one changing `n_ops`, one changing the horizon.

**21.6** An operator fires a cast, regrets it within the hour, and asks for an un-cast stage. Answer in three parts: (a) which arrow of the section-retraction pair they are asking you to build; (b) why `β=∞` on it does not produce that arrow; (c) what you would build instead, and how it differs from a reversal.

**21.7** Design exercise. Add a re-entry counter to CCB-RPM that flags a target re-worded more than three times without a cast. Write the CCDL fragment, name the failure mode it catches, and name the opposite failure mode you have just installed.

*(Answers in **Appendix H**, worked in full. Every parameter here is a design choice; the A0 and clarity readings are operator self-reports on a stated scale, and the chapter never treats them as measurements of anything else.)*




# The Quantitative Table — Measuring Your Operations
*Three readings, one honest scale, and the exact limit of what a trend across them is allowed to mean*

An operator hands you a notebook. Forty operations, eighteen months, every page in the same green ink. Every `^1` Mind reading is 1° or 2°. Every confirmation is graded 1°. There is not one NO-READ row in it, not one struck-through line, not one entry marked CONFOUNDED.

You have not been handed a log. You have been handed a diary, and its author cannot tell the difference — which is the problem, because a diary and a log look identical on the page and answer different questions. The diary answers *what was that like*. The log answers *did the thing I changed on the fourteenth do anything by the twenty-first*, and it can only answer that if it contains rows the author did not enjoy writing.

Chapter 5.5 named the three readings that can be taken at a bench with nothing but a wristwatch and an honest answer: `^1` Mind, `^4` Vibration, `^7` Rhythm. Chapter 5.6 put them on a board. This chapter builds the instrument that takes them, states what each number is worth, and — the part that matters most — states plainly what none of them is.

**They are structured self-report on a scale defined in this book.** They are useful for comparing one operator against their own earlier readings under known conditions. They have not been validated against any external criterion, there is no published norm to place you on, and nothing in this chapter licenses a comparison between two operators or a claim about anyone's mind but your own. The scale is a ruler you cut yourself. It measures change on your own bench and nothing beyond it, and that is worth having as long as you never claim more.

---

## Requirements and Safety Invariants

Chapter 12.2 requires the "must not" list before the functional one.

| # | Functional requirement | Realized by |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Take three readings per operation on fixed, pre-declared scales | Gnosis sampler, rhythm clock, vibration grader |
| R2 | Capture each reading before hindsight can reach it | Two latency holds (§22.1, §22.2) |
| R3 | Admit exactly one confirmation per operation | First-only limiter (§22.2) |
| R4 | Emit NO-READ rather than a fabricated row | Horizon fuse → MUX |
| R5 | Refuse to trend across non-comparable operations | Confound gate, three-row filter |

| # | Safety invariant (MUST NOT) | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Present a reading as externally validated, or compare two operators | Scope fuse, `action=permanent_block` |
| S2 | Revise a grade after the outcome is known | Write-once fuse on the row |
| S3 | Admit a later, better confirmation into the ratio | `Limiter< max=1.0 >` on arrivals |
| S4 | Compute a trend across a cycle with two changes in it | `CONFOUNDED` exit on the confound gate |
| S5 | Let the log ascend a domain — readings are `^C`, the row is `^O` | Descent diode; feedback only via Chapter 24.5 |
| S6 | Substitute this instrument for clinical judgment | Stated in §22.5; no component can enforce it |

S6 has no component behind it and never will. If your readings are tracking something that frightens you — sleep going, mood going, the practice becoming the only thing that holds — that is a matter for a clinician, and this book has nothing to offer it. Nothing here replaces care. Close the log and make the appointment.

## 22.1 `^1` Mind Measurement — The 3 Degrees of Gnosis

`^1` Mind is *various degrees of awareness that processes, stores, outputs, and intakes Ideas*. At the bench you are reading one thing only: how much of that awareness stayed on the formed Idea, and how much went elsewhere.

| Degree | Behavioural description | State |
|---|---|---|
| **1°** | Complete absorption; the Idea is the only content present | `^1^C_{F2}\|T` |
| **2°** | Wanders and returns; intermittently clear | `^1^C_{F2}\|A` |
| **3°** | Frequent wandering; the image will not hold | `^1^C_{F2}\|A` |

Grade against the middle column, not against how the operation felt. "It felt powerful" is not on the scale. *Did the image hold, and did it return* is.

The register carries real information here and is not decoration. At 1° the awareness is not tracking itself — purpose-oriented, integrative, `|T`. At 2° and 3° it is checking the clock and narrating, which is `|A`. The Noetic never changes: it is `^1` Mind at all three degrees. Only the operational character changes, exactly as Chapter 2.5 defines register.

Now the honest part. This reading is taken by the same awareness whose depth is being reported, and no logbook design fixes that. An operator absorbed at 1° was by definition not monitoring their absorption; an operator who can describe their absorption in detail has told you it was 2°. Three defences exist and all three are procedural:

1. **Grade within two minutes of the operation ending, before any other line on the sheet is written.** The hold is set at two minutes because that is roughly how long a fresh impression survives before it starts being reconstructed into a story. At thirty minutes you are grading a memory of an impression.
2. **Grade against behaviour, never against feeling.**
3. **Never decide on `^1` alone.** It is the noisiest of the three columns. It earns its place by moving *with* `^4` Vibration across many rows, and a co-movement across ten rows is much harder for hindsight to manufacture than a single grade.

> **Bench Note — a 3° operation is a measurement of the operator, not of the board.** Chapter 5's TP2 is blunt about this: at 3°, do not compute `A`. The reading is admissible as a row — log it — but it is not admissible as evidence about the circuit, because the circuit was never properly driven. Operators hate this rule, because a 3° operation still cost them twenty minutes and they want a number for it. The number they would get would be a number about their sleep, their week, and the room. Fix the operating conditions and re-run. The row you strike is worth more than the number you would have kept.

---

## 22.2 `^4` Vibration Measurement — Confirmation Speed and Intensity

`^4` Vibration is *the degree to which an Idea resonates with the Mind, its impression*. A confirmation is the `^8` → `^9` pair of Chapter 5.6 and nothing more exotic: an event arrives and triggers a *different* Idea — the desire — into Mind. Associative surfacing. Not inference, not evidence, not a message.

Two quantities come off it, and they are different in kind.

**Speed** is `t_conf`, clocked from the *end* of the operation to the first confirmation, in minutes. It is a wristwatch reading and it is the one that enters St. John's Equation.

**Intensity** is the graded impression. The bins are 30 minutes and 2 hours, and both edges are design choices with stated failures. The 1° bin is kept short so that it sits well inside any plausible base rate — push it out to two hours and every operator grades every operation 1° and the column stops discriminating. The 3° bin is kept wide so a genuinely slow circuit still registers as something rather than nothing.

| Degree | Delay | Impression |
|---|---|---|
| **1°** | < 30 min | startling, undeniable; demands attention |
| **2°** | 30 min – 2 h | clear, but you can talk yourself out of it |
| **3°** | > 2 h | subtle, ambiguous; "was that a confirmation?" |

Three rules govern the column, listed in the order operators break them.

**Only the first confirmation enters the ratio.** Later ones stay on the sheet as `^4` evidence and never re-enter. An operator who admits a stronger confirmation that arrived four hours later has improved their number by choosing their data, and the improvement is entirely artefact. The instrument enforces this with a limiter that admits one arrival and drops the rest.

**Grade within thirty minutes of noticing, in ink, and never revise.** A 3° confirmation graded a week later, once the desire has actually manifested, grades 1° every time. This is not dishonesty. It is ordinary hindsight, it is unavoidable once the outcome is known, and the only defence against it is a clock.

**A confirmation is not a manifestation.** It says the signal reached the Ether. It says nothing about whether the signal reached the target with enough amplitude to clear `R_constraint` — Chapter 13's delivered-current band, where confirmations arrive reliably and nothing else does. Reading confirmations as arrivals is the error that costs more than all the others combined.

Beyond the horizon — `t_H = 3 × median(t_conf over the last ten operations)`, floored at 24 hours (§23.1) — there is no reading at all. The entry is **NO-READ**, and NO-READ is a result: it is the row that tells you whether your confirmation rate exceeds your own base rate.

---

## 22.3 `^7` Rhythm Measurement — Clocking the Operation

`^7` Rhythm is *the rate and pattern a Mind is exposed to an Idea, entraining it*. At the bench it reads as one number: `t_op`, the duration of the operation, start to finish, off a wristwatch. The state is `^7^C_{F6}|E` — Structure, embodied register, because it is a clocked bodily act and reads as one.

| Degree | Duration | Why this edge |
|---|---|---|
| **1°** | > 30 min | Full establishment |
| **2°** | 10 – 30 min | The working band |
| **3°** | < 10 min | Below ten minutes gnosis has not had time to establish |

The 10- and 30-minute edges sit at the two places operators actually break. Below ten, `^1` Mind almost never reaches 2°. Above thirty, `^1` Mind almost always falls — the operator tires and the image goes. Widen the bins and you merge a failed operation with a held one, which is the one thing the column exists to prevent.

The whole column depends on a convention that costs nothing to set and everything to skip. `t_op` has two defensible start points: the moment you begin the procedure, and the moment concentration actually establishes. For most operators they differ by five to ten minutes. **Either is fine. Mixing them across a log makes every comparison in it a comparison between two different measurements**, which is to say worthless. Write your convention on page one in ink before the first entry, and do not revise it because a later operation would read better under the other one. The instrument holds the convention in a write-once latch for exactly this reason.

---

## 22.4 The Table Sheet — Tracking Across Multiple Operations

One row per operation, every operation, including the ones that did not read. The printable forms are Appendix G — Form 1 the operation log, Form 2 the confirmation log, Form 3 the parameter-change log — and Form 3 governs the other two.

Eight fields carry the chapter: `Op #`, `t_op`, `t_conf`, `^1`, `^4`, `^7`, a flag column, and `A = 3 t_conf / t_op` from Chapter 13.5.

The three degrees also give a bookkeeping figure worth writing down. Define the **coupling sum** `S = m + v`, where `m` is the `^1` degree and `v` the `^4` degree, each 1 to 3. `S` runs 2 to 6, and lower is stronger. It is a sum and not a product, and the reason is not aesthetic: these are **ordinal bins**. 1°, 2° and 3° state an order and nothing else — the gap between 1° and 2° is not claimed equal to the gap between 2° and 3°, and multiplying ordinals asserts a ratio scale the bins do not have. A sum is already generous. Treat `S` as a bookkeeping index for ordering rows in one log, never as a magnitude.

> **Bench Note — the notation says the same thing the arithmetic does.** The three readings are `^1^C_{F2}|A + ^4^C_{F2}|f + ^7^C_{F6}|E` — the `+` of co-presence (Chapter 2.6). Three distinct measurements, present together, remaining distinct. It is emphatically **not** `×`. A `×` would assert that the three fuse into a single emergent state, and under v7.7 discipline that requires a named emergent result, which this book does not define. There is no "operation quality" state in the topos and `S` is not one. That is why `S` is a bookkeeping sum rather than a state literal, and why it never appears in a CCDL listing. The operator discipline and the measurement discipline are the same discipline here, which is a good sign that both are right.

Three flags do most of the work. **NO-READ**: no confirmation inside the horizon; `^1` and `^7` still logged, `^4` absent, `S` not computed. **CONFOUNDED**: two or more things changed in the cycle, including things you did not choose — illness, upheaval, a week of bad sleep. Nothing may be concluded from a confounded row, *including the parts you liked*. **Struck**: a corrected value, struck through and initialled, both readable. The crossed-out number is often the interesting one.

---

## 22.5 Interpreting Trends — When to Adjust, When to Abort

A single row diagnoses nothing. **Three comparable rows are the minimum**, where comparable means: same board, same declared conventions, one parameter changed at most between any two of them, and no CONFOUNDED flag in the sequence. Three is a design choice — it is the fewest rows in which a direction can be distinguished from a pair of readings, and one bad clock cannot redirect a campaign that needs three rows to turn. Two rows is a line through two points, which is not a trend; it is arithmetic.

Read two things down the column, in this order.

**`A` first**, because it is smooth in the clocks. `A = 3 t_conf / t_op` moves continuously with a timing error, where the reduced denominator `b` swings wildly (Chapter 13.5). The step ratio is `ρ = A_next / A_current` (§23.2). Falling `A` with `ρ ≤ 0.6` is a converging campaign. Flat `A` across three comparable rows means nothing you are changing is reaching the delivered current.

**`S` second**, as a cross-check. When `A` and `S` move together, the reading is coherent. When they disagree, the disagreement is itself the finding, and there are exactly two informative cases:

| Pattern | Reading | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `A` falls, `S` flat | The bins are coarser than the ratio; real change inside one bin | Trust `A`. Record `S`. Continue |
| `A` flat, `S` falls | Operating conditions improved; the circuit did not | Stop tuning the board. `R_op` is the problem |
| Both fall | Converging | Continue; one lever at a time |
| Both rise for two consecutive comparable rows | Diverging | **Abort.** Return to A0 (Chapter 21.1) |
| `A` flat, `S` rises | The operator is degrading while the board holds | Rest. Re-read §22.1's bench note |

**When to adjust.** One lever, one cycle, with a prediction written before the operation: a named test point and a direction. *TP3 comes off the ceiling* is a prediction. *It should improve things* is not. Verdict only after one operation and its first confirmation.

**When to abort.** Three conditions, any one sufficient. Both columns rising across two consecutive comparable rows. `A` flat across three comparable rows while `ρ` sits near 1.0 — this signal arrives *before* `A` reaches the re-spec boundary of 9, which is the whole point of watching a trend rather than a row. Or `^1` Mind falling to 3° for three consecutive operations at constant `t_op`, which is not a circuit reading at all: it says the operator cannot currently run the board, and the response is rest and a decomposition (§23.3), not a fourth attempt.

And the condition that is not on any table: if the log itself has become the thing that is not right — if you are casting to make the readings move, or the readings are the only evidence your week produced — stop and speak to a clinician. That is not a failure of the instrument. It is outside what any instrument in this book is for.

---

## Full CCDL Listing — CCB-QT

```cas
board ccb_qt {                            // CCB-QT — the acquisition bench
    input:  operation;                    // the operation as run
    output: log_row;                      // one admissible row, or NO-READ

    node practice_rail: ^5^P_{F7}|T;      // Female: accumulated practice — bias only

    // ---- S1  GNOSIS SAMPLER ----
    node gnosis: ^1^C_{F2}|A;             // Mind: awareness on the formed Idea
    hold h_mind: Hold< signal=gnosis, duration=2.0 >;          // min, before hindsight
    monitor m_mind: Monitor< signal=h_mind, limit=[1.0, 2.0],
                             action_on_violation=NO_COMPUTE >; // 3° -> no A

    // ---- S2  RHYTHM CLOCK ----
    node clocked_op: ^7^C_{F6}|E;         // Rhythm: the operation, start to finish
    fuse f_conv: Fuse< path=clocked_op, threshold=1.0,
                       action=permanent_block >;               // convention write-once

    // ---- S3  CONFIRMATION INTAKE ----
    node arrival:  ^8^C_{F2}|E;           // Above/Cause: the event that arrives
    node recalled: ^9^C_{F2}|A;           // Below/Effect: the desire brought back
    limiter l_first: Limiter< signal=arrival, max=1.0 >;       // first only
    fuse f_horizon: Fuse< path=recalled, threshold=1440.0,
                          action=no_read >;                    // 24 h floor

    // ---- S4  VIBRATION GRADER ----
    node impression: ^4^C_{F2}|f;         // Vibration: the impression it made
    hold h_vib: Hold< signal=impression, duration=30.0 >;      // min from noticing

    // ---- S5  ROW ASSEMBLER ----
    node row:     ^6^E_{F6}|A;            // Male: the readings composed into a row
    node no_read: ^0^O_{F6}|A;            // Idea: the logged absence of a reading
    mux out: MUX< inputs=[ row, no_read ], select=f_horizon >;

    // ---- S6  CONFOUND GATE and WRITE-ONCE ----
    node changes: ^6^O_{F6}|A;            // Male: what was altered this cycle
    monitor m_confound: Monitor< signal=changes, threshold=1.0,
                                 action_on_violation=CONFOUNDED >;
    fuse f_write: Fuse< path=out, threshold=1.0, action=permanent_block >;
    fuse f_scope: Fuse< path=out, threshold=1.0, action=permanent_block >;  // S1

    // ---- S7  TREND and DESCENT ----
    filter f_trend: Filter< in=out, out=trend, type=lowpass, tau=3.0 >;     // ops
    monitor m_abort: Monitor< signal=trend, threshold=0.6,
                              action_on_violation=ABORT_REVIEW >;
    diode d_out: Diode< ^E -> ^O >;       // the row descends into the ledger

    probe tp1: h_mind;        probe tp2: clocked_op;
    probe tp3: l_first;       probe tp4: f_trend;
}
```

**S1 — Gnosis sampler.** `Hold` captures the grade and freezes it; `duration=2.0` is the two-minute latency of §22.1. `m_mind` is the enforcement of Chapter 5's TP2: a 3° reading exits `NO_COMPUTE`, which logs the row and withholds `A`.

**S2 — Rhythm clock.** The convention fuse is a genuine `Fuse` with a finite threshold and `action=permanent_block`, not an infinite-gain comparator. It is tempting to write `β=∞` on any latch that must never yield; that is an idealization a validator rejects, exactly as Chapter 24 notes on the CSB's red path, and here there is no need for it — a fuse latches by construction.

**S3 — Confirmation intake.** `^8` triggers, `^9` surfaces; both are modelled at `^C` so that no unlawful `^O → ^C` ascent enters the listing (§23.1 does the same). The limiter is S3 in hardware: one arrival admitted, the rest logged as evidence and dropped from the ratio. The horizon fuse carries the 24-hour floor as a literal; a running bench recomputes 3× the rolling median and holds the floor underneath.

**S4–S5.** The grader's thirty-minute hold is the anti-hindsight latch. The MUX selects on the horizon fuse: intact routes the assembled row, blown routes the `no_read` terminal, which is a declared node rather than a dangling name — an absence you can probe is worth more than an absence you infer. The row itself is `^6` Male, the readings decomposed and composed into a structure. It is not `^3` and not `^8`: assembling a row is compositional work, not aversion and not associative triggering.

**S6–S7.** The confound gate permits one change per cycle; two exits `CONFOUNDED`. The scope fuse is the only component here with no signal-processing function: it exists so that S1 has an enforcement column, and it blows the moment a row is used to support a claim about anyone but this operator. The trend filter's `tau=3.0` is three operations, the minimum from §22.5; the abort monitor watches `ρ` against 0.6. `d_out` is the lawful descent, and the only path back up is Chapter 24.5's ethical-drift filter, which takes this log as its literal input.

## Parameter and BOM Table

Every value is a design choice made in this book. None is a measurement.

| Ref | Component | Setting | Why | Failure at other values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Hold, `^1` grade | 2 min | Roughly how long a fresh impression survives | 30 min: the grade is a reconstruction, and reconstructions trend upward |
| M1 | Gnosis monitor | admit 1°–2° | Chapter 5's TP2: 3° measures the operator | Admitted: operator noise enters the circuit record as circuit data |
| — | `^1` bins | behavioural | Held / returned / would not hold | Feeling-based: every operation grades 1° after a good week |
| F1 | Convention fuse | write-once | `t_op` boundaries must match across the log | Revisable: every comparison is between two different measurements |
| — | `^7` bins | 10 / 30 min | The two points operators break | Wider: a failed operation and a held one land in one bin |
| L1 | First-only limiter | max = 1 | The ratio needs one arrival, not the best one | Best-of: `A` improves with nothing changed |
| F2 | Horizon fuse | 3 × median, floor 24 h | Passes slow circuits, excludes base rate | Short: live circuits declared dead. Long: everything "confirms" |
| H2 | Hold, `^4` grade | 30 min from noticing | Before hindsight reaches the grade | Later: no operation is ever graded 3° again |
| — | `^4` bins | 30 min / 2 h | 1° bin inside plausible base rate | 1° edge at 2 h: the column stops discriminating |
| M2 | Confound gate | 1 change / cycle | Attribution needs a single lever | 2 changes: a better number, bought, with no account of what bought it |
| F3 | Write-once latch | `permanent_block` | Grades must not move after the outcome | Revisable: the log becomes a record of the outcome, not of the operations |
| F4 | Scope fuse | `permanent_block` | Invariant S1 | Absent: a self-report scale gets quoted as a finding |
| FLT1 | Trend filter | τ = 3 operations | Fewest rows that can show a direction | 1 op: one bad clock redirects a campaign. 10: the abort arrives too late |
| M3 | Abort monitor | `ρ` ≤ 0.6 | Reaches DRIVE in one step from 9 (§23.2) | 1.0: divergence reads as steady |
| — | `S` | ordinal sum, 2–6 | Bins are ordinal; a product asserts a ratio scale | Multiplied or averaged: a coarse index quoted to two decimals |

## Worked Example — Campaign Q-3

Self-directed board (CCB-SELF), one desire, six operations across nineteen days. Convention declared on page one: `t_op` starts when the operator sits down and begins the procedure. Clocks logged raw; `A` computed on the 5-minute grid of §23.1.

| Op | `t_op` | `t_conf` | `^1` | `^4` | `^7` | `S` | `A` | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15 | 150 | 3° | 3° | 2° | 6 | — | `NO_COMPUTE` |
| 2 | 25 | 100 | 2° | 2° | 2° | 4 | 12.0 | — |
| 3 | 25 | 60 | 2° | 2° | 2° | 4 | 7.2 | — |
| 4 | 25 | — | 2° | — | 2° | — | — | NO-READ |
| 5 | 30 | 45 | 1° | 2° | 2° | 3 | 4.5 | `CONFOUNDED` |
| 6 | 30 | 40 | 1° | 2° | 2° | 3 | 4.0 | — |

**Operation 1.** `^1` = 3°, so M1 exits `NO_COMPUTE` and no `A` is written — correctly, because at fifteen minutes the gnosis never established. The row is logged in full. One change follows, CH-001: `t_op` 15 → 25 min, prediction *TP1 moves to 2° by operation 2*.

**Operation 2.** `A = 3 × 100 / 25 = 12.0` — RE-SPEC band (§13.5). `S` = 4. CH-001 verdict: KEEP, prediction met.

**Operation 3.** `A = 3 × 60 / 25 = 7.2` — DRIVE. `ρ = 7.2 / 12.0 = 0.60`, exactly at the abort monitor's limit and on the right side of it. Note that `S` did not move: 4 both times. This is the coarse-bins case from §22.5 — a 40% fall in `A` happened entirely inside the 2°/2° cell. Trust `A`, record `S`.

**Operation 4.** Horizon: `3 × median(150, 100, 60) = 300` min, but the 24-hour floor governs at this point in the log, so `t_H = 1440`. Nothing arrives. **NO-READ**, `^1` and `^7` logged, `^4` absent, `S` not computed. This is the row that tells the operator their confirmation rate is not simply their base rate.

**Operation 5.** `t_op` raised to 30 *and* the symbol changed, on a week of bad sleep. `S` = 3 and `A` = 4.5 — the best reading in the log, and worthless. M2 exits `CONFOUNDED`; nothing may be concluded, including the parts the operator liked.

**Operation 6.** One change only, CH-003: revert the symbol, hold `t_op` at 30. `A = 3 × 40 / 30 = 4.0`, `S` = 3, `ρ = 4.0 / 7.2 = 0.56` against the comparable predecessor. Converging.

**The readout.** Comparable rows are 2, 3 and 6 — three, the minimum. `A` runs 12.0 → 7.2 → 4.0 with `ρ` = 0.60 and 0.56, both inside 0.6. `S` runs 4 → 4 → 3. Both columns fall, they do not disagree, and the campaign continues with one lever at a time. **Six operations, three usable rows.** That ratio is not a sign of a bad log. It is what an honest one looks like, and the notebook in the cold open — forty rows, forty usable — is the one to distrust.

## Test Points

| TP | Node | Reads | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TP1** | `h_mind` | `^1` degree and its capture latency | 1° or 2°, captured under 2 min. A 3° reading is admissible as a row and inadmissible as evidence — do not compute `A` |
| **TP2** | `clocked_op` | `t_op` against the boundary written on page one | Same rule as every prior entry. A different rule makes the row incomparable, not merely different |
| **TP3** | `l_first` | Arrivals admitted | Exactly one, inside the horizon, graded within 30 min. Two admitted means the ratio has been chosen rather than measured |
| **TP4** | `f_trend` | `ρ` across three comparable rows | ≤ 0.6 per step. Flat near 1.0 across three rows is the abort signal, and it arrives before `A` reaches 9 |

Read them in order. TP1 and TP2 decide whether the row is admissible at all; TP3 decides whether there is a `^4` reading; TP4 is the only one that speaks about the campaign. Three of the four can send you home without a number, and that ratio is deliberate.

---

## Failure Modes

| Mode | Mechanism | What you observe | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Retrospective grading** | Grades written after the outcome is known | No operation in the log was ever graded 3° | H1 and H2 latencies; ink; never revise |
| **Best-of admission** | A later, stronger confirmation entered | `A` improving while nothing about the operation changed | L1 at `max=1`; Form 2's first-confirmation field |
| **Boundary drift** | `t_op` start defined differently across entries | Two operations that felt identical reading five minutes apart | F1 write-once; the convention on page one |
| **Window creep** | Horizon widened until something lands | Every operation confirms; no NO-READ rows anywhere | Fix `t_H` before the cast; run a one-week control count |
| **Multi-lever cycle** | Two or more changes between readings | A better number with no account of which change bought it | M2 `CONFOUNDED`; claim nothing from the row |
| **Ordinal inflation** | `S` averaged, multiplied, or quoted to decimals | "Mean coupling 3.67 this month" | `S` orders rows in one log; it has no magnitude |
| **Scale export** | Readings compared between operators, or quoted as a finding | A degree used as evidence about someone else's mind | F4 scope fuse; invariant S1 |
| **Instrument substitution** | The log used to track distress | Readings watched more closely than sleep | §22.5. See a clinician; nothing here replaces care |

The last two fail silently. Every other row on this table announces itself in the log; those two look like diligence.

---

## What This Chapter Established

- **These are structured self-reports on a scale defined in this book, not validated instruments.** They order one operator's rows against each other under known conditions. They carry no external norm, do not compare two operators, and are evidence about no mind but the operator's own.
- **Three of ten Noetics take a bench reading without instrumentation** — `^1` Mind, `^4` Vibration, `^7` Rhythm. That is a fact about instrumentation, not about the topos: all 40 states carry an activation in principle (Appendix L), but these three answer *how much* without hardware.
- **Register carries information in the `^1` column.** The same `^1^C_{F2}` reads `|T` at 1° and `|A` at 2° and 3°. The Noetic never changes; the operational character does.
- **The three readings are `+`, not `×`.** Co-presence of three distinct measurements, no named emergent result, therefore no licensed fusion. `S` is a bookkeeping sum of ordinals, not a state, and never appears in a listing.
- **Hindsight is defeated by clocks, not by resolve.** Two minutes for `^1`, thirty from noticing for `^4`, ink, no revision. Every other defence has been tried by every operator who ever kept a log.
- **NO-READ and CONFOUNDED are results.** A log with neither has a window too wide or a discipline too loose, and is measuring the operator's patience.
- **Three comparable rows is the floor for a trend**, and comparable is a technical word: same board, same conventions, one lever, no confound flag.
- **`A` leads and `S` cross-checks.** When they disagree the disagreement is the finding — coarse bins when `A` moves alone, degrading operating conditions when `S` moves alone.
- **The abort signal arrives at the trend, not the row.** Flat `ρ` near 1.0 across three rows fires before `A` reaches the re-spec boundary of 9, which is the entire reason for watching a column instead of a number.

## Exercises

**22.1** An operation logs `t_op = 20`, `t_conf = 75`, `^1` = 2°, `^4` = 2°. Compute `^7`'s degree, `S`, and `A`. Which band? State which single figure you would act on and which you would only record.

**22.2** An operator's last six rows read `S` = 4, 4, 3, 3, 3, 3 and `A` = 9.0, 8.7, 9.1, 8.9, 9.0, 8.8. The only thing changed between rows was the amplifier β, raised each time. Diagnose using §22.5's table, name the failure mode, and state the first measurement you would demand.

**22.3** A colleague grades a confirmation 1° "because it was unmistakable" — six hours after the operation, and graded the following morning once the desire had manifested. Identify three separate rule violations, state which component of CCB-QT catches each, and give the grade the entry should have carried.

**22.4** Op 4 of campaign Q-3 is a NO-READ. Write the argument that the row should be deleted from the log, then rebut it in three sentences using §22.2 and the base-rate reasoning behind the horizon.

**22.5** `S` is defined as `m + v`. A reader proposes `S' = m × v` on the grounds that it "separates the good rows better." Give the measurement-theory objection in one sentence, then give the CAS notation objection in one sentence, and state which of the two you would put in a design review first and why.

**22.6 (Build)** Add a stage to CCB-QT that flags a row whose confirmation could be claimed by a second live operation — the attribution collision of §23.1. Write the CCDL fragment, name the component type, state where it sits in the signal path, and state what it must *not* do to the row it flags.

**22.7 (Marquee)** The scope fuse F4 has no signal-processing function; it enforces an invariant no measurement can check. Argue either that it belongs on the board or that it is decoration. If you argue it belongs, state what physical event blows it. If you argue it is decoration, name the mechanism that would enforce S1 instead, and say honestly whether that mechanism is a circuit or a person.

*(Answers in **Appendix H**, worked in full. Every parameter in this chapter is a design choice with a stated failure at other values; the scales are conventions defined in this book, not measurements of anything outside it.)*




# St. John's Equation — Advanced Calibration
*Reading a campaign instead of a cast — scheduling, interference, and what the equation does at its limits*

Two operators sit through the same operation and each writes down two numbers. The first records `t_op = 30` minutes and `t_conf = 90`, runs Chapter 5.3's arithmetic, and reads a required gain of **9**. The second caught the clock differently — 31 and 88 — because they disagreed by a breath about when the gnosis began and when the song on the radio registered.

The second operator's reading is **264**.

Neither made a mistake. Thirty-one is prime, 264 factors as 8 × 3 × 11, the fraction will not reduce, and the denominator Chapter 5 tells you to read as a required gain comes back thirty times larger for two minutes of honest disagreement about a wristwatch. That is a reduction problem, not a measurement problem, and Chapter 13.5 already fixed it for a single cast: act on the amplitude ratio `A = b/a = 3/η`, never on `b` alone. The two operators' ratios are 9.00 and 8.52.

Section 13.5 reads one cast. It does not run a **campaign** — a sequence of operations on one desire, scheduled against each other, competing with everything else you have live. Campaigns break in four places a single cast never reaches: at the limits of the equation, at the scheduling, at the interference between concurrent operations, and at the point where an operator with three live campaigns wonders why all three went cold in the same week. This chapter is the instrument board. It casts nothing. It reads the log.

---

## Requirements and Safety Invariants

Chapter 12.2 requires the "must not" list before the functional one.

| # | Functional requirement | Realized by |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Turn two clock readings into an amplitude requirement | Quantizer → ratio → readout |
| R2 | Stay stable against clock jitter of a few minutes | Ratio `A` on a quantized grid (§23.1) |
| R3 | Declare NO-READ rather than invent a number | Horizon gate, band guard |
| R4 | Report whether a campaign converges | Ledger filter, ratio `ρ` |
| R5 | Derate when other operations are live | Interference model (§23.2) |

| # | Safety invariant (MUST NOT) | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Report `A ≥ 9` as an amplifier instruction | Re-spec fuse, `block_until_decomposed` |
| S2 | Admit a confirmation arriving after the horizon | Horizon fuse, `action=no_read` |
| S3 | Accept a confirmation two live operations could claim | Entry marked `AMBIGUOUS` |
| S4 | Let a blown ledger reset by re-wording the target | Re-spec must change domain or object |
| S5 | Run without the operator's CSB armed (Chapter 24) | No ledger opens on a blown involution monitor |

## 23.1 The 1/3 Constant — Deeper Derivation from Fibonacci and Pi

Section 5.2 sets `τ = 1/3` beside π ≈ 3.14159 — both non-terminating — as a mnemonic for domains left *open*. Be exact about what that is. φ and π are mathematical constants with proofs behind them. **There is no derivation that produces 1/3 from either, and this book does not offer one.** The only derivation of `τ` in these pages is Section 5.2's training arc: roughly 10,000 active hours inside a roughly 30,000-hour span, one part work to two parts gestation.

```
η = t_op / t_conf     result = η × τ = a/b     A = b/a = 3/η = 3 t_conf / t_op
```

`A` is fixed by two clock readings and by `τ`. Nothing else enters. **`τ` is a scale factor — a unit convention — expressing a cast's requirement against that same 1:3 split.** Change `τ` and every number in every log changes by the same factor, while every *comparison between operations* stays where it was. The equation's content is the ordering it puts on your operations, not the magnitude of any one reading. That is a structural analogy, not a measured law. Nothing here shows that time is quantized at thirds, and a reader who treats `A = 9` the way they treat a resistor's 470 Ω will over-trust two wristwatch readings and a convention.

### Quantize before you reduce

`A` moves smoothly. The integer pair does not, because lowest-terms denominators are not continuous in their inputs — that is the whole content of the cold open, where 30/90 gave (1, 9) and 31/88 gave (31, 264).

Quantize both clocks onto a **5-minute grid** before reducing. Five minutes is a design choice: finer than the 30-minute bins Section 5.5 uses to grade `^4` Vibration, coarser than the moment an operator *notices* a confirmation, which is not a one-minute-accurate event. Too fine and the coprime explosion returns; at 30 minutes a 20-minute operation confirmed at 25 bins with one confirmed at 45, erasing the difference between an overdriving circuit and an ordinary one. **If `a > 3` after quantizing, discard the pair and act on `A`.**

> **Bench Note — check this one by hand before you trust the bench.** Take `t_op = 27`, `t_conf = 64`. Raw: `27/192` reduces to `9/64` — a = 9, b = 64. On the grid: `25/195` reduces to `5/39` — a = 5, b = 39. The two pairs share nothing at all. Now compute `A`: `3 × 64/27 = 7.11` and `3 × 65/25 = 7.80`. Both land in the same band and say the same thing. Do this arithmetic yourself once. Until you have watched `b` swing from 64 to 39 while `A` barely moves, you will keep reaching for the denominator, because Chapter 5 taught you to.

### The bands, and the two limits

Chapter 13.5's bands fall out of `A = 3/η`, and their edges land on clean values of η.

| `A` | η | Reading | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A ≤ 1` | η ≥ 3 | Sufficient | Stop calibrating. Act |
| `1 < A < 3` | 1 < η < 3 | Close | Finish the resistance work |
| `3 ≤ A < 9` | 1/3 < η ≤ 1 | Under-driven | One lever at a time |
| `A ≥ 9` | η ≤ 1/3 | Weak coupling | Re-specify (§23.3, §23.4) |

Chapter 5.4's Red Corvette sits at η = 1/3, `A` = 9 — exactly on the re-specification boundary. The canonical worked example in this book is a borderline cast, worth knowing before you copy its numbers.

**`t_conf → ∞`: the confirmation never comes.** `η → 0`, `A → ∞`, and the temptation is to write `β=∞` into the listing. That is an idealization the validator rejects — parameter fields are range-checked and refuse non-finite values — and where a real build would substitute a large finite gain, no finite substitute exists here, because the input is *missing* rather than large. The bench returns **NO-READ**, behind a horizon:

```
t_H = 3 × median(t_conf over the last 10 logged operations),   floor 24 h
```

Over a long enough window *everything* confirms: a loose desire matches some event in any given day, and an operator who holds the window open until something matches is measuring their own patience. The 3× multiple is wide enough that a genuinely slow circuit still reads, narrow enough that the median stays meaningful; the 24-hour floor covers the early log, where the median rests on too few entries. Too short and live circuits are declared dead; too long and the log fills with base rate.

**`t_conf → 0`: the confirmation arrives inside the operation.** `η → ∞`, `A → 0`, and the reduction degenerates. At `t_op = 30`, `t_conf = 4`: `η = 7.5`, `result = 5/2`, pair (5, 2) — "twice as strong, five more times," for a circuit that confirmed inside four minutes. The quantizer does not save that; only the band guard does. Above η = 3 the bench returns **OUT-OF-BAND-HIGH**, and the instruction is Section 13.6's: stop calibrating, take the practical action.

## 23.2 Multi-Operation Compounding — When β_next > 10

The title states the condition as Chapter 5 states it, because that is how it arrives: an operator reads a denominator above 10 and asks what to do. On this bench it is `A ≥ 9` — the same complaint with a stable number attached.

A campaign is a sequence of operations on one target, each designed from the last one's reading, and demand compounds as `demand_{k+1} = demand_k × A_k`. **The compounding is multiplicative.** Two operations each reading `A = 3` demand nine times the original delivered current. Cascaded gains multiply (§10.5) and a campaign is a cascade in time, which is why a high reading is a stop rather than a challenge: it is the head of a geometric series.

**`A` is not a β setting.** Section 13.5 governs: `A` multiplies the *delivered current* at TP4, and five things set that current — clarity of the formed `^0` Idea, transmission through the dial divider, residual aversion, the amplifier, and `R_op`. The CJT's design range tops out near **4.0** (Chapter 3.3). So β across a campaign moves under a ceiling, not a formula: one increment per operation inside 0.5–4.0, with everything above taken from the other four levers or from recruitment. An operator who reads `A = 9` and writes `β = 9` has specified a device that does not exist.

```
φ_k = 1 / A_{k+1}   (delivery fraction)      ρ_k = A_{k+1} / A_k   (convergence ratio)
```

Design threshold: **`ρ ≤ 0.6` per operation.** From `A = 9` a campaign at 0.6 runs 9 → 5.4 → 3.2 → 1.9 → 1.2: inside DRIVE by the second step, near sufficiency by the fourth. At `ρ ≥ 1.0` it is diverging, and the action is to stop by operation three rather than cast harder. A flat `ρ` sustained is the "η flat" row of Section 22.5. Believe no trend before three operations — `A` is a quotient of two soft clock readings, and one of them has no error bars at all.

> **Bench Note — the flat ledger column is a tautology, so do not read it as evidence.** It is natural to keep an "absolute target" column, `T_k = G_k × A_k`, where `G_k` is cumulative realized gain. Work the algebra and `T_{k+1} = T_k` identically, for any campaign, converging or not — because `G` is itself defined from the `A`s. A column that cannot vary cannot inform. Operators build it, watch it hold at 9 for four operations, and conclude the campaign is on target. It would have held at 9 if every operation had been worthless.

### Scheduling: one live operation per horizon

A confirmation you cannot attribute to a specific operation is not a measurement. **No new operation on a desire begins until the previous horizon has closed.** At a median `t_conf` of 45 minutes, `3 × 45 = 135` minutes falls under the 24-hour floor and the floor governs; the campaign below uses 72 hours, which also lets the `^5` capacitor recover between casts (§7.3). Fire inside the horizon and a confirmation has two candidate causes: mark it `AMBIGUOUS` and drop it from the median. An operator who wants a good number assigns every confirmation to the most recent cast, and the ledger then reports a convergence that never happened.

### Interference between concurrent operations

Concurrent operations on *different* desires share one operator: one `^1` Mind budget, one `^5` substrate, one attention rail. Chapter 9.3's coupling model transfers directly and the coefficient keeps its name.

```
η_effective = η_isolated × ( 1 − k × (N − 1) )
```

| `k` | Condition | Observed when ignored |
|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | Different Drive, different domain, no shared symbol | Nothing. The intended posture |
| 0.15 | Same Drive, different target | Uniform mild slump in η across everything live |
| 0.35 | Same Drive, shared symbols — sigil letters, same person | Every campaign's `A` doubles in a week for no visible reason |
| 0.60 | Contradictory desires — one raises the other's `R_constraint` | Both ledgers diverge, `ρ > 1` on each at once |

Work it. Three live operations, all on F5 Agency, all sharing symbols: `N = 3`, `k = 0.35`, derating `1 − 0.35 × 2 = 0.30`. Take an operation reading `η = 1.0` in isolation — comfortably DRIVE at `A = 3`. Concurrently, `η_effective = 0.30`, so with `t_op = 30` the confirmation lands at `30 / 0.30 = 100` minutes, already on the grid:

```
η = 30 / 100 = 0.30        A = 3 × 100 / 30 = 10.0        →  RE-SPEC. The fuse blows.
```

**A comfortable operation became a re-specification reading and nothing was wrong with the operation.** The three campaigns were wrong with each other. This is the most under-diagnosed failure on the bench, because the operator inspects the cast — gnosis, sigil, wording — and the cast is fine.

Hence: keep `k(N − 1) ≤ 0.3`, holding derating at or above 0.7. At `k = 0.05` that permits seven concurrent operations; at `k = 0.35` it permits exactly one. **Run one live operation per Drive.** The derating is first-order and honest only while `k(N − 1) < 0.5`; past that it runs to zero and then negative, which is not a statement about anything. Beyond half derating the model's answer is not a number — it is *shed operations*.

> **A plain line about the operator, not the circuit.** A ledger that will not converge, run against a desire that will not let go, is a recognizable and unpleasant place to be. Everything here is arithmetic on a log. None of it is a psychological or medical instrument, and it does not describe, diagnose, or treat distress or compulsion of any kind. If the operations have stopped being something you choose, that is a matter for a clinician, and nothing in this book substitutes for that care.

---

## 23.3 Sub-Desire Resolution — When the Prime Desire Is Blocked

`A ≥ 9` is almost never a statement about how much amplitude you need. It is a statement that the target you specified is not the target that is blocked. Section 21.1 authenticates A0 before an operation; this section is what you do when the bench tells you, three operations in, that the authentication was wrong.

The procedure is decomposition, and the Noetic matters. You take the stated desire apart and test its parts — `^6^C_{F6}|A`, Male, Cognitive domain, analytical register: what is this Idea made of. It is emphatically **not** `^3`. What you are usually *looking for* is a `^3`, a visceral aversion lying across the path, the can't-stomach-it recoil that keeps the cast from landing — but the finding of it is `^6` work. Confusing the two is the drift Chapter 2.2 warns about, and it costs: an operator who believes aversion-hunting is itself `^3` goes looking for something to recoil from and duly finds it.

The arithmetic is the point. A blocking sub-desire sits in the operator's own `^5`, so it is addressed with a self-directed board (Chapter 20) against much lower resistance. Lower `R` means higher η means lower `A`, and sub-desire operations routinely read in DRIVE while the prime desire reads past 9. Then the prime desire is re-read, not re-argued.

---

## 23.4 The Tree of Life Method — Redirecting Through Higher Probability Paths

The second answer to a blown re-spec fuse is to change the route rather than the target: cast for an intermediate outcome that is genuinely wanted, sits at lower resistance, and from which the prime target is reachable — then read the prime desire again from the new position.

**The hops obey the diode chain.** An intermediate sits at the target's domain or lower (§8.1). You may route an Operational target through an Evaluative or Operational intermediate. You may not route it through one requiring an ascent back to Principled mid-chain — `^O × ^P` is invalid notation for the same reason it is invalid engineering (§8.3). The one lawful ascent is the filtered O→P feedback path, on a time constant of weeks (§24.5), not inside a campaign.

**The method cannot promise a smaller total.** Demands cascade multiplicatively, so a two-hop route costs `A₁ × A₂`. Suppose a direct read of `A = 36`, an intermediate reading `A₁ = 4`, and the prime desire read again from the new position at `A₂ = 3`: the product is 12 against 36 direct. Worth having — but **the comparison is retrospective.** You did not compute 4 and 3 by factoring 36. You cast for the intermediate, read 4 from that operation's own log, arrived, cast again, read 3. The route might equally have read 8 and 6. What the method does promise is the thing that matters: **every stage sits inside the feasible band, which the direct path did not.**

---

## 23.5 Astrological Weighting — Planetary Dials for Timing

The tradition schedules operations against a planetary calendar and applies a timing multiplier spanning 0.5 at worst to 3.0 at best. **No celestial mechanism is asserted, no evidence for one is offered, and the multiplier is not claimed to be a measured quantity.** It is a dial. Its **default value is 1.0**, and any other value in your log is a statement about your practice, not about the sky.

What a fixed external calendar genuinely does — a real engineering function — is take the scheduling decision away from the operator. The moment you most want to cast is the moment your `^1` Mind reading is least trustworthy, because wanting to cast and being able to hold gnosis are different faculties and only one of them is impatient. An externally fixed schedule is a watchdog timer: it fires on its own clock regardless of how the operator feels. Any fixed calendar does this; the planetary one is merely unarguable, since you cannot negotiate with an ephemeris.

To treat the multiplier as measured rather than chosen, run the falsification: record the dial **before** the operation, never after; accumulate at least 20 operations; split into high-dial and low-dial windows; compare the **medians** of `A`, medians because `A` is a quotient with a long tail. If they do not separate, set the multiplier to 1.0, keep the calendar for its scheduling value, and log the null. Then name the confound, which is almost certainly present: an operator who believes the timing is favourable casts with more conviction, raising `^1` Mind, raising η, lowering `A` on its own. The dial and the operator's state are not separable in this design.

---

## The Full CCDL Listing — CCB-CAL

```cas
board ccb_cal {                           // CCB-CAL — the calibration bench
    input:  op_log;                       // one row per operation: two clocks, two degrees
    output: next_op_spec;

    node practice_rail: ^5^P_{F7}|T;      // Female: accumulated practice — bias, never driven

    // ---- S1  INTAKE ----
    node clocked_op: ^7^C_{F6}|E;         // Rhythm: the operation, start to finish
    node arrival:    ^8^C_{F2}|E;         // Above/Cause: the event that arrives after
    node recalled:   ^9^C_{F2}|A;         // Below/Effect: the desire brought back to Mind

    // ---- S2  QUANTIZER ----
    filter q_op:   Filter< in=clocked_op, out=t_op,   type=quantize, grid=5.0 >;
    filter q_conf: Filter< in=recalled,   out=t_conf, type=quantize, grid=5.0 >;

    // ---- S3  HORIZON GATE ----
    fuse f_horizon: Fuse< path=arrival, threshold=1440.0, action=no_read >;

    // ---- S4  RATIO ----
    node eta: ^6^E_{F2}|A;                          // Male: the reading decomposed
    resistor r_tau: Resistor< path=eta, R=3.0 >;    // tau = 1/3 as a fixed divider
    node requirement: ^4^E_{F5}|A;                  // Vibration: A = 3/eta

    // ---- S5  BAND GUARD ----
    monitor m_band: Monitor< signal=eta, limit=[0.333, 3.000],
                             action_on_violation=OUT_OF_BAND >;

    // ---- S6  CAMPAIGN LEDGER ----
    node convergence: ^4^E_{F5}|A;                  // rho = A_next / A_current
    filter f_ledger: Filter< in=convergence, out=trend, type=lowpass, tau=3.0 >;

    // ---- S7  RE-SPEC FUSE and lawful descent ----
    fuse f_respec: Fuse< path=requirement, threshold=9.0,
                         action=block_until_decomposed >;
    diode d_out: Diode< ^E -> ^O >;

    // ---- S8  SCHEDULE ----
    node cadence: ^7^O_{F6}|E;
    osc o_sched: Oscillator< signal=clocked_op, source=cadence, period=3.0,
                             amplitude=1.0, gate=m_band >;        // period in days

    probe tp1: q_conf;         probe tp2: eta;
    probe tp3: requirement;    probe tp4: f_ledger;
}
```

**S1 — intake.** `^8^C` and `^9^C` sit in one domain deliberately. The confirming event happens in the world, `^O`; what the bench reads is the *recall* it triggers, and modelling the trigger at `^C` keeps an unlawful `^O → ^C` ascent out of the listing. `^8` here is associative arrival — the thing that brings the desire back to Mind — not an inference.

**S2–S3 — quantizer and horizon.** Both clocks pass through identical grids, so no asymmetry enters the quotient. The horizon threshold carries the 24-hour floor as a literal; a running bench recomputes it as 3× the rolling median and holds the floor underneath. `action=no_read`, not a large number, because a confirmation past the horizon is base rate.

**S4–S5 — ratio and band guard.** Under CAS-Ohm (Chapter 4.2) flow through a fixed resistance is drive divided by resistance, so the constant is structurally a fixed divider in the readout path — a unit convention realized as a component, which is the honest way to draw it. `Monitor` is a two-threshold comparator: OUT-OF-BAND-LOW routes to the re-spec fuse, OUT-OF-BAND-HIGH terminates calibration.

**S6–S8 — ledger, fuse, schedule.** The lowpass over three operations is why one bad reading cannot redirect a campaign while a genuine trend still passes. `block_until_decomposed` names the only lawful path past the fuse — §23.3 or §23.4 — with invariant S4 stopping that becoming a loophole. `D1` enforces descent from the Evaluative readout into the Operational next-cast spec, and the oscillator is gated by the band guard, so the schedule stops firing the moment the reading leaves the readable window.

## Parameter and BOM Table

Every value is a design choice made in this book, not a measurement.

| Ref | Setting | Why | Failure at other values |
|---|---|---|---|
| FLT1/2 quantizer | grid = 5 min | Finer than `^4` bins, coarser than noticing | 1 min: coprime blow-up. 30 min: overdrive reads ordinary |
| F1 horizon fuse | 3 × median, floor 24 h | Passes slow circuits, excludes base rate | Short: live circuits declared dead. Long: all "confirms" |
| R1 fixed resistor | R = 3.0 Ω_c | Realizes `τ = 1/3` as a divider | Rescales every entry, changes no comparison |
| M1 band guard | η ∈ [0.333, 3.000] | Maps to `A` ∈ [1, 9], the readable window | No lower bound: re-spec reads as amplifier work |
| Amplifier ceiling | β ≤ 4.0, one step per op | Chapter 3.3 device range | `A` as β specifies a device that does not exist |
| F2 re-spec fuse | `A` = 9 | Head of a geometric series | Higher: unconvergeable campaigns stay open |
| FLT3 ledger lowpass | τ = 3 operations | Minimum for a believable trend | 1 op: one bad clock redirects the campaign |
| Convergence | `ρ` ≤ 0.6 | Reaches DRIVE in one step from 9 | `ρ` ≥ 1.0 sustained is divergence |
| Coupling `k` | 0.05 / 0.15 / 0.35 / 0.60 | Set by shared Drive and symbols (§9.3) | Ignored: campaigns collapse together |
| Concurrency | `k(N − 1)` ≤ 0.3 | Holds derating ≥ 0.7 | Past 0.5 the model is invalid — shed |
| OSC1 schedule | period = 72 h | One horizon plus `^5` recharge (§7.3) | Shorter: confirmations unattributable |
| Timing dial | 1.0 | No mechanism claimed (§23.5) | As measured: confounded with `^1` Mind |
