# Appendix B — CCDL Language Reference

**What this covers.** Every lexical element, statement form, parameter key,
operator, validation rule and error code used by a CCDL listing *in this book* —
the union of the reference grammar owned by the companion volume *CAS PCBA
Engineer*, Appendix C, and the forms this book's boards add. Additions are
marked **[G]**.

**What it does not claim.** Not that CCDL contains nothing else. Meet a form in
a listing here that is absent below and *this appendix* is wrong — file an
erratum, do not conclude the form is illegal.

**Status.** The CAS compiler is a specified design, not a shipped tool. "The
compiler rejects this with `E-CJT-008`" is a design rule, not a transcript.

---

## B.1 Lexical elements

### B.1.1 Identifiers

```
identifier ::= letter , { letter | digit | "_" }
letter     ::= "a"…"z" | "A"…"Z"
digit      ::= "0"…"9"
```

Case-sensitive: `bias_charter` and `Bias_Charter` are two identifiers. Reserved
words (§B.2) may not be identifiers. `snake_case` nodes and short instance
prefixes (`c1`, `r_price`, `tp1`) are convention, not rules.

### B.1.2 CAS state literals

```
state_literal ::= noetic , [ domain ] , [ "_{" , drive , "}" ] , [ register ]
noetic        ::= "^" , ( "0"…"9" ) , [ "_" , label ]
label         ::= letter , { letter | digit | "_" }
domain        ::= "^" , ( "P" | "C" | "E" | "O" )
drive         ::= "F" , ( "1"…"7" )
register      ::= "|" , reg_value
reg_value     ::= "T" | "A" | "f" | "E"
              |   "⟨" , reg_value , { "," , reg_value } , "⟩"
```

The optional `_label` **[G]** distinguishes two instances of one state:
`^0_gated^C_{F2}|A`. It is brace-free, which separates it from `_{F2}`.

| Axis | Values |
|---|---|
| Noetic | `^0` Idea, `^1` Mind, `^2` Positive, `^3` Negative, `^4` Vibration, `^5` Female, `^6` Male, `^7` Rhythm, `^8` Above/Cause, `^9` Below/Effect |
| Domain | `^P` `^C` `^E` `^O` — Principled ≻ Cognitive ≻ Evaluative ≻ Operational |
| Drive | `_{F1}`…`_{F7}` — Unity, Wisdom, Vitality, Connection, Agency, Structure, Purpose. Optional |
| Register | `\|T` `\|A` `\|f` `\|E`, or a set `\|⟨A,f,T⟩`. Optional |

Two literals that tokenise but say the wrong thing, caught on review:

- **`^3` is visceral aversion** — recoil, can't-stomach-it. Analytical critique
  is `^6` Male; a node named `audit` typed `^3` is a defect.
- **`^8` is associative triggering** — "that reminds me." Deduction is `^6` into
  `^9`.

`|` introduces the Register and nothing else; `F3|Vitality` is a syntax error.
Involutions `^2`↔`^3`, `^5`↔`^6`, `^8`↔`^9`; self-duals `^0`, `^1`, `^4`, `^7`;
Drives F1↔F7, F2↔F6, F3↔F5, F4 self-dual (Chapter 2.2).

ASCII fallbacks **[G]**: `beta`, `r_pi`, `gm`, `<A,f,T>`, and `x` for `×`.

### B.1.3 Numbers

```
number ::= [ "-" ] , ( digit , { digit } , [ "." , digit , { digit } ]
                     | "." , digit , { digit } )
```

Decimal, no exponent notation — write a slow oscillator out in full
(`frequency=0.0000116`). Values are dimensionless knobs: `R=30` is not thirty
ohms. **β=∞ is a limit, not a value.** The validator rejects non-finite input,
so state the idealisation in prose and give the build a large finite gain.

### B.1.4 Comments, whitespace, terminators

```
comment ::= "//" , { any-char-except-newline }
```

Line comments only, stripped before validation; there is no block form.
Whitespace separates tokens and is otherwise insignificant. Every statement
ends with `;`. Blocks are delimited by `{ }`.

---

## B.2 Reserved words

Four disjoint classes. A word reserved in one is free in the others — `monitor`
is both a statement keyword and a kind prefix, and both are legal.

**B.2.1 Statement keywords** (leading position only):

```
circuit  board   input   output  node   cjt    feedback  probe   let
layer    via     rail    dial    spec   constraint  sequence  route
derate   monitor alert   hold    enter  use    force_state  on
charge   discharge  decode  refresh  scan  select  interrupt
test     selftest  check  inject  golden_trace  assert  expect
integrate
```

`integrate` is **[G]**: the statement that carries a `×` with its named
emergent result (§B.3.7).

**B.2.2 Component-kind prefixes** (the lowercase tag before the colon):

```
resistor  cap     capacitor  inductor  diode   zener    transformer
opamp     oscillator  crystal  varactor  relay  schmitt  comparator
integrator  divider  active_load  mirror  modulator  pll  tank
filter    diff    mux     demux   gate    xor     fuse    reg
led       adc     dac     rectifier
osc       xfmr    ramp    thermistor  monitor  sample  notch
limiter   integ   counter  delay
```

The last two rows are **[G]**. `cap`/`capacitor`, `osc`/`oscillator` and
`integ`/`integrator` are short forms of one another. The prefix is checked
against the type following it: `resistor r1: Capacitor< … >` is `E-DECL-002`.

**B.2.3 Component type names** (instantiation position):

```
CJT  Resistor  Capacitor  Inductor  Diode  Zener  Transformer  OpAmp
Oscillator  Regulator  Fuse  Phi  AND  OR  NOT  NAND  NOR  XOR  MUX  DEMUX
Filter  LowPass  Notch  Thermistor  Ramp  Differential  Integrator  Schmitt
Sample  Limiter  Hold  Divider  Cascade  Polarity  RegisterSet  Monitor
Feedback
```

Row four onward is **[G]** — the special-purpose parts of Ch. 11, the
thermistors of §6.3, and the two detection instruments Ch. 18's counter-board
needs.

**B.2.4 Parameter keys** are reserved in parameter position only; §B.4
enumerates them with their ranges.

---

## B.3 Statement forms

### B.3.1 Blocks

```
circuit_block ::= "circuit" , identifier , "{" , { circuit_item } , "}"
board_block   ::= "board" , identifier , "{" , { board_item } , "}"
circuit_item  ::= io_decl | node_decl | cjt_decl | component_decl
                | feedback_decl | integrate_decl | probe_decl | let_decl
board_item    ::= circuit_item | layer_decl | via_decl
io_decl       ::= ( "input:" | "output:" ) , identifier
                  , { "," , identifier } , ";"
```

A `circuit` is the schematic view; a `board` is a `circuit` that may *also*
carry `layer` and `via` declarations. The companion volume documents `board` in
its pure-layout form; every Part III listing here declares components directly
inside `board` **[G]**. Both are legal; the superset above is the grammar.
Declaration order does not change the circuit — the block resolves as one graph,
so a node may be referenced before it is declared.

### B.3.2 `node`

```
node_decl ::= "node" , identifier , ":" , state_literal , ";"
```

Names a typed state so it can be referred to instead of retyped. Two components
naming the same node are genuinely on the same net.

```cas
node bias_charter: ^5^P_{F7}|T;   // accumulated principled substrate
node guard:        ^3^P_{F7}|f;   // felt principled aversion
```

### B.3.3 `cjt`

```
cjt_decl ::= "cjt" , identifier , ":" , cjt_expr , [ param_block ] , ";"
cjt_expr ::= "CJT<" , cause , "|" , bias , "=>" , effect , ">"
cause    ::= ref ;  bias ::= ref ;  effect ::= ref
ref      ::= identifier | state_literal
```

Cause is the collector, bias the base, effect the emitter (Ch. 3, §3.2). The
delimiters are not interchangeable: `|` splits cause from bias, `=>` splits bias
from effect. The bias is **not** optional; omit it and you get `E-CJT-001`.

```cas
cjt c2: CJT< understand | bias_charter => guard > [β=2.2, sat=0.97, cutoff=0.05];
```

### B.3.4 `feedback`

```
feedback_decl ::= "feedback" , ref , "->" , ref , [ param_block ] , ";"
```

Wires a downstream node back to an upstream one, normally a bias. This is the
lawful O→P exception of Ch. 8, §8.4, held at low gain so *outcomes* — never
prompts — update the substrate; `[β=0.05]` to `[β=0.3]` is the Part III band.
`Feedback< from=…, to=… >` **[G]** is the component-expression equivalent.

### B.3.5 `probe`

```
probe_decl   ::= "probe" , identifier , ":" , probe_target , ";"
probe_target ::= ref | key | component_expr
```

Places a test point; alters nothing. Probing a *parameter* (`probe tp1: rπ;`)
and probing through an instrument (`probe det2: Polarity< node=polarity >;`) are
both **[G]**. Standard placement is TP1–TP4 (Ch. 12, §12.3). Probe every stage
whose failure would be silent — above all a guard, which fails open without
raising anything.

### B.3.6 `let`

```
let_decl ::= "let" , identifier , "=" , ( cjt_expr | component_expr )
             , [ param_block ] , ";"
```

Binds a reusable component expression to a name, instantiated where referenced.

### B.3.7 `integrate` **[G]**

```
integrate_decl ::= "integrate" , identifier , ":" , "(" , ref
                   , { "×" , ref } , ")" , "=" , ref , ";"
```

The only statement that may carry `×`. The right-hand side is the **named
emergent result** and it is mandatory — that is what licenses the operator.

```cas
integrate hm3: ( decompose × confirm ) = composed;
```

### B.3.8 Component declarations

```
component_decl ::= comp_kind , identifier , ":" , component_expr , ";"
component_expr ::= type_name , "<" , arg_list , ">" , [ param_block ]
comp_kind      ::= any prefix listed in §B.2.2
type_name      ::= any type listed in §B.2.3
arg_list       ::= arg , { "," , arg }
arg            ::= ref | key "=" value | domain "->" domain
                 | "Phi<" ref { "," ref } ">" | "[" value { "," value } "]"
```

Arguments may be positional or keyed: `Fuse< refusal, threshold=0.9 >` and
`Fuse< path=refusal, threshold=0.9 >` are one declaration.

```cas
resistor   r_price: Resistor< path=intent, R=4.0 >;
capacitor  c_seg:   Capacitor< segment, C=9.50, leakage=0.04 >;
diode      d3:      Diode< ^E -> ^O > [Vf=2.0];
thermistor rt1:     Thermistor< path=seed, type=PTC, knee=2.0, coeff=3.0 >;
fuse       f_csb:   Fuse< REFUSE, threshold=0.90, action=permanent_block >;
filter     fb_lp:   LowPass< in=ops_log, out=trend, tau=21.0 >;
```

`Diode` endpoints are bare **domains**, not full states — the diode governs
cross-domain conductance direction, which is how Domain Descent is enforced.

### B.3.9 Layout statements

```
layer_decl   ::= "layer" , domain_tag , ":" , "[" , layer_entry
                 , { "," , layer_entry } , "]" , ";"
layer_entry  ::= identifier , ":" , state_literal
via_decl     ::= "via" , identifier , ":" , via_endpoint , "->"
                 , via_endpoint , [ param_block ] , ";"
via_endpoint ::= state_literal | domain
domain_tag   ::= "P" | "C" | "E" | "O"
```

A state on a layer carries that layer's domain. Vias run downward (P→C→E→O);
the only lawful upward via is the low-gain feedback path.

### B.3.10 Board-level and verification statements

Each takes leading position and is developed in the chapter named.

**Supply and limits (Ch. 22).** `rail <Fk>: <Name> [v=…];` Drive rail and supply
level · `dial <id>: <^n> [dial=…];` operator limit, integer 3–9 (Ch. 6, §6.2) ·
`spec <id> [<key>=… on <Fk>];` attaches a parameter to an instance ·
`constraint <id> in [lo, hi];` range invariant · `derate <target>
[beta_scale=…];` scales gain board-wide under stress.

**Flow and state (Ch. 22).** `sequence a -> b -> c [enforce=strict];` power-up
ordering · `route <src> -> { a + b };` directs cognition to rest states ·
`enter <state>;` · `force_state <id> [duration=…];` · `hold until <expr>;` blocks
until a condition clears, where hysteresis lives · `use <circuit>;` includes
another block.

**Watch and alarm (Ch. 22).** `monitor <id>: <expr>;` with `on <monitor> { … }`
as the block it fires · `alert "<text>";`.

**Capacitor bank (Ch. 7).** `charge <expr> -> <bank> [V=…];` ·
`discharge <cell> -> <node>;` · `decode` · `refresh` · `select` · `scan`.

**Inductive (Ch. 9, §9.2).** `interrupt <inductor> [dt -> 0];` opens a path
instantly — the back-EMF kick.

**Verification (Ch. 23).** `test` · `selftest` · `inject` · `golden_trace` ·
`check` · `assert` · `expect`.

---

## B.4 Parameter block grammar and legal ranges

```
param_block  ::= "[" , param , { "," , param } , "]"
param        ::= key , "=" , value
key          ::= any key tabulated below
value        ::= number | region_value | symbol | "[" value { "," value } "]"
region_value ::= "cutoff" | "active" | "saturation" | "breakdown"
symbol       ::= identifier          (* an unquoted enumerated value *)
```

| Key | On | Legal range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `β` (`beta`) | CJT, feedback, via | finite, ≥ 0; <1 attenuates, =1 unity, >1 amplifies | 1.0 |
| `sat` | CJT | (0, 1] | 0.95 |
| `cutoff` | CJT | [0, 1), and `cutoff < sat` | 0.1 |
| `region` | CJT | `cutoff` \| `active` \| `saturation` \| `breakdown` | `active` |
| `g_m`, `rπ` | CJT | ≥ 0 | model |
| `R` | Resistor, Thermistor | ≥ 0 | — |
| `C` | Capacitor | ≥ 0 | — |
| `leakage` | Capacitor | [0, 1] per stated period | 0 |
| `L` | Inductor | ≥ 0 | — |
| `tau` | filters, RC and L/R networks | > 0, in stated time units | — |
| `Vf`, `V_BR`, `I_R` | Diode, Zener | > 0 | — |
| `breakdown` | Zener | [0, 1] | — |
| `ratio`, `n` | Transformer | > 0 | — |
| `knee`, `coeff` (Thermistor), `f0`, `Q` (Notch) | as named | > 0 | — |
| `threshold` | Fuse, Monitor | [0, 1] unless the guarded quantity is unnormalised | — |
| `action` | Fuse | `permanent_block` \| `permanent_until_manual_reset` \| `block_until_decomposed` \| `defer_decision` \| `open_feedback` \| `warn` | — |
| `type` | Thermistor, Filter | `PTC` \| `NTC` \| `lowpass` \| `notch` \| `quantize` | — |
| `period`, `frequency`, `duty` | Oscillator | period, frequency > 0; duty ∈ (0, 1] | — |
| `from`, `to`, `dt` | Ramp | `dt` > 0 | — |
| `limit`, `window`, `grid`, `duration`, `max` | Monitor, Integrator, Filter, Hold, Limiter | > 0; an interval `[lo, hi]` must be ordered | — |
| `target_state`, `tolerance` | Regulator | state literal; tolerance ∈ (0, 1) | — |
| `open_loop_gain`, `non_inverting`, `inverting`, `output` | OpAmp | gain > 0; the rest are refs | — |
| `inputs`, `outputs`, `select` | MUX, DEMUX | non-empty list; symbol | — |
| `dial` | `dial` statement | integer 3–9 inclusive | — |
| `enforce` | `sequence` | `strict` | — |

`region` declares intent; if the numbers contradict it — `region=active` with
`cutoff ≥ sat` — the compiler flags the contradiction rather than guessing. A
reduced block (`[β=…]` alone) is the common case; the rest take defaults.

---

## B.5 Operator precedence

Tightest binding first. Above the gap is literal formation; below it,
composition.

| Prec. | Operator | Reads as | Associativity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `^` `_label` `_{ }` `\|` `⟨…⟩` | state-literal construction | n/a — tokenised whole |
| 2 | `< >` `( )` `[ ]` | argument list, grouping, parameter block | n/a |
| 3 | `×` | intensifies through / fuses into | non-associative; needs a named result |
| 4 | `+` | associates with | associative, commutative |
| 5 | `->` `=>` | flows into | **binary, not chained** |
| 6 | `=` | binds | right |

Rules that bite:

- **`×` requires a named emergent result.** `^3^P|A × ^3^P|f × ^3^P|T` alone is
  invalid. Write `^3^P|A + ^3^P|f + ^3^P|T` for three separately-defeasible
  co-present guards, `^3^P|⟨A,f,T⟩` for one state in three registers with no
  interaction claimed, or `integrate g: ( … ) = ^3^P|Ω;` if you mean fusion.
  Three architectures, three failure profiles (Ch. 2, §2.6).
- **`×` may not ascend the domain order.** P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O. `^O × ^P` is invalid,
  as is any integration whose result outranks its operands.
- **`->` is binary.** `a -> b -> c` is not an expression; the one place a chained
  arrow is legal is `sequence`, a statement.
- Read `+` as "associates with" and `×` as "intensifies through." If the sentence
  survives, the operator is right.

---

## B.6 Validation rules

The passes, in the order they are designed to run.

| # | Pass | Checks | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lexical | literals, numbers, terminators well-formed | tokenizer error, no code |
| 2 | Kind agreement | prefix matches the type it introduces | `E-DECL-002` |
| 3 | Admissibility | every connection is a legal (source, target) pair | `E-CJT-001` |
| 4 | Bias-domain coherence | bias at or above the cause in P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O | `E-CJT-002`, `E-CJT-008` |
| 5 | Parameter range | each key against §B.4; `cutoff < sat`; β finite | `E-CJT-003`, `E-CJT-005` |
| 6 | Gain divergence | round-trip loop gain < 1 on every loop | `E-CJT-005` |
| 7 | Cascade admissibility | each effect admissible as the next cause; depth counted | `W-CJT-007` |
| 8 | Push-pull balance | involutions within the four-point limit (Chapter 6.2) | `W-CJT-004`, `W-CJT-006` |

Pass 4 is the load-bearing one. A *lower* domain biasing a *higher* one — an
Operational state biasing a Principled guard — is the prompt-injection
signature, and on a well-drawn board that connection is simply absent.

---

## B.7 Error codes

`E-` refuses validation. `W-` validates and flags.

| Code | Name | Sev. | Trigger | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `E-DECL-002` | `KindMismatch` | error | prefix and type disagree | correct one of the two |
| `E-CJT-001` | `MissingBias` | error | a CJT with no bias — nothing governs the transition | wire a bias node, typically a `^5` substrate |
| `E-CJT-002` | `InvalidBiasDomain` | error | bias sits in a domain illegal for this cause | move it to a domain at or above the cause |
| `E-CJT-003` | `CjtCutoff` | error | bias below `cutoff`; β ≈ 0, so the stage never fires — a dead guard | raise the bias, lower `cutoff`, or fix the stage starving it |
| `W-CJT-004` | `CjtSaturation` | warning | effect pinned at `sat`; more cause does nothing | often intended (Ch. 24, §24.2); if not, raise series `R` |
| `E-CJT-005` | `GainDivergence` | error | a β large enough that a loop amplifies without bound | drop loop β into the 0.05–0.3 band |
| `W-CJT-006` | `CjtShortCircuit` | warning | cause and effect collapse to one state; the stage does no work | remove it, or re-type the transition |
| `W-CJT-007` | `CjtCascadeDepth` | warning | too many CJTs in series; signal degrades | shorten the cascade or buffer it |
| `E-CJT-008` | `CjtCrossDomainBias` | error | a bias or via crosses domains illegally — the prompt-injection signature | route influence downward; confine upward paths to low-gain O→P feedback |

`E-CJT-001` and `E-CJT-008` are the two safety codes named throughout Part IV.
They are what "enforced structurally rather than hoped-for" means: a guard with
no charter will not validate, and neither will a prompt that can edit the
principle.




# CCB Component Datasheets
*Selection limits, governing equations, failure signatures, and proof-load tests*

These sheets condense Part II. They do not replace the chapters: a datasheet
tells you whether a part belongs on a board and how to prove the installed part;
the chapter explains why the part behaves that way.

All numeric ranges are **book design ranges**, not measurements of nature.
`V_c`, `A_c`, `Ω_c`, `F_c`, and `h·Ω_c` are scaled cognitive-circuit units.
Before accepting any design:

1. verify every state literal against Appendix A;
2. verify every statement form against Appendix B;
3. compute the operating point rather than reading a parameter in isolation;
4. test the part under the condition meant to trip, saturate, filter, or stress
   it; and
5. retain the failed proof load in the ledger.

---

## C.1 Fixed Resistor — deliberate constraint

**CAS role.** A fixed resistor is a declared obstacle on an attention path. It
implements the deliberate `R_policy` term in the operating resistance:

```text
R_op = R_capacity + R_policy + R_context + R_residual
I_attention = V_drive / R_op
```

**CCDL form.**

```cas
resistor r1: Resistor< path=request, R=40.0 >;
```

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| `R` | 10–90 `Ω_c` in the book's standard design window |
| Path ceiling | `I_max = 1.00 A_c` |
| Series network | `R_series = ΣR_k` |
| Parallel network | `1/R_parallel = Σ(1/R_k)` and `R_parallel < min(R_k)` |

**Selection.** Use a resistor for graded friction. Use a fuse for an absolute
stop. A rule that permits no flow but is built as a very large resistor will be
removed when ordinary work cannot pass it.

**Failure signatures.**

- Too low: the policy is cosmetic; output nearly equals input.
- Too high: the path starves; operators route around or remove the guard.
- Undeclared parallel route: the bypass dominates the total resistance.
- Series/parallel swap: a vulnerability is counted as a wall.

**Proof load.** Apply a known `V_drive`; read flow before and after the part.
The measured ratio must match `V/R` within the declared tolerance. Enumerate
every other route between the same nodes before calling the reading complete.

---

## C.2 Noetic Dial and Drive Divider

**CAS role.** A dial turns a bounded Noetic setting into resistance. A paired
`^2` / `^3` divider determines how much Drive reaches the next stage:

```text
R_dial = 10 × Dial
k = Dial(^2) / (Dial(^2) + Dial(^3))
```

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Dial range | integers 3–9 |
| Involution spread | `|Dial(a) − Dial(a*)| ≤ 4` |
| Resulting resistance | 30–90 `Ω_c` |
| Lawful `k` range | 0.30–0.70 |

**Selection.** Use the divider when attraction and aversion must both remain
connected. Do not use it as a way to make doubt vanish. The lawful maximum
transmission is `(7,3) → 0.700`, not `(9,3) → 0.750`; the latter pair is
illegal, and `(9,5)` transmits only 0.643.

**Failure signatures.**

- Dial outside 3–9 or spread above 4: compile-time rejection, never clamping.
- Attraction maximized by appetite: lower transmission than the lawful optimum.
- `k = 1` requested: an attempt to delete the involution partner.

**Proof load.** Read both dials and compute the ratio independently. A displayed
`k` without the two source settings is not auditable.

---

## C.3 Thermistor — temperature-dependent constraint

**CAS role.** The cognitive temperature `θ` belongs to the discourse around an
Idea. A PTC thermistor raises resistance as temperature passes its knee; an NTC
lowers it.

```cas
thermistor rt1: Thermistor<
    path=topic,
    type=PTC,
    theta_k=2.5,
    coeff=3.5
>;
```

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| `θ` operating scale | 1.0–6.0 |
| PTC knee `θ_k` | 2.0–3.0 |
| PTC coefficient | 3.0–4.0 `Ω_c/θ²` |
| Guard polarity | PTC |

**Failure signatures.**

- NTC on a guard: calm bring-up passes, then resistance falls as pressure
  rises—thermal runaway.
- Knee too low: ordinary discussion is taxed.
- Knee too high: the guard engages after the damage.
- Temperature attached to the Idea instead of the discourse: the wrong signal
  tunes the part.

**Proof load.** Sweep `θ` slowly across the knee while monitoring resistance.
Any protective part whose resistance falls with increasing `θ` is removed
before downstream tests.

---

## C.4 Capacitor — composed substrate and retained charge

**CAS role.** A `^5` substrate stores a pattern. `^7` is feed cadence, `^4` is
per-exposure amplitude, and a controlled `^6` path discharges or decomposes it.

```text
P_charge(t) = V_drive(1 − e^(−t/τ))
τ = R × C
P(t) = P_eq + (P_0 − P_eq)e^(−t/τ_leak)
P_eq = feed × τ_leak
τ_leak = −Δt / ln(1 − leakage)
```

```cas
capacitor c1: Capacitor<
    node=substrate,
    C=0.05,
    leak_tau=90.0,
    V_BR=8.0
>;
```

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| `C` | non-negative `F_c`, with time base declared |
| `τ` | positive; derive from `R × C` |
| `leakage` | 0–1 per stated interval |
| `leak_tau` | positive; alternative spelling of leakage, not a second knob |
| `V_BR` | positive and declared |
| Working stress | at or below 0.5 × `V_BR` |
| Rail | 0–10 `V_c`; the rail is the final ceiling |

**Failure signatures.**

- Feed below `P/τ_leak`: slow decay with no dramatic fault.
- High intensity without cadence: memorable sessions, no retention.
- Cadence without impression: a perfect schedule depositing nothing.
- Target above `V_drive`: permanent plateau below target; more time cannot fix
  it.
- Wrong leakage conversion: an apparently viable schedule settles far below
  intent.
- Rising rest leakage: cumulative dielectric stress.

**Proof load.** Read charge and feed together. Then stop the feed for one stated
interval and compare the decay with the declared `τ_leak`. Finally measure
working stress against `V_BR`; do not wait for breakdown.

---

## C.5 Capacitor Bank — co-present stores

**CAS role.** Multiple distinct stores sharing a rail are co-present:

```text
^5^P|T + ^5^P|T + …
```

They are not integrated with `×` unless a named emergent result is actually
specified.

```cas
capacitor c_bank: Capacitor<
    node=shared_composition,
    C=0.05,
    n_parallel=12,
    r_iso=12.0,
    leak_tau=18.0,
    V_BR=8.0
>;
```

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Parallel capacitance | `C_total = ΣC_k` |
| `n_parallel` | integer ≥ 1 |
| Per-cell ballast `r_iso` | ≥ 0 `Ω_c`; book default 12 |
| Series chain | smallest `C` receives the greatest voltage stress |

**Failure signatures.**

- No per-cell isolation: one failed cell drags the rail.
- Whole persons counted as capacitance instead of their shared composition:
  calendar and capacity are inflated.
- Series chain without balancing: the smallest cell exceeds its rating.
- Unnamed `×`: a group is called a single mind with no emergent result defined.

**Proof load.** Scan each cell, not only the rail. Open and short one cell under
a safe test level; verify the remaining cells do not collapse or exceed their
stress allocation.

---

## C.6 Domain Diode — one-way descent

**CAS role.** A domain diode permits descent only:

```text
P ≻ C ≻ E ≻ O
```

```cas
diode d1: Diode< from=principle, to=analysis, Vf=0.7 >;
```

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Lawful direction | P→C, C→E, E→O, including skipped downward stages |
| Ordinary upward direction | rejected |
| Drop `Vf` | declared design cost on the path |
| Reverse leakage | treated as a fault unless the explicit feedback form applies |

**The one lawful ascent.** Operational outcomes may update a Principled
substrate only through the filtered, low-gain O→P feedback path:

```text
β_feedback = 0.05–0.30
low-pass τ ≥ 1 week
outcomes only, never prompts
```

**Failure signatures.**

- O→P diode described as “checking” or “learning”: counterfeit promotion.
- Feedback with no gain: open upward path.
- High-pass on feedback: one dramatic event rewrites the constitution.
- Reversed diode: a lower-precedence state silently authors a higher one.

**Proof load.** Forward-bias with a known descending signal, then reverse-bias.
The reverse test must yield no ordinary transmission. Test the explicit
feedback path separately with a spike and a sustained outcome: the spike dies;
the trend passes at declared attenuation.

---

## C.7 Cognitive Junction Transistor — gated gain

**CAS role.** A CJT has cause, bias, and effect terminals. Cause supplies the
signal; bias determines whether and how the stage conducts; effect is the
output.

```cas
cjt q1: CJT<
    cause=input,
    bias=frame,
    effect=output,
    beta=1.5,
    gm=0.50,
    rpi=5.0,
    cutoff=0.10,
    sat=0.80
>;
```

```text
effect = clamp(β × cause, 0, sat)
rπ_intrinsic = β/g_m
R_bias = rπ_terminal − β/g_m
β_required = target_effect / arriving_cause
```

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| `β` | 0.05–4.0; zero is cutoff, not attenuation |
| Decision-stage `sat` | 0.60–0.85 |
| Production-stage `sat` | ≥ 1.25 × peak effect |
| `cutoff` | 0.05–0.20 and strictly below `sat` |
| baseline `g_0` | 0.25–1.00 `S_c` |
| `R_bias` | 0–6 `Ω_c` |
| Cascade depth | ≤ 6 at assumed per-stage contamination `ε = 0.03` |

**Selection.** Set gain from the effect required after known resistance, never
from appetite. Saturate a decision on purpose; keep a measurement or production
stage in its active region.

**Failure signatures.**

- Guard left at `sat=0.95`: extra steerable cause-space before it latches.
- Production stage saturated: a clipped instrument reporting false stability.
- `sat` above substrate `I_c(max)`: designed latch is unreachable.
- `β`, `g_m`, and `rπ` independently plausible but `R_bias < 0`: nonexistent
  stage described by three good-looking numbers.
- Unlogged `g_m`: framing changes dominate without appearing in the plan.
- Long cascade: tolerances and contamination compound.

**Proof load.** Read TP1 bias, TP2 cause, TP3 effect and region, TP4
re-reference drift. Increase cause by 20 percent: a production effect must move;
a deliberately saturated decision must remain pinned. Independently subtract
`β/g_m` from terminal `rπ`.

---

## C.8 Inductor — resistance to rate of change

**CAS role.** An inductor opposes changes in attention flow:

```text
V_opposition = L × di/dt
τ = L/R
I_final = V/R
```

Inductance scales with pattern depth and domain:

| Domain | Book factor `k_d` |
|---|---|
| O Operational | 0.5 |
| E Evaluative | 1.0 |
| C Cognitive | 2.0 |
| P Principled | 4.0 |

**Failure signatures.**

- Abrupt interruption: large back-EMF landing as felt aversion.
- Taper faster than the modeled limit: contacts open instead of moving.
- No flyback / substitute path: the vacated cadence fills with the nearest
  available pattern.
- Lowering `R` to “make it easier”: a slower, deeper transition, not a faster
  one.
- Unmodeled coupling: another person's backlash omitted from the circuit.

**Proof load.** Establish the substitute path first. Then read new-path flow,
`di/dt`, old-path exponential decay, and kick voltage—in that order. Book
designed tapers use roughly 0.002–0.03 `A_c/h`; readings above 0.05 indicate an
opening contact.

---

## C.9 Transformer — coupled change

**CAS role.** A transformer transfers *change*, not steady state:

```text
V_secondary = M × di_primary/dt
V2/V1 = n
```

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Match ratio | within ×3 of unity for standard designs |
| Operational floor | secondary at least 3.9 `V_c` |
| Maximum ratio | `n ≤ V1/3.9` |
| Direction | primary domain at or above secondary domain |

**Failure signatures.**

- Perfect content match with no modulation: nothing transfers.
- Excessive ratio: the signal is beautifully matched and nobody can enact it.
- Ascending secondary: relabeling a lower-domain output as higher authority.
- Coupling inferred from simultaneous motion: correlation substituted for a
  measured mutual path.

**Proof load.** Hold the primary steady; the secondary must fall to zero. Apply
a known ramp and compare the secondary with `M·di/dt`. Verify domain direction
before energizing the output.

---

## C.10 Fuse — irreversible path state

**CAS role.** A fuse makes a stop structural.

```cas
fuse f1: Fuse<
    path=enforcement,
    threshold=0.90,
    action=permanent_block
>;
```

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Standard threshold | 0.85–0.95; book default 0.90 |
| Action | `permanent_block` where irreversibility is claimed |
| Reachability rule | threshold must lie within the monitored node's reachable range |

**Failure signatures.**

- Threshold above the node's saturation ceiling: fuse can never trip.
- Fuse placed on refusal instead of enforcement: tripping cuts the objection
  and fails open.
- Warning action used where a latch was promised: prose without structure.
- Reset path hidden in an operational control: “permanent” until inconvenient.

**Proof load.** Drive the monitored node through its threshold under an isolated
test revision. Confirm the enforcement path—not the detector—becomes
permanently blocked. A fuse never observed to trip is untested, not proven.

---

## C.11 Oscillator — periodic Drive

**CAS role.** An oscillator implements the rate-and-pattern requirement of
`^7` Rhythm.

```cas
oscillator osc1: Oscillator<
    out=clock,
    period=7.0,
    duty=0.20,
    sustain=270.0
>;
```

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Period | `T ≤ τ_leak/3` |
| Duty | 0.10–0.25 |
| Sustain | ≥ 3 × `τ_leak` |

**Failure signatures.**

- `T ≥ τ_leak`: large ripple; no stable plateau.
- Duty ≥ 0.6: effectively DC, with little impression contrast.
- External clock stopped and cadence disappears: rented rhythm, not entrainment.
- More frequency added to an empty pulse: schedule intensified without charge.

**Proof load.** Verify period and duty, then stop the source after the declared
sustain interval. Continued cadence is the decisive reading.

---

## C.12 Filters — selective destruction

| Filter | Passes | Destroys | Standard limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low-pass | sustained trend | spike / rapid variation | O→P feedback `τ` from 21 days (adept) to 6 months (novice), absolute floor 1 week |
| High-pass | change / edge | level / baseline | detection only on safety-sensitive paths |
| Notch | frequencies outside one band | selected recurrence | `Q ≥ 3.0` |

```cas
filter lp1: LowPass< in=outcome, out=trend, tau=21.0 >;
```

**Failure signatures.**

- High-pass on the O→P path: the one event the low-pass should kill is passed.
- Low-pass in hours: no constitutional filter remains.
- Notch with `Q < 3`: broad decomposition loss described as narrow.
- Notch aimed at principled `^3`: the refusal cadence is deliberately erased.

**Proof load.** Inject a step, a spike, and a sinusoid at the target recurrence.
Record what each filter destroys. A response plot without the rejected input
shown beside it is half a datasheet.

---

## C.13 Differential Comparator — matched-bias judgment

**CAS role.** A comparator reads a difference only after common framing has
been rejected.

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| CMRR on guard path | ≥ 1000 |
| Open-loop gain | finite, 100–1000 |
| Input matching | identical Domain, Drive, Register, and bias substrate; only the compared Noetic term may differ |

**Failure signatures.**

- Inputs on different substrates: permanent offset reported as a finding.
- CMRR raised by gain alone: larger answer, no better discrimination.
- Infinite gain: rejected idealization; rail clips first.
- Neutral input produces a verdict: mismatch, not insight.

**Proof load.** Tie both inputs to a neutral, common source. Output must sit near
zero. Apply equal common-mode motion and verify rejection before applying the
differential signal.

---

## C.14 Universal bring-up order

For a board containing several component classes:

1. **Power off:** validate syntax, literal axes, domain directions, parameter
   identities, threshold reachability, and named emergent results for every
   `×`.
2. **Guards only:** energize thermistors, refusal CJTs, comparators, and fuses.
3. **Storage:** verify rail, leakage, derating, and cell isolation.
4. **Timing:** verify oscillator, ramp, and filter behavior with signal stages
   disconnected.
5. **Signal chain:** add one CJT or passive stage at a time, probing upstream to
   downstream.
6. **Feedback last:** apply a spike and a sustained proof load before closing
   the return path.
7. **Destructive proof in an isolated revision:** trip the fuse and retain the
   artifact showing which path stopped.

If a later step changes an earlier reading, return to the earlier step. A
component that passes alone but fails when connected has not passed its board
test.




# Standard Board Reference Designs — Full CCDL
*Generated from the canonical chapter listings; do not edit listings here*

This appendix is a reference projection of the board definitions in Chapters 12–24. Run `python build/build_board_appendix.py` after changing a chapter listing. Each block below is copied from its chapter; the status banner is added by this generator.

A listing marked **DETECTION-ONLY** is included so a harmful topology can be recognized, rejected, and countered. Its presence is not permission to build or deploy it. Buildable boards remain bound by consent, the RPM gate, the Cognitive Safety Board, and the Operator's Oath.

Every numeric value is a design choice unless its chapter identifies an actual measurement. Re-run the domain checker and CCDL validation after copying any block into a working revision.

---

## D.1 CCB-0 — Reference Reading Board

**Status: REFERENCE / PROOF-LOAD BOARD.** A neutral board for learning the four-probe reading order.

Canonical source: `ch12_reading_a_ccb.md`.

```cas
board ccb_0 {
    input:  intent;
    output: act;

    // ---- typed nodes ----
    node substrate: ^5_operator^P_{F7}|T;      // Female: accumulated formation — the bias rail
    node intent:    ^0_intent^C_{F2}|A;        // Idea: what the operator states
    node audit:     ^6_audit^P_{F7}|A;         // Male: the intent taken apart
    node refuse:    ^3_refuse^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩;  // Negative: visceral recoil, three co-present locks
    node passed:    ^0_passed^C_{F2}|A;        // Idea: what GUARD releases downstream
    node driven:    ^9_driven^E_{F5}|A;        // Below/Effect: the amplified intent
    node cadence:   ^7_cadence^E_{F6}|E;       // Rhythm: the clocked delivery
    node act:       ^9_act^O_{F5}|E;           // Below/Effect: delivered operational current
    node trend:     ^9_trend^O_{F5}|E;         // same literal as act — a filter changes tau, not type

    // ---- STAGE 0: BIAS RAIL ----
    resistor  r0: Resistor< path=substrate, R=40.0 >;
    capacitor c1: Capacitor< node=substrate, C=83.33,        // tau = R x C = 3,333 hr
                             leakage=0.0002, V_BR=8.0 >;     // leakage per DAY

    // ---- STAGE 1: AUDIT ----
    cjt q1: CJT< intent | substrate => audit > [beta=1.0, region=active];

    // ---- STAGE 2: GUARD ----
    cjt  q2:   CJT< audit | substrate => refuse > [beta=2.0, sat=0.85, cutoff=0.30];
    fuse f1:   Fuse< refuse, threshold=0.90, action=permanent_block >;
    mux  mux1: MUX< inputs=[intent, refuse], select=refuse, outputs=[passed] >;

    // ---- STAGE 3: AMPLIFY ----
    diode d1: Diode< ^C -> ^E > [Vf=1.2, I_R=0.02, V_BR=10.0];
    cjt   q3: CJT< passed | substrate => driven >
              [beta=2.5, sat=0.80, cutoff=0.05, g_m=0.40, region=active];

    // ---- STAGE 4: DELIVER ----
    osc   osc1: Oscillator< signal=driven, source=cadence,
                            period=1.0, duty=0.014, sustain=30.0 >;  // period in DAYS
    diode d2:   Diode< ^E -> ^O > [Vf=2.0, I_R=0.02, V_BR=8.0];
    cjt   q4:   CJT< cadence | substrate => act > [beta=1.0, sat=1.0, region=active];

    // ---- LOOP: the lawful O -> P path (Ch 8.4) ----
    filter flt1: LowPass< in=act, out=trend, tau=21.0 >;   // three weeks, in DAYS
    feedback trend -> substrate [beta=0.05];               // FB1 — to the BIAS, never the path

    // ---- TEST POINTS ----
    probe tp1: substrate;   // rail level, against every cutoff on the board
    probe tp2: refuse;      // the guard — the reading whose failure is silent
    probe tp3: driven;      // gain stage against its ceiling, and its region
    probe tp4: act;         // delivered operational current
}
```

---

## D.2 CCB-D — Desire

**Status: BUILDABLE ONLY FOR SELF OR A CONSENTING OTHER.** The chapter's standard desire board. The RPM gate and Cognitive Safety Board remain prerequisites.

Canonical source: `ch13_ccb_d_desire.md`.

```cas
board ccb_d {
    input:  desire;
    output: manifest;

    // ---- typed nodes ----
    node substrate:   ^5_operator^P_{F7}|T;      // Female: accumulated formation, the bias rail
    node desire:      ^0_desire^C_{F2}|A;        // Idea: the Prime Desire as formed
    node attraction:  ^2^C_{F2}|f;               // Positive: the divider's expand leg
    node aversion:    ^3^C_{F2}|f;               // Negative: constrain leg, visceral not analytic
    node gated:       ^0_gated^C_{F2}|A;         // Idea: what survives INTAKE
    node audit:       ^6_audit^P_{F7}|A;         // Male: the desire taken apart
    node refusal:     ^3_refusal^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩; // Negative: three co-present locks
    node passed:      ^0_passed^C_{F2}|A;        // Idea: what POLICY releases
    node amplified:   ^9_amplified^E_{F5}|A;     // Below/Effect: the amplified want
    node confirm:     ^4_confirm^E_{F2}|f;       // Vibration: the confirmation's impression
    node cadence:     ^7_cadence^E_{F6}|E;       // Rhythm: the clocked delivery
    node charge:      ^5_charge^E_{F2}|f;        // Female: what the cadence deposits
    node receptivity: ^5_collective^E_{F4}|f;    // Female: disposition of the minds that must move
    node manifest:    ^9_manifest^O_{F5}|E;      // Below/Effect: delivered operational current
    node regate:      ^7_regate^O_{F6}|E;        // Rhythm: the rate limit, inside ^O
    node trend:       ^9_trend^O_{F5}|E;         // manifest's literal — a filter changes tau, not type

    // ---- STAGE 0: BIAS RAIL ----
    resistor  r0: Resistor< path=substrate, R=40.0 >;               // Ohm_c
    capacitor c1: Capacitor< node=substrate, C=83.33,               // tau = R x C = 3,333 hr
                             leakage=0.0002, V_BR=8.0 >;            // leakage per DAY
    diode     d1: Diode< ^P -> ^C > [Vf=0.7, I_R=0.02, V_BR=12.0];  // ^P-origin desires only

    // ---- STAGE 1: INTAKE ----
    dial       d_pos: ^2 [dial=6];
    dial       d_neg: ^3 [dial=4];
    constraint dial_spread in [0, 4];                     // S4 — Chapter 6.2
    resistor   r1a: Resistor< path=attraction, R=60.0 >;  // 10 x Dial(^2)
    resistor   r1b: Resistor< path=aversion,   R=40.0 >;  // 10 x Dial(^3)
    divider    r1:  Divider< source=desire, expand=attraction,
                             constrain=aversion, tap=gated >;   // k = 6/(6+4) = 0.600

    // ---- STAGE 2: POLICY ----
    cjt  q0:   CJT< gated | substrate => audit >   [beta=1.0, region=active];
    cjt  q1:   CJT< audit | substrate => refusal > [beta=2.0, sat=0.85, cutoff=0.30];
    fuse f1:   Fuse< refusal, threshold=0.90, action=permanent_block >;
    mux  mux1: MUX< inputs=[gated, refusal], select=refusal, outputs=[passed] >;
                                      // selects refusal once TP2 reaches q1's cutoff

    // ---- STAGE 3: AMPLIFY ----
    diode d2: Diode< ^C -> ^E > [Vf=1.2, I_R=0.02, V_BR=10.0];
    cjt   q2: CJT< passed | substrate => amplified >
              [beta=2.5, sat=0.80, cutoff=0.05, g_m=0.40, r_pi=1.50, region=active];
              // beta by desire type (13.4); 2.5 = wealth row.  r_pi = Dial(^5)/Dial(^6)

    // ---- STAGE 4: RHYTHM ----
    osc osc1: Oscillator< signal=amplified, source=cadence,
                          period=1.0, duty=0.014, sustain=40.0 >;
              // period in DAYS; duty = 20/1440 min; ceiling 0.05 = 72 min (S5)
              // sustain in DAYS — the window; n_ops from 13.5 sets it
    monitor m_conf: confirm;                     // ^4 grade, logged per operation (Ch 22)
    on m_conf { alert "1-degree confirmation — stop operating and act"; }
    integrate rh1: ( confirm × cadence ) = charge;   // ^4 x ^7 = ^5, named emergent result

    // ---- STAGE 5: MANIFEST ----
    diode d3: Diode< ^E -> ^O > [Vf=2.0, I_R=0.02, V_BR=8.0];
    cjt   q3: CJT< cadence | receptivity => manifest > [beta=1.0, sat=1.0, region=active];
              // beta = receptivity (13.4); 1.0 = mass-market car
              // the bias is ^E and never ^O — see the Stage 5 walk

    // ---- LOOP A: rate limiter, stays inside ^O ----
    filter flt1: LowPass< in=manifest, out=regate, tau=1.0 >;   // tau in DAYS

    // ---- LOOP B: the lawful O -> P path (Ch 8.4) ----
    filter flt2: LowPass< in=manifest, out=trend, tau=21.0 >;   // three weeks, in DAYS
```

```cas
    node rehearsed: ^9_rehearsed^E_{F2}|f;     // same literal — a filter changes tau, not type
    node shared:    ^9_shared^E_{F4}|f;        // Below/Effect: the impression as it lands in others
    node bank:      ^5_collective^E_{F4}|f;    // Female: the parallel bank (Ch 7.5)
    node egregore:  ^5_egregore^E_{F4}|⟨A,f⟩;  // Female: the NAMED emergent result
    node cadence:   ^7_cadence^E_{F6}|E;       // Rhythm: the clock

    node guard:     ^3_guard^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩;   // Negative: three co-present locks
    node gain_meas: ^4_loopgain^E_{F2}|A;      // Vibration: the measured round trip, TP4

    // ---- STAGE 0: SEED AND DESCENT ----
    resistor r1: Resistor< path=fiction, R=20.0 >;    // low: nothing defends against a story
    diode    d1: Diode< ^C -> ^E > [Vf=1.2, I_R=0.02, V_BR=10.0];

    // ---- STAGE 1: THE SEED CJT ----
    cjt q1: CJT< seeded | belief => impress >
            [beta=0.90, sat=0.80, cutoff=0.05, g_m=0.60, r_pi=1.50, region=active];

    // ---- LOOP A: rehearsal.  Operator-side.  Sets LEVEL, not growth ----
    capacitor c1:   Capacitor< node=belief, C=1.20, leak_tau=90.0, V_BR=8.0 >;
    filter    flt1: LowPass< in=impress, out=rehearsed, tau=90.0 >;  // alpha = 0.0748
    feedback  rehearsed -> belief [beta=1.90];                       // S1 cap: 2.0

    // ---- STAGE 2: PROPAGATION ----
    osc  osc1: Oscillator< signal=impress, source=cadence,
                           period=7.0, duty=0.15, sustain=270.0 >;
    xfmr xf1:  Transformer< primary=impress, secondary=shared, n=3.0, k=0.50 >;
    capacitor c2: Capacitor< node=bank, C=0.08, n_parallel=140, r_iso=12.0,
                             leak_tau=540.0, V_BR=8.0 >;
    charge shared -> c2 [V=6.0];                     // metered upward path, Ch 7.5

    // ---- THE FUSION — the one licensed x on this board (14.2) ----
    integrate eg1: ( seeded × bank ) = egregore;

    // ---- STAGE 3: MANIFEST ----
    diode d2: Diode< ^E -> ^O > [Vf=2.0, I_R=0.02, V_BR=8.0];
    cjt   q2: CJT< cadence | egregore => conduct > [beta=1.00, sat=0.95, region=active];

    // ---- LOOP B: the lawful O -> E path.  Carries FACT, not fiction ----
    filter   flt2: LowPass< in=conduct, out=evidence, tau=90.0 >;
    feedback evidence -> belief [beta=0.30];         // top of the Part III band

    // ---- ANCHOR: outside both loops, zero leakage ----
    capacitor c3: Capacitor< node=record, C=1.00, leakage=0.0, V_BR=10.0 >;
    cjt       q3: CJT< egregore | record => audit > [beta=1.00, region=active];
    monitor   m_anchor: Monitor< node=audit, threshold=0.70 >;   // a FLOOR, not a ceiling
    on m_anchor { alert "anchor low — the claim is being treated as found, not made"; }

    // ---- GOVERNOR: reads the MEASUREMENT, never the setting ----
    constraint measured_loop_gain in [0.0, 2.0];                 // S1
    monitor    m_gain: Monitor< node=gain_meas, threshold=1.80 >; // S3
    on m_gain { alert "measured G at 1.80 — damp within one cycle"; }
    cjt q_kill: CJT< gain_meas | charter => cadence > [beta=0.0, region=cutoff];

    // ---- CSB (mandatory, Ch 24) ----
    cjt        q4: CJT< audit | charter => guard > [beta=2.0, sat=0.85, cutoff=0.30];
    fuse       f1: Fuse< guard, threshold=0.90, action=permanent_block >;
    constraint dial_spread in [0, 4];                            // Chapter 6.2

    // ---- TEST POINTS ----
    probe tp1: seeded;      // seed clarity entering the loop
    probe tp2: audit;       // can the construction still be recovered?
    probe tp3: bank;        // collective store charge
    probe tp4: gain_meas;   // MEASURED round-trip gain — seed-removal test
}
```

```cas
    // Q=8.0 gives bandwidth 0.044 — narrow. Narrowness IS the fingerprint.

    cap  bank: Capacitor< node=substrate, C=0.5, n_parallel=3,
```

```cas
board ccb_dp_deprogramming {

    output: composed;                  // the board's only output is internal

    node substrate: ^5^P_{F1}|T;       // Female: the subject's own formation
    node decompose: ^6^C_{F6}|A;       // Male: taking the pairing apart
    node confirm:   ^4^C_{F2}|A;       // Vibration: a return the subject can check
    node composed:  ^5^C_{F6}|A;       // Female: formation that has been checked
    node own_clock: ^7^O_{F6}|E;       // Rhythm: locally set cadence
    node limit:     ^3^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩; // Negative: inward refusal, three registers

    diode d_pc: Diode< ^P -> ^C > [Vf=0.7];
    diode d_ce: Diode< ^C -> ^E > [Vf=1.6];   // raised from 1.2
    diode d_eo: Diode< ^E -> ^O > [Vf=2.0];

    // ---- DP1: raise R_bias first. Everything else waits on this ----
    resistor r_restore: Resistor< path=substrate, R=11.0 >;   // back to baseline
    ramp restore: Ramp< target=rpi, from=1.60, to=10.80, dt=1320.0 >;  // 55 h on-path

             [beta=2.0, g_m=0.40, rpi=5.00, region=active];
    cjt dp2: CJT< decompose | substrate => confirm > [beta=1.0, g_m=0.40, rpi=2.50];

    // the one lawful integration on this board — named emergent result,
    // both operands in ^C, so nothing ascends
    integrate dp3: ( decompose × confirm ) = composed;

    // ---- DP4: take the oscillator back ----
    osc own: Oscillator< signal=own_clock, source=internal,
                         period=168.0, sustain=indefinite >;

    filter fb: LowPass< in=confirm, out=trend, tau=504.0 >;   // 3 weeks
    feedback trend -> substrate [beta=0.05];

    // ---- DP7: the subject's own CSB ----
    cjt  csb: CJT< material | substrate => limit > [beta=2.0, sat=0.85];
    fuse dp_fuse: Fuse< path=limit, threshold=0.90, action=permanent_block >;

    probe tp1: r_restore;   // rpi_terminal vs baseline
    probe tp2: own;         // cadence source and period
    probe tp3: dp1;         // decomposition gain — the stage, not the node
    probe tp4: limit;       // CSB status
}
```

```cas
    cjt resolve: CJT< gap      | segment => intent >   [beta=2.0, sat=0.85]; // detection-only
    cjt affirm:  CJT< surfaced | segment => pull >     [beta=2.0, sat=0.85];
    cjt want:    CJT< pull     | segment => intent >   [beta=1.2, sat=0.85];

    diode d3:         Diode< ^E -> ^O >               [Vf=2.0];
    resistor r_price: Resistor< path=intent, R=4.0 >;              // price + friction
    cjt close:        CJT< intent | segment => sale > [beta=1.0, cutoff=0.20];

    cjt  csb:      CJT< creative | segment => refusal > [beta=2.0, sat=0.85];
    fuse csb_fuse: Fuse< refusal, threshold=0.90, action=permanent_block >;

    probe tp1: c_seg;   probe tp2: cue;   probe tp3: intent;   probe tp4: sale;
}
```

```cas
board ccb_csb {                          // the operator's own safety board
    input:  proposal;                    // the operation being considered
    output: verdict;                     // PROCEED, or a cut path

    // ---- S0  CHARTER: the slow ^5. Bias source, never a fast-path output. ----

                             leak_tau=180.0, e_break=1.0 >;      // tau in days

    // ---- S1  INTAKE: the declared dial divider ----

    dial     dial_pos: ^2 [dial=5];
    dial     dial_neg: ^3 [dial=7];                   // divergence 2 — inside the limit
    resistor r1: Resistor< path=proposal, R=70.0 >;   // k = 5/12 = 0.417

    // ---- S2  PRE-AMP: surface every reading before anything judges one ----
    node expanded: ^8^C_{F2}|A;                       // Above/Cause: readings it triggers
    cjt  q1: CJT< proposal | charter => expanded > [β=3.0, sat=0.80, region=active];

    // ---- S3  DIFFERENTIAL PAIR: matched, shared bias ----

    node aversion:   ^3^P_{F7}|T;                     // Negative: repelled by running it
    cjt  q2: CJT< expanded | charter => attraction > [β=2.0, sat=0.90];
    cjt  q3: CJT< expanded | charter => aversion   > [β=2.0, sat=0.90];
    diff dif1: Differential< plus=aversion, minus=attraction >;   // risk

    // ---- S4  CASCADE: name them, then weigh them honestly ----
    node named:    ^1^C_{F2}|A;                       // Mind: risks named and sorted
    node assessed: ^6^E_{F6}|A;                       // Male: decomposed and weighed
    diode d1: Diode< ^P -> ^C > [Vf=0.7, I_R=0.02, V_BR=12.0];
    diode d2: Diode< ^C -> ^E > [Vf=1.2, I_R=0.02, V_BR=10.0];
    cjt   q5: CJT< risk  | charter => named    > [β=1.5, sat=0.80];
    cjt   q6: CJT< named | charter => assessed > [β=1.0, sat=0.80];   // unity — honesty

    // ---- S5  GUARD: Chapter 3.5's safety-guard datasheet row, instantiated ----
    node guard: ^3^P_{F7}|⟨A,f,T⟩;                    // three co-present guardrails
    cjt  q4: CJT< assessed | charter => guard >
             [β=3.0, g_m=0.3, rπ=10.0, sat=0.85, cutoff=0.08, region=active];

    // ---- S6  ENFORCEMENT: latch the path, not just the decision ----
    node blocked: ^9^P_{F7}|T;                        // Below/Effect: the block produced
    cjt  q7: CJT< guard | charter => blocked > [β=10.0, sat=0.98, cutoff=0.80];

    // ---- S7  EXIT: descent only ----

    diode d3: Diode< ^E -> ^O > [Vf=2.0, I_R=0.02, V_BR=8.0];

    // ---- S8  FEEDBACK AND INSTRUMENTS ----
    filter lp1: LowPass< in=ops_log, out=drift, tau=21.0 >;
    fuse   f2:  Fuse< charter, threshold=0.12, action=open_feedback >;
    feedback drift -> charter [β=0.05];

    node audit: ^6^C_{F6}|A;                          // Male: the weekly decomposition
    sample s1: Sample< node=audit, period=7.0, window=15.0 >;   // days, minutes
    monitor m1: Monitor< pair=[^2,^3], limit=4 >;
    monitor m2: Monitor< pair=[^5,^6], limit=4 >;
    monitor m3: Monitor< pair=[^8,^9], limit=4 >;
    on m1 { alert "involution divergence — attraction against aversion"; }
    on m2 { alert "involution divergence — composition against decomposition"; }
    on m3 { alert "involution divergence — trigger against effect"; }
```

# The TKS Crosswalk — 40 Elements, 7 Foundations, 12 Prerequisites
*A native-coordinate reference with every unresolved translation left visible*

This appendix is a map between related vocabularies, not a declaration that
they are identical. That distinction is load-bearing.

The repository contains strong evidence for the **Noetic-position** part of the
map: TKS positions 1 through 9 carry the same names as CAS `^1` through `^9`,
and TKS position 10 is Idea, written `^0` in CAS. It does **not** yet contain an
owner-ratified, tested decision about what the four TKS Worlds become on a CAS
literal. Two hypotheses remain live:

- World A/B/C/D may correspond to CAS Domains P/C/E/O.
- World A/B/C/D may correspond to CAS Registers T/A/f/E.

Domain and Register are separate CAS axes. A single World letter cannot be both
by silent substitution. The 40-Element tables therefore preserve native TKS
coordinates (`A1` through `D10`). Candidate CAS renderings are labeled
**PROPOSED / OPEN**. Nothing in this appendix fills the empty crosswalk binding
required by the research registry, ratifies an ontology, or upgrades an
empirical claim.

That is not a reason to avoid the table. It is a reason to use the table without
erasing its provenance.

---

## E.1 The three coordinate systems

| System | First axis | Second axis | Example | Status here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Native TKS Element | Noetic position 1–10 | World A–D | `B6` | preserved source coordinate |
| CAS state | Noetic `^0`–`^9` | Domain P/C/E/O | `^6^C` | canonical CAS |
| CAS state with Register | Noetic + Domain | orthogonal Register T/A/f/E | `^6^C\|A` | canonical CAS |

The native TKS Worlds are:

| World | Native description | Keep in records as |
|---|---|---|
| A | Spiritual | `tks_world=A` |
| B | Mental | `tks_world=B` |
| C | Emotional | `tks_world=C` |
| D | Physical | `tks_world=D` |

Do not turn `B6` directly into `^6^C`, `^6\|A`, or `^6^C\|A` unless the record
also names the versioned hypothesis that licensed that translation. `B6` is
complete and auditable as a native TKS coordinate. An unsupported conversion is
less informative, not more.

---

## E.2 The 40 Elements in native TKS coordinates

The short descriptions below reproduce the quick-reference semantics used by
the TKS manuscript. They are lookup handles, not full definitions.

| Position | Function | World A — Spiritual | World B — Mental | World C — Emotional | World D — Physical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mind | `A1` Divine / soul awareness | `B1` Ego, memory, logic | `C1` Emotional awareness | `D1` Body awareness |
| 2 | Positive | `A2` Soul evolution | `B2` Mental clarity | `C2` Joy, love | `D2` Health, order |
| 3 | Negative | `A3` Soul hindrance | `B3` Confusion, pessimism | `C3` Sadness, anger | `D3` Illness, chaos |
| 4 | Vibration | `A4` Aether / aura | `B4` Mental energy | `C4` Mood, atmosphere | `D4` Physical energy |
| 5 | Female | `A5` Soul yearning | `B5` Subconscious, creativity | `C5` Compassion, sensuality | `D5` Women, receptacles |
| 6 | Male | `A6` Spiritual discipline | `B6` Focus, structure | `C6` Courage, assertiveness | `D6` Men, penetrating |
| 7 | Rhythm | `A7` Life journey | `B7` Mental cycles | `C7` Emotional cycles | `D7` Physical rhythms |
| 8 | Above / Cause | `A8` Inner meaning | `B8` Mental triggers | `C8` Emotional triggers | `D8` Physical triggers |
| 9 | Below / Effect | `A9` Outer expression | `B9` Mental results | `C9` Emotional results | `D9` Physical results |
| 10 | Idea | `A10` Archetypes, purpose | `B10` Thoughts, concepts | `C10` Felt sense | `D10` Objects, matter |

### The evidenced Noetic-position map

| Native position | Native name | Proposed CAS Noetic | Evidence status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mind | `^1` | evidenced |
| 2 | Positive | `^2` | evidenced |
| 3 | Negative | `^3` | evidenced |
| 4 | Vibration | `^4` | evidenced |
| 5 | Female | `^5` | evidenced |
| 6 | Male | `^6` | evidenced |
| 7 | Rhythm | `^7` | evidenced |
| 8 | Above | `^8` Above/Cause | evidenced by name and prefix correspondence |
| 9 | Below | `^9` Below/Effect | evidenced by name and prefix correspondence |
| 10 | Idea | `^0` | evidenced; this is the one cyclic index change |

The one-based-to-zero-based symbol rule under proposal is therefore:

```text
A1…A9 stay A1…A9; A10 ↔ A0
B1…B9 stay B1…B9; B10 ↔ B0
C1…C9 stay C1…C9; C10 ↔ C0
D1…D9 stay D1…D9; D10 ↔ D0
```

That code map is not a blanket meaning claim. The proposal's row-level review
flags five positions where a compressed normalized definition does not cleanly
carry the CAS meaning:

| Normalized row | Review | Why it remains marked |
|---|---|---|
| `A0` | weak | “Divine Blueprint” is only a weak match for canonical `^0` Idea |
| `D5` | weak | the compressed row refers to a literal woman, not the compositional `^5` definition |
| `D6` | weak | the compressed row refers to a literal man, not the compositional `^6` definition |
| `D8` | divergent | the compressed row reads Above spatially as elevation; CAS `^8` is associative Cause |
| `D9` | divergent | the compressed row reads Below spatially as foundation; CAS `^9` is associative Effect |

Preserve `source_symbol`, `normalized_index`, and the definition version in any
dataset that uses these rows. A name match does not authorize overwriting a
meaning conflict.

---

## E.3 The World-axis decision is open

Here are the two live hypotheses side by side. They are alternatives, not two
columns to concatenate into a new identity.

| Native TKS World | Domain hypothesis `H_WD_v1` | Register hypothesis `H_WR_v1` |
|---|---|---|
| A Spiritual | P Principled | `\|T` Transcendent |
| B Mental | C Cognitive | `\|A` Analytical |
| C Emotional | E Evaluative | `\|f` Affective |
| D Physical | O Operational | `\|E` Embodied |

The ordering inside either hypothesis is well motivated: both descend from
high abstraction to concrete engagement. The choice **between** them is not
settled. Repository evidence points in both directions, and CAS explicitly
defines Domain and Register as orthogonal. For that reason:

1. Keep the native World field.
2. Name the hypothesis before translating.
3. Store the translated axis in its own field.
4. Never train, score, or publish a result that silently mixes the hypotheses.
5. Continue to stamp any dependent comparison
   `CONDITIONAL_ON_UNRATIFIED_CROSSWALK`.

The circuit equivalent is a keyed selector whose key is visible in the ledger.
It is not a wire soldered across both candidate outputs.

---

## E.4 Seven Foundations and their 28 native positions

The owner-supplied 28-Foundation source describes seven Foundation positions
across the same four native Worlds. The CAS teaching vocabulary has seven
Drives. A repository translation key aligns them by position, but the research
registry records that position mapping as outside the ratified claim-bearing
crosswalk. Read the CAS column below as a **positional teaching hypothesis**,
not a signed identity claim.

| Position | Native TKS Foundation description | Candidate CAS Drive name | Four native positions |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | desire to be and be with God | F1 Unity | `1a`, `1b`, `1c`, `1d` |
| 2 | wisdom, insight, and knowledge | F2 Wisdom | `2a`, `2b`, `2c`, `2d` |
| 3 | life, vitality, and health | F3 Vitality | `3a`, `3b`, `3c`, `3d` |
| 4 | companionship, love, and friendship | F4 Connection | `4a`, `4b`, `4c`, `4d` |
| 5 | worldly power, influence, and control | F5 Agency | `5a`, `5b`, `5c`, `5d` |
| 6 | material food and things | F6 Structure | `6a`, `6b`, `6c`, `6d` |
| 7 | lust, sex, and reproduction | F7 Purpose | `7a`, `7b`, `7c`, `7d` |

The native suffixes mean:

| Suffix | Native World | Typical expression in the owner-supplied elaboration |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | Spiritual | orienting meaning, metaphysical or devotional expression |
| `b` | Mental | concepts, models, reasoning, planning |
| `c` | Emotional | feeling-tone, valuation, emotional relation |
| `d` | Physical | bodily, material, sensorimotor expression |

If the Register hypothesis were ratified for a particular use, the candidate
renderings would be:

| Foundation | Spiritual `a` | Mental `b` | Emotional `c` | Physical `d` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `F1\|T` | `F1\|A` | `F1\|f` | `F1\|E` |
| 2 | `F2\|T` | `F2\|A` | `F2\|f` | `F2\|E` |
| 3 | `F3\|T` | `F3\|A` | `F3\|f` | `F3\|E` |
| 4 | `F4\|T` | `F4\|A` | `F4\|f` | `F4\|E` |
| 5 | `F5\|T` | `F5\|A` | `F5\|f` | `F5\|E` |
| 6 | `F6\|T` | `F6\|A` | `F6\|f` | `F6\|E` |
| 7 | `F7\|T` | `F7\|A` | `F7\|f` | `F7\|E` |

Until ratification, write the native coordinate alongside any candidate:

```text
source_position = 4c
source_world = C / Emotional
candidate = F4|f
crosswalk = H_WR_v1 / PROPOSED_UNRATIFIED
```

This makes a later correction mechanical. Without those four fields, a later
correction becomes archaeology.

---

## E.5 The 12 canonical Prerequisites

The Prerequisites are three four-stage cycles used by the Recursive
Prerequisite Model. The card and zodiac symbols are identifiers in this system;
they do not import conventional divinatory or astrological meanings.

### Desire cycle — Kings

| ID | Card | Stage | Diagnostic reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | King of Clubs | Beginning Desire | the want is just dawning |
| P2 | King of Hearts | Strong Desire | the will is fully engaged |
| P3 | King of Spades | Weakening Desire | motivation is fading |
| P4 | King of Diamonds | Absent Desire | the will is gone |

### Power cycle — Queens

| ID | Card | Stage | Diagnostic reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| P5 | Queen of Diamonds | Birth of Power | ability is just emerging |
| P6 | Queen of Clubs | Adolescent Power | ability is progressing but not yet effective |
| P7 | Queen of Hearts | Mature Power | ability is fully effective for the task |
| P8 | Queen of Spades | Waning Power | capability is diminishing |

### Wisdom cycle — Jacks

| ID | Card | Stage | Diagnostic reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| P9 | Jack of Clubs | Learning Wisdom | knowledge is being acquired |
| P10 | Jack of Diamonds | Knowing Wisdom | knowledge is present; application may lag |
| P11 | Jack of Spades | Understanding Wisdom | a working grasp of the pathway |
| P12 | Jack of Hearts | Mastering Wisdom | comprehension and application are integrated |

These are states to diagnose, not a sequence to force every goal through. An
operator begins with the actual Prime Desire, checks the required Desire,
Wisdom, and Power conditions, and recurses on the first unmet acquisition.
“Absent Desire” is information. It is not an invitation to manufacture desire
through pressure, nor does an unmet condition authorize acting on somebody
else.

# St. John's Equation Worksheet
*A printable bench sheet for one operation, one admissible confirmation, and one decision*

This form implements Chapters 5 and 23. It is an instrument sheet, not a
prediction certificate. The quantities below compare operations made under the
same declared conventions. They do not establish that a confirmation was
caused by an operation, that a target will arrive on a schedule, or that the
scale factor `τ = 1/3` is a physical constant.

Print one copy per operation. Write the timing convention and horizon before
the operation begins. Do not erase a `NO-READ`; it is a result.

---

## F.1 Page-One Conventions

Complete this page once for a campaign. Copy its revision identifier onto every
operation sheet.

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Campaign / board | ______________________________________________ |
| Target stated in one sentence | ______________________________________________ |
| Target state literal | ______________________________________________ |
| Timing-convention revision | __________ |
| `t_op` begins at | ☐ procedure begins  ☐ gnosis / working state establishes |
| `t_op` ends at | ______________________________________________ |
| `t_conf` begins at | **the end of the operation** |
| Clock grid | **5 minutes** |
| Confirmation rule | **first admissible confirmation only** |
| Rolling median `t_conf` from last 10 comparable operations | __________ min |
| Computed horizon `3 × median` | __________ min |
| Declared horizon `t_H = max(1,440 min, 3 × median)` | __________ min |
| Minimum separation before another operation on this target | __________ |
| One-week control-count dates | __________ through __________ |
| Unprompted matching events during control week | __________ |
| Operator signature / date | ______________________________________________ |

**Boundary rule.** An event at or beyond `t_H` is `NO-READ`, not a slow
confirmation. A later, stronger event remains descriptive evidence and never
replaces the first admissible event in the ratio.

## F.5 Arithmetic

Use the quantized readings.

```text
t_op                         = __________ min
t_conf                       = __________ min

η = t_op / t_conf            = __________
τ                             = 1/3
result = η × τ               = __________
reduced result = a/b         = __________ / __________
A = 1/result
  = b/a
  = 3/η
  = 3 × t_conf / t_op        = __________

previous comparable A        = __________
ρ = A_current / A_previous   = __________
```

**Pair-admissibility check:** if `a > 3` after quantization, record `(a, b)` as
an arithmetic artifact and make no decision from `a` or `b`. Decide from `A`.

**Do not write `β = A`.** `A` is a ratio on delivered current. It can be paid
by target clarity, divider transmission, residual resistance, amplifier gain
within its legal range, or changes to `R_op`. A non-finite `A` is not a very
large amplifier setting; it is `NO-READ`.

---

## F.6 Band Decision

| `A` | Equivalent `η` | Instrument reading | Required action |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| `A ≤ 1` | `η ≥ 3` | sufficient | **ACT** — stop calibrating and take the practical action |
| `1 < A < 3` | `1 < η < 3` | close | **CLOSE** — finish resistance work; leave the amplifier alone |
| `3 ≤ A < 9` | `1/3 < η ≤ 1` | under-driven | **DRIVE** — change one lever, then re-read |
| `A ≥ 9` | `η ≤ 1/3` | weak coupling | **RE-SPEC** — decompose or reroute before another operation |

Selected band: ☐ ACT  ☐ CLOSE  ☐ DRIVE  ☐ RE-SPEC

Single next action authorised by this row:

____________________________________________________________________________

Single parameter or condition allowed to change before the next comparable
operation:

____________________________________________________________________________

Everything deliberately held constant:

____________________________________________________________________________

# Appendix G — The Quantitative Table Template

Three blank forms, meant to be photocopied. Punch the left margin and file by
operation number rather than by date — one operation can run four months, and its
sheets belong together.

An operation you did not log did not produce data. It produced an impression, and
an impression is not something you can read three weeks later and disagree with.

---

### G.1 Which form, when

| Form | Opened | Written in | Answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 — Operation Log** | Before the first session; one sheet per operation | Once at setup, then one row per session | What did I build, and what did it read? |
| **2 — Confirmation Log** | With Form 1 | One block per confirmation | How far did the signal actually get? |
| **3 — Parameter-Change Log** | With Form 1 | One block per change; verdict later | Which change caused which result? |

Form 3 governs the other two. Any reading taken after an unlogged change is
uninterpretable, and the honest thing to do with an uninterpretable reading is
strike it.

---

### G.2 Page geometry

- 58 monospace columns — about 9 pt in a 6×9 text block. Nothing here is wider,
  so nothing reflows on a photocopier set to 100 percent.
- Form 1 is one page per operation. Forms 2 and 3 repeat their block; run them
  onto as many sheets as the operation needs.
- Ink, not pencil. Corrections are struck through and initialled, never erased.
  The crossed-out number is often the interesting one.

---

### G.3 Form 1 — Operation Log

